## Sources

- [Dive into Systems — Ch 13.3 Virtual Memory](sources/dis-13-3-virtual-memory.md) — **Third leaf** of Ch 13 *The Operating System* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — supplies the **address-translation mechanism** under [[dis-2-1-scope-memory|Ch 2.1]]'s four-region [[ProcessMemory|program memory]] cartoon: every process sees its own private [[VirtualAddress|virtual address space]], the OS maps [[VirtualMemory|virtual]] to [[PhysicalAddress|physical]] addresses through a per-process [[PageTable|page table]], and the [[TLB|translation lookaside buffer]] caches recent translations to avoid two memory accesses per load. Fixed-size [[Page|pages]] (typically 4 KiB) replace contiguous-allocation; [[Paging]] decouples virtual contiguity from physical layout. **[[PageFault|Page fault]]** = the page-table entry says *"not resident"* — the OS reads the page from the [[SwapFile|swap file]] on disk (millions of cycles), evicts another page if needed, retries the access. **[[DemandPaging|Demand paging]]** loads pages on first reference rather than at process start — a process's virtual address space can exceed physical RAM. **120th ingested DIS chapter.** Mints **10 new concept pages** ([[VirtualMemory]], [[VirtualAddress]], [[PhysicalAddress]], [[PageTable]], [[Page]], [[Paging]], [[PageFault]], [[TLB]] promoted from forward-ref, [[SwapFile]], [[DemandPaging]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 13.2 Processes](sources/dis-13-2-processes.md) — **Second leaf** of Ch 13 *The Operating System* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — turns the [[Process]] noun named in [[dis-13-1-booting-running|13.1]] into a full state machine + OS data structure + POSIX [[SystemCall|syscall]] API. **Four [[ProcessState|process states]]** (Ready / Running / Blocked / Exited); the **[[ProcessControlBlock|process control block]]** (PID + address space + register snapshot + open files + state); the **mechanism / policy split** ([[ContextSwitch|context switch]] = *how*, [[Scheduler|scheduling]] = *which*). [[Multiprogramming|Multiprogramming]] (switch on I/O block) + [[Timesharing]] (quantum-bounded preemption) keep the CPU busy. POSIX surface: [[Fork|`fork()`]] (returns twice — `0` to child, child [[ProcessID|PID]] to parent), [[Exec|`execvp`]] (overlays image, never returns on success), [[Wait|`wait` / `waitpid`]] (reaps [[Zombie|zombies]], unblocks parent on [[Signal|`SIGCHLD`]]). [[Init|`init` (PID 1)]] is the root of the process hierarchy. Closes with the [[WallTime|wall time]] vs [[CPUTime|CPU time]] distinction. **119th ingested DIS chapter.** Mints **11 new concept pages** ([[ProcessState]], [[ProcessControlBlock]], [[Exec]], [[Wait]], [[Scheduler]], [[ProcessScheduling]], [[Multiprogramming]], [[Zombie]], [[Init]], [[WallTime]], [[CPUTime]]) and extends [[Process]] / [[Fork]] in place.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 13.1 Booting and Running the OS](sources/dis-13-1-booting-running.md) — **Opening leaf** of Ch 13 *The Operating System* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — pivots from Part IV performance-tuning into the **OS-implementation arc**. Codifies how the OS itself gets started ([[Booting]] via [[Firmware|firmware]] like [[BIOS]] / [[UEFI]] that loads the [[Bootloader|boot block]] from disk), how it launches user programs (allocate RAM → load binary → create [[Process|process]] state → initialize [[CPU]]), and the **interrupt-driven architecture** that lets the [[Kernel|kernel]] sleep until a hardware device or user program needs service. Codifies the **dual-mode CPU** ([[KernelMode]] vs [[UserMode]]) and the **[[SystemCall|system-call]] trap** as the controlled gateway between them — *"When an application wants to invoke a system call, it places the desired call's number in a known location and issues a trap instruction to interrupt the OS"*. **Two interrupt sources**: hardware ([[Interrupt|interrupt]] bus, devices) and software (traps from user-mode trap instructions). Kernel-in-every-address-space optimization makes [[ContextSwitch|context switching]] cheap — Meltdown vulnerability later forced stricter kernel-user separation. **118th ingested DIS chapter — opens Ch 13.** Mints **5 new concept pages** ([[Bootloader]], [[Kernel]], [[KernelMode]], [[UserMode]], [[SystemCall]]) and **extends [[Interrupt]] / [[ContextSwitch]] in place** with the OS-level treatment.

Two transports — stdio (`stdio_client` + `StdioServerParameters` for local processes) and streamable HTTP (`streamablehttp_client` for remote servers) — same `ClientSession` API once open. Bumped to 319 with [[dis-7-11-x86-64-exercises]] (Dive into Systems Ch 7.11 — **exercises section closing Ch 7 *64-bit x86 Assembly*** — single-page redirect to the book's interactive exercises platform, no inline problems; drills the full Ch 7.1–Ch 7.10 [[X86_64|x86-64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] surface (registers / [[X86AddressingMode|addressing modes]] / [[X86MovInstruction|`mov`]] / arithmetic / [[AsmIfThenElse|if-else]] / [[AsmLoopPattern|loop]] / [[CallingConvention|function-call]] / [[Recursion|recursion]] / [[AsmArrayAccess|array]] / matrix / [[StructLayout|struct]] / [[StackSmashing|buffer-overflow]]); **76th ingested DIS chapter — fully completes Ch 7**; structural sibling of [[dis-1-8-exercises|Ch 1.8]] / [[dis-2-11-exercises|Ch 2.11]] / [[dis-4-10-exercises|Ch 4.10]] / [[dis-5-11-exercises|Ch 5.11]]; no new concept pages — pure problem-set close). Bumped to 318 with [[dspy-data]] (DSPy Learn page 10 of 13 — **second page of the Evaluation stage**; expands Step 1 of the four-step iterative-evaluation loop into the concrete data primitive [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] (a typed Python dict-with-utilities — arbitrary field names, dot-notation access, `with_inputs(...)` input/label tagging, non-mutating `inputs()` / `labels()` partition accessors) and the dataset shape (plain `list[dspy.Example]` — no `Dataset` class; train/dev/test splits are Python slicing); commits the framework to three load-bearing positions — *DSPy is a machine learning framework, so working in it involves training sets, development sets, and test sets* (locates DSPy inside the supervised-ML tradition), *datasets are plain Python lists* (no `Dataset` class — small-API discipline consistent with [[dspy-modules|*"DSPy is just Python code"*]]), *inputs-only sufficiency* (*"You can use DSPy effectively without any intermediate or final labels, but you will need at least a few example inputs"* — the data-side mirror of [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview's]] *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* commitment); establishes [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] as a **subclass of `dspy.Example`** (*"Your DSPy modules will return values of the type `Prediction`, which is a special sub-class of `Example`"*) which makes the [[DSPyMetrics|metric]]'s `(example, prediction) -> score` contract type-symmetric — both arguments share dot-access / `inputs()` / `labels()` surface; mints 2 concept pages — [[DSPyExample]] (the data primitive) and [[DSPyData]] (the dataset / split convention); **resolves both long-standing forward references** ([[DSPyData]] + [[DSPyExample]]) carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] since the Evaluation stage opened on page 9). Bumped to 320 with [[dspy-metrics]] (DSPy Learn page 11 of 13 — **third page of the Evaluation stage**; expands Step 2 of the four-step iterative-evaluation loop into the **`(example, pred, trace=None) -> score`** function-signature contract — *"A DSPy metric is just a function in Python that takes `example` (e.g., from your training or dev set) and the output `pred` from your DSPy program, and outputs a `float` (or `int` or `bool`) score"*; documents the **dual-purpose `trace` argument** — continuous `float` return when `trace is None` for evaluation/optimization, strict `bool` return when `trace is not None` for bootstrap demo selection — the structural reason a single function serves both DSPy compilation phases; the two regimes (simple scalar like `example.answer.lower() == pred.answer.lower()` + built-ins `dspy.evaluate.metrics.answer_exact_match` / `answer_passage_match`, vs AI-feedback via a `class Assess(dspy.Signature)` rubric + N `dspy.Predict(Assess)` invocations summed and thresholded — DSPy's structural operationalization of [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]]); the worked tweet metric showing **hybrid AI-feedback + deterministic hard gate** (`len(tweet) <= 280` mixed with two `Predict(Assess)` outputs) — the wiki's first demonstration that DSPy metrics are not all-or-nothing AI-feedback; the `validate_hops` trace-aware bootstrap recipe — the only intermediate-step validator in the *Learn* corpus so far; operationalizes the **recursive-metric-optimization** claim (Step 4 of the four-step loop) — the AI-feedback metric is itself a DSPy program and thus optimizable by an Optimizer; documents **`dspy.Evaluate`** as the parallel dev-set-evaluation harness with the `devset` / `num_threads` / `display_progress` / `display_table` kwargs; mints 2 concept pages — [[DSPyMetrics]] (the canonical metric contract — **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] / [[dspy-data]] / [[DSPyExample]] / [[DSPyPrediction]] / every prior DSPy ingest since the corpus opened) and [[DSPyEvaluate]] (the dev-set-evaluation utility — a thread-parallel wrapper around `for x in devset: pred = program(**x.inputs()); score = metric(x, pred)` with progress + tabular display)). Bumped to 334 with [[dspy-optimizers]] (DSPy Learn **page 13 of 13 — closes the DSPy *Learn* corpus** at 13/13; ships the **catalog** of specific optimizers (`LabeledFewShot` / `BootstrapFewShot` / `BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch` / `KNNFewShot` / `COPRO` / `MIPROv2` / `SIMBA` / `GEPA` / `BootstrapFinetune` / `Ensemble` / `BetterTogether`) deferred from [[dspy-optimization-overview|page 12]]; resolves every long-standing forward reference the prior twelve pages carried — [[DSPyOptimizers]], [[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], [[MIPROv2]], [[BootstrapFinetune]], [[GEPA]]; mints 6 concept pages — [[DSPyOptimizers]] (catalog sibling of [[DSPyOptimization]] — workflow vs catalog, mirroring [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]]), [[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], [[MIPROv2]], [[GEPA]], [[BootstrapFinetune]]; names the historical rename — *"Formerly called teleprompters"*; records the **composability** claim (`MIPROv2 → MIPROv2` or `MIPROv2 → BootstrapFinetune`, the **structural essence** of `BetterTogether`); names cost ballpark ($2 typical, cents-to-tens-of-dollars range); three worked receipts — **MIPROv2 + ReAct on HotPotQA: 24%→51%**; **MIPROv2 + RAG with [[llmasjudge|`SemanticF1`]] on StackExchange: 53%→61%**; **BootstrapFinetune + Banking77 on `gpt-4o-mini-2024-07-18`: 66%→87%** (only weight-tuning receipt; **only `set_lm(...)` exercise** in the corpus); the five-rule getting-started rubric (10→`BootstrapFewShot`, 50+→`BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch`, 200+→`MIPROv2`, 0-shot→`MIPROv2(0-shot)`, post-success→`BootstrapFinetune`); `MIPROv2`'s three-stage decomposition (bootstrapping → grounded proposal → discrete search via [[BayesianOptimization|Bayesian Optimization]]) as the **structural template** for non-trivial optimizers; plain-text-JSON `save()`/`load()` inspectability commitment). Bumped to 325 with [[dspy-optimization-overview]] (DSPy Learn page 12 of 13 — **opens the Optimization stage** of the three-stage Programming → Evaluation → Optimization model; defines an optimizer's three-input contract — *program* + *metric* + *training set* — and its one output (an optimized program with refined instructions / demonstrations / weights); commits the framework to four load-bearing positions — *the optimizer's job is to tune prompts or weights against a metric*, *training-set size scales from 30 to 300+* (*"You can often get substantial value out of 30 examples, but aim for at least 300 examples"*), *the conventional ML train/val split is inverted to 20/80 for most prompt optimizers* (because prompt optimizers overfit on small training sets) with **[[GEPA]] as the named carve-out** (the only specific optimizer mentioned on this page, and only to disclose that it follows standard ML practice instead), *iterative development spans four axes — data / program structure / metric / optimizer-choice* (three of the four point back into prior stages, making Optimization an open-under-revision stage rather than a black-box terminus); mints [[DSPyOptimization]] as the canonical concept page for the optimization **workflow** (the *fourth artifact* of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] — completes the four-artifact picture Signatures / Modules / Adapters / Optimizers at the workflow level); deliberately defers the **catalog** of specific optimizers ([[BootstrapFewShot]], [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]], [[MIPROv2]], [[BootstrapFinetune]], [[GEPA]]) to page 13 ([[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizers]]) — the split mirrors the [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]] precedent (one page anchors the workflow, the sibling anchors the per-algorithm machinery); single sibling ingest remains to close the *Learn* corpus at 13/13). -->


- [Dive into Systems — Ch 12.4 Summary](sources/dis-12-4-summary.md) — **Fourth and final leaf** of Ch 12 *Code Optimization* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — single-page summary **closing Ch 12** and the [[DiveIntoSystems]] Part IV performance-tuning arc. Six structural commitments recapped: (1) algorithm/data-structure choice as the highest-leverage optimization (e.g., **Sieve of Eratosthenes** = **12× speedup** over a naive custom prime generator); (2) prefer well-tested standard library functions like `sqrt` — compilers recognize and optimize them; (3) **profile-driven optimization** — *"optimization should never be based on gut feelings"*; (4) split complex operations into multiple small functions for both readability and compiler [[FunctionInlining|inlining]] eligibility; (5) memory access patterns / [[LocalityOfReference|cache locality]] often beat instruction-count optimization for cache-bound work; (6) modern compilers (SSA, polyhedral models) continue improving — diminishing returns for manual transformations. **117th ingested DIS chapter — closes Ch 12** and **completes Ch 12**. **No new concept pages** — pure recap.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 12.3 Memory Considerations](sources/dis-12-3-memory-considerations.md) — **Third leaf** of Ch 12 *Code Optimization* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — pivots from compiler-side optimizations ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations|Ch 12.2]]) to the **memory-locality lens** the [[CCompiler|compiler]] usually **cannot** optimize for the programmer. Three transformations dominate: **loop interchange** (reorder nested loops so the innermost stride matches [[CacheLine|cache-line]] layout — *"data is loaded into cache in blocks not elements"*), **loop fission** (split one loop into multiple loops over the same range — improves per-loop working-set locality and enables multicore distribution), and **loop fusion** (combine loops over the same range — inverse of fission, reduces loop overhead, improves [[TemporalLocality|temporal locality]] when bodies touch the same data). **Headline empirical result**: a 10,000 × 10,000 matrix-vector multiply collapses from **2.01 s → 0.27 s** (~**8× speedup**) after reordering nested loops to traverse [[RowMajorOrder|row-major]] — zero algorithmic-complexity change. Introduces **[[Massif]]** — the [[Valgrind]] heap-profiling tool — completing the [[Valgrind]] optimization triad ([[Callgrind]] from [[dis-12-1-first-steps|Ch 12.1]] + [[Cachegrind]] from [[dis-11-5-cachegrind|Ch 11.5]] + [[Massif]] here). Massif example: matrix-vector program — **800 MB total allocation, 99.96% in a single allocation function**. **116th ingested DIS chapter — third leaf of Ch 12.** Mints **1 new concept page** ([[Massif]]); reuses [[LocalityOfReference]] / [[SpatialLocality]] / [[CacheLine]] / [[RowMajorOrder]] / [[Valgrind]] from earlier ingests.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 12.2 Other Compiler Optimizations: Loop Unrolling and Function Inlining](sources/dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations.md) — **Second leaf** of Ch 12 *Code Optimization* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — surveys two classical optimizations that **modern [[GCC|GCC]] performs automatically** and that programmers **should generally leave to the compiler**: **[[FunctionInlining|function inlining]]** (replaces a function call with the callee body, enabling downstream [[ConstantFolding|constant folding]] / constant propagation / [[DeadCodeElimination|dead-code elimination]] — *"makes it easier for the compiler to identify other potential improvements"*) and **[[LoopUnrolling|loop unrolling]]** (reduces iteration count by factor `n` while increasing per-iteration work by `n`, eliminating branch overhead). GCC controls: **`-finline-functions`** (auto-on at **[[GccOptLevels|`-O3`]]**), **`static inline`** keyword hint, **`-funroll-loops`** (compile-time-known trip counts), **`-funroll-all-loops`** (aggressive, including variable trip counts). **Empirical result on 5,000,000-prime `isPrime` benchmark**: manual unrolling yielded only **marginal** improvements; GCC flags produced **comparable** speedups **without sacrificing readability**. Headline recommendation: *"code today is more often read than it is written... a programmer should let the compiler optimize whenever possible."* **115th ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of Ch 12.** Mints **4 new concept pages** ([[FunctionInlining]], [[ConstantFolding]], [[DeadCodeElimination]], [[GccOptLevels]]) and **extends [[LoopUnrolling]] in place** with the DIS GCC-flag treatment.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 12.1 Code Optimization First Steps](sources/dis-12-1-first-steps.md) — **First leaf** of Ch 12 *Code Optimization* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **opens Ch 12** by framing optimization as a **measurement discipline**, not an intuition exercise. Anchored on Knuth's canonical warning: *"premature optimization is the root of all evil (or at least most of it)"*. Teaches the **profile-then-optimize** loop: identify [[HotSpot|hot spots]] via [[Callgrind]] (a [[Valgrind]] tool that counts per-function instruction executions), then apply a targeted transformation. Worked **`isPrime`** example: **loop-invariant code motion** lifts `sqrt(x)+1` out of the loop condition — `sqrt` invocations drop from **2,700,000 (20.5% of total instructions) → 100,001 (96% reduction)**, yielding **47% runtime improvement** on the 5,000,000-prime benchmark **before** any [[GCC|compiler]] optimizations. Introduces **loop execution accounting** (initializer 1×, boolean `k+1×`, body + step `k×` for `k` iterations) and the **compiler limitation** that prevents [[GCC|GCC]] from making this optimization automatically — opaque function calls like `sqrt` may have side effects the compiler cannot rule out. **114th ingested DIS chapter — opens Ch 12.** Mints **4 new concept pages** ([[Profiling]], [[Benchmarking]], [[HotSpot]], [[Callgrind]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.8 Exercises](sources/dis-11-8-exercises.md) — **Eighth and final leaf** of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **exercise-set close** that **fully completes Ch 11** — every chapter of Part IV's memory-hierarchy arc is now in the wiki. Single-page redirect into the book's external interactive exercises platform; drills the full Ch 11.1–11.6 surface: six-tier pyramid, storage-device tradeoffs, [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] axes, [[CacheMemory|cache]] placement / replacement / write policy, [[Cachegrind|empirical profiling]], and multicore [[CacheCoherency|coherency]]. **Structural twin** of [[dis-1-8-exercises|Ch 1.8]] / [[dis-2-11-exercises|Ch 2.11]] / [[dis-4-10-exercises|Ch 4.10]] / [[dis-5-11-exercises|Ch 5.11]] / [[dis-7-11-x86-64-exercises|Ch 7.11]] / [[dis-8-11-ia32-exercises|Ch 8.11]] / [[dis-9-11-arm64-exercises|Ch 9.11]] — *exercise-set closes chapter* pattern. **113th ingested DIS chapter — closes Ch 11.** **No new concept pages.**
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.7 Summary](sources/dis-11-7-summary.md) — **Seventh leaf** of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — single-page chapter summary that distills the Ch 11.1–11.6 arc into seven structural commitments: the storage-device performance/capacity/cost/volatility trade-off, hierarchical organization (fast/small primary → slow/dense secondary), the data-management strategy (*"data that's being actively used in faster storage devices"*), the two-axis [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] taxonomy ([[TemporalLocality|temporal]] + [[SpatialLocality|spatial]]), the [[CacheMemory|CPU cache]] mechanism as locality's hardware exploit, the **tag/index/offset address decoding** decomposition, and [[Cachegrind]] empirical performance profiling. CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 licensed. **112th ingested DIS chapter — seventh leaf of Ch 11.** **No new concept pages** — pure recap.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.6 Looking Ahead: Caching on Multicore Processors](sources/dis-11-6-cache-coherency.md) — **Sixth leaf** of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — extends the [[dis-11-1-memory-hierarchy|Ch 11.1]]–[[dis-11-5-cachegrind|Ch 11.5]] uniprocessor cache story to **[[Multicore|multicore]]** systems with private L1 + shared L2/L3. Names the [[CacheCoherency|**cache-coherence problem**]] verbatim: *"the value of a copy of a block of memory stored in one core's L1 cache is different than the value of a copy of the same block stored in another core's L1 cache"*. Introduces the **MSI** (Modified / Shared / Invalid) invalidate protocol as the pedagogical baseline — the simpler cousin of the production-grade [[MESI]] protocol covered by [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism|ParProc Ch 3]]. **Two implementation strategies**: **snooping** (every cache controller monitors a shared bus for transactions to addresses it caches — supports write-invalidate; simple but doesn't scale) vs **directory-based** (a directory tracks which caches hold each block; coherence messages target only those caches — scales better, more metadata + latency). **[[FalseSharing|False sharing]]** named as the multithreaded-program pathology coherency creates, with details deferred to Ch 14.5. **Justification**: per-core L1 hit-rates beat a single shared L1 — coherency is the price of independent instruction streams + shared memory. **111th ingested DIS chapter — sixth leaf of Ch 11.** **Extends [[CacheCoherency]] in place** with the DIS multicore framing (MSI baseline + snooping/directory + private/shared cache topology); [[MESI]] / [[FalseSharing]] / [[Multicore]] reused.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.5 Cache Analysis and Cachegrind](sources/dis-11-5-cachegrind.md) — **Fifth leaf of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — closes the theory→mechanism→measurement chain by introducing **[[Cachegrind]]**, the [[Valgrind]] suite's [[CacheMemory|cache]]-simulation tool. Where [[dis-11-3-locality|Ch 11.3]] argued *why* [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] matters and [[dis-11-4-caching|Ch 11.4]] explained *how* hardware exploits it, **Ch 11.5 makes it measurable** — `valgrind --tool=cachegrind --cache-sim=yes ./prog` produces deterministic L1 + LL [[CacheHit|hit]] / [[CacheMiss|miss]] counts, decoded per source line via `cg_annotate`. **Headline result**: the same matrix-sum algorithm in [[RowMajorOrder|row-major]] vs column-major form yields **62,688 vs 1,062,996 D1 misses** — a **~17× miss-count delta** producing **4.61× runtime delta** at zero algorithmic-complexity change. Sharpens [[dis-11-3-locality|Ch 11.3]]'s *~5×* row-vs-column claim into a precise [[Cachegrind]]-instrumented benchmark. **Counters**: Ir / Dr / Dw / D1mr / D1mw / DLmr / DLmw / ILmr; L1 + LL only (L2 abstracted away). **110th ingested DIS chapter — fifth leaf of Ch 11.** **Promotes [[Cachegrind]] from forward-reference to full concept page** (the only new concept this ingest).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.4 Caching](sources/dis-11-4-caching.md) — **Fourth leaf of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — operationalizes [[dis-11-3-locality|Ch 11.3]]'s [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] property into the concrete **CPU [[CacheMemory|cache]]** mechanism. Answers the three structural cache-design questions: *which* subset of memory to hold ([[CacheLine|cache lines]] of 16–64 bytes), *when* to transfer ([[WriteBackCache|write-back]] vs [[WriteThroughCache|write-through]]), and *how* to determine presence (tag/index/offset address decomposition). Introduces the **three placement architectures** — [[DirectMappedCache|direct-mapped]] (simplest, highest conflict-miss rate), [[SetAssociativeCache|set associative]] (the modern dominant compromise, typically 2–8 way), and [[FullyAssociativeCache|fully associative]] (impractical at general scale; survives in [[TLB|TLBs]]) — with a worked example showing **2 conflict misses on direct-mapped vs 0 on two-way set associative**. **[[LeastRecentlyUsed|LRU]]** named as standard [[CacheReplacementPolicy|replacement policy]] ("recently used data is likely to be used again"). **3C miss taxonomy**: compulsory / capacity / conflict. Write-policy split: [[WriteThroughCache|write-through]] (simple, no dirty bit) vs [[WriteBackCache|write-back]] (modern dominant — "amortizing the cost of a memory access across many writes significantly improves performance"). **109th ingested DIS chapter — fourth leaf of Ch 11.** Mints **10 new concept pages** ([[CacheLine]], [[CacheHit]], [[CacheMiss]], [[CacheReplacementPolicy]], [[LeastRecentlyUsed]], [[DirectMappedCache]], [[SetAssociativeCache]], [[FullyAssociativeCache]], [[WriteBackCache]], [[WriteThroughCache]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.3 Locality](sources/dis-11-3-locality.md) — **Third leaf of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — pivots from [[dis-11-2-storage-devices|Ch 11.2]]'s storage-device taxonomy into the **empirical program-behavior property** that makes the [[MemoryHierarchy|memory hierarchy]] workable. Codifies the **two-axis [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] taxonomy** — *"the two basic forms of locality are temporal locality and spatial locality"* — and frames locality as the system-designer's exploit (move frequently-accessed data to fast storage) that produces *"the illusion of having massive fast memory"*. Worked **`sum_array` example** shows both axes simultaneously (loop variables → [[TemporalLocality|temporal]]; consecutive array elements → [[SpatialLocality|spatial]] via the [[CacheLine|cache line]]). **Headline payoff**: row-major `mat[i][j]` vs column-major `mat[j][i]` matrix sum executes **~5× apart** at zero algorithmic change — the row-major form aligns with C's [[RowMajorOrder|row-major]] layout. **Desk / bookshelf / library analogy** supplies the [[WorkingSet|working-set]] intuition. **108th ingested DIS chapter — third leaf of Ch 11.** Mints **3 new concept pages** ([[TemporalLocality]], [[SpatialLocality]], [[WorkingSet]]) and expands [[LocalityOfReference]] in place.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.2 Storage Devices](sources/dis-11-2-storage-devices.md) — **Second leaf of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — populates [[dis-11-1-memory-hierarchy|Ch 11.1]]'s six-tier pyramid with concrete device technologies and the canonical **latency / capacity / cost / volatility** table. Splits storage into **primary** (volatile — [[CpuRegister|registers]] <1 ns, [[SRAM]] cache ~5 ns, [[DRAM]] main memory ~100 ns) and **secondary** ([[NonVolatileMemory|non-volatile]] — [[SolidStateDrive|SSD]] 0.1–1 ms, [[HardDisk|HDD]] 5–10 ms, magnetic tape, optical, network-remote). Introduces the **[[SRAM]] vs [[DRAM]] technology split** for RAM (six-transistor latches vs 1T1C capacitors) and the **mechanical anatomy of HDDs** (rotating platters at 5,000–15,000 RPM, tracks, sectors, seek + rotational latency). [[SolidStateDrive|SSDs]] introduced by their headline property only — *"no moving parts (and thus lower latency)"* — flash-internal mechanics (pages / blocks / wear leveling) deferred. **Grace Hopper nanoseconds** named as the pedagogical motif for why *distance ⇒ latency*; **von Neumann bottleneck** identified as the [[MemoryBus|memory-bus]] latency wall that the [[CacheMemory|cache]] hierarchy hides. **107th ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of Ch 11.** Mints **3 new concept pages** ([[HardDisk]], [[SolidStateDrive]], [[NonVolatileMemory]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 11.1 The Memory Hierarchy](sources/dis-11-1-memory-hierarchy.md) — **First leaf of Ch 11 *The Memory Hierarchy*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — opens **Part IV** after the three-ISA assembly arc (Ch 7 / 8 / 9) and the Ch 10 cross-ISA closer. Single short opening section codifies the **fundamental performance/capacity trade-off** — *"devices with higher capacities offer lower performance... no single device does both. This trade-off between performance and capacity is known as the memory hierarchy"* — and enumerates the **six-tier pyramid** from highest performance / lowest capacity to lowest performance / highest capacity: [[CpuRegister|Registers]] → [[CacheMemory|Cache]] ([[CacheLevel|L1 / L2 / L3]]) → [[RAM|Main Memory]] → [[FlashMemory|Flash Disk]] → Traditional Disk → Remote Secondary Storage. Cost dimension named (*"faster devices are more expensive, both in terms of bytes per dollar and operational costs (e.g., energy usage)"*); multi-level cache structure introduced (*"L1 (very small and fast, near the [[ALU]]), L2 (larger and slower), and L3 (shared among multicore CPUs)"*); programmer-stance commitment fixed (*"Ideally, programmers wouldn't need to worry about data location, though performance-critical code sections may justify such optimization"*). **No latency numbers, no [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] discussion, no *memory wall* term** — deferred to 11.2 *Storage Devices* / 11.3 *Locality* / 11.4 *Caching* / 11.5 *Cache Analysis and Cachegrind* / 11.6 *Caching on Multicore Processors* / 11.7 *Summary* / 11.8 *Exercises*. **106th ingested DIS chapter — opens Ch 11.** Mints **1 new concept page** ([[CacheLevel]]) and **expands [[MemoryHierarchy]] in place** from a [[d2l-computational-performance|D2L]] / [[parproc-appA-systems-issues|ParProc-App-A]] stub into full [[DiveIntoSystems|DIS]] coverage.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 10 Key Assembly Takeaways](sources/dis-10-asm-takeaways.md) — **Single-page Ch 10** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — short **cross-ISA closer** that distills the three preceding assembly chapters (Ch 7 *[[X86_64|x86-64]]* + Ch 8 *[[IA32]]* + Ch 9 *[[ARM64|ARMv8]]*) into a small set of [[ISA]]-independent invariants: every machine defines an [[ISA]] (`uname -m`); every [[ISA]] exposes [[CpuRegister|registers]] (general-purpose + special-purpose); every instruction has an [[OpCode|opcode]] + [[Operand|operands]]; *"core instructions are often combined to represent more complex data structures like arrays, structs, and matrices"*; the [[CCompiler|compiler]] uses the [[CallStack|stack]] of the process's [[AddressSpace|virtual address space]] to store temporary data — *"on all modern systems, the program stack grows toward lower memory addresses"*; and *"all systems are vulnerable to security vulnerabilities like [[BufferOverflow|buffer overflow]]"* — defended uniformly by [[BoundsChecking|bounded-input C functions]] ([[Fgets|`fgets`]] / [[Strncpy|`strncpy`]] / `snprintf`). Closes with a *Further Reading* pointer to the Intel and ARM [[ISA]] specs. **105th ingested DIS chapter — closes the three-ISA assembly arc.** **No new concept pages** — pure recap; reuses [[ISA]] / [[X86_64]] / [[IA32]] / [[ARM64]] / [[CpuRegister]] / [[OpCode]] / [[Operand]] / [[CallStack]] / [[BufferOverflow]] / [[Fgets]] / [[Strncpy]] / [[EmbeddedSystems]] / [[CCompiler]].
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.11 Exercises (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-11-arm64-exercises.md) — **Eleventh and final leaf** of Ch 9 of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — exercise-set close that **fully completes Ch 9 *64-bit ARM Assembly***. Single-page redirect into the book's interactive exercises platform; drills the full Ch 9.1–Ch 9.10 [[ARM64|AArch64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] surface (registers / addressing modes / [[LoadStoreArchitecture|load/store]] / data movement / arithmetic / control flow / functions / recursion / arrays / matrices / structs / buffer overflow). **Structural twin** of [[dis-7-11-x86-64-exercises|Ch 7.11]] / [[dis-8-11-ia32-exercises|Ch 8.11]]; structural sibling of [[dis-1-8-exercises|Ch 1.8]] / [[dis-2-11-exercises|Ch 2.11]] / [[dis-4-10-exercises|Ch 4.10]] / [[dis-5-11-exercises|Ch 5.11]] — *exercise-set closes chapter* pattern. **All three assembly chapters** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* (Ch 7 + Ch 8 + Ch 9) now in the wiki — full [[CISC]] / [[RISC]] cross-ISA comparability. **104th ingested DIS chapter — closes Ch 9.** **No new concept pages.**
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.10 Buffer Overflows (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-10-arm64-buffer-overflow.md) — **Tenth leaf** of Ch 9 of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-10-x86-64-buffer-overflow|Ch 7.10]] / [[dis-8-10-ia32-buffer-overflow|Ch 8.10]] — the **security payoff** of the Ch 9 stack-discipline tour. Inverts the [[dis-9-5-arm64-functions|Ch 9.5]] / [[dis-9-6-arm64-recursion|Ch 9.6]] [[CallStack|call-stack]] discipline: unbounded `scanf("%s", buf)` overwrites the **saved [[LinkRegister|`x30`]] in the stack frame** (spilled there by the [[ARM64FunctionPrologue|prologue]]'s `stp x29, x30, [sp, #-N]!`), redirecting [[ARM64Ret|`ret`]] (which sets `pc = x30`) to attacker-chosen code. **Headline [[ARM64]]-specific attack-surface note**: although [[LinkRegister|`x30`]] is register-resident during the call, **non-leaf functions spill it to the stack** — recreating the [[X86_64|x86]] / [[IA32]] stack-resident return-address vulnerability. **Leaf functions immune** (no spill) — a structural defense [[X86_64|x86]] / [[IA32]] cannot offer because [[CallInstruction|`callq` / `call`]] always pushes. Same defense taxonomy ([[StackCanary]] / [[AddressSpaceLayoutRandomization|ASLR]] / [[ExecutableSpaceProtection|NX]] / bounded input). **103rd ingested DIS chapter — tenth leaf of Ch 9.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[BufferOverflow]] / [[StackSmashing]] / [[ReturnAddressOverwrite]] / [[StackCanary]] / [[AddressSpaceLayoutRandomization]] / [[ExecutableSpaceProtection]] / [[ReturnOrientedProgramming]] from [[dis-7-10-x86-64-buffer-overflow|Ch 7.10]].
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.9 Structs in Assembly (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-9-arm64-structs.md) — **Ninth leaf** of Ch 9 of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-9-x86-64-structs|Ch 7.9]] / [[dis-8-9-ia32-structs|Ch 8.9]]. Compiles [[CStruct|C struct]] at [[ARM64]] width: fields stored contiguously in declaration order, accessed via the second [[ARM64AddressingMode|addressing-mode form]] `[xN, #imm]` (base + signed immediate offset — `str w1, [x0, #64]` writes a 4-byte field 64 bytes past struct base). **Same 8-byte [[AlignmentRule|alignment]] policy as [[X86_64|x86-64]]** (unlike [[IA32]]'s 4-byte cap); [[StructPadding|padding]] inserted by compiler. Floating-point fields use `sN` / `dN` SIMD/FP registers. **102nd ingested DIS chapter — ninth leaf of Ch 9.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[StructLayout]] / [[StructPadding]] / [[AlignmentRule]] / [[CStruct]] / [[MemoryAlignment]] / [[ARM64AddressingMode]].
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.8 Matrices in Assembly (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-8-arm64-matrices.md) — **Eighth leaf** of Ch 9 of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-8-x86-64-matrices|Ch 7.8]] / [[dis-8-8-ia32-matrices|Ch 8.8]]. Extends [[dis-9-7-arm64-arrays|Ch 9.7]]'s 1-D pattern to 2-D [[MultidimensionalArray|matrices]] at the [[ARM64]] surface. **Contiguous** (`int M1[4][3]`) — `M[i][j]` collapses to single linear offset `(i*cols+j)*4` via [[ARM64AddressingMode|`[xN, xM, LSL, #2]`]] scaled-index form; **noncontiguous [[ArrayOfArrays|array-of-arrays]]** (`int **`) requires two-stage dereference (scale-8 load row pointer with `LSL, #3`, then scale-4 load element with `LSL, #2`). [[RowMajorOrder|Row-major]] layout invariant — [[CLanguage|C]]-language-level, ISA-independent. Nested `cmp` + [[ARM64ConditionalBranch|`b.cond`]] loops from [[dis-9-4-3-arm64-loops|Ch 9.4.3]]. **101st ingested DIS chapter — eighth leaf of Ch 9.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[MultidimensionalArray]] / [[RowMajorOrder]] / [[ArrayOfArrays]] / [[AsmArrayAccess]] / [[ScaledIndexAddressing]] / [[ARM64AddressingMode]].
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.7 Arrays in Assembly (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-7-arm64-arrays.md) — **Seventh leaf** of Ch 9 of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-7-x86-64-arrays|Ch 7.7]] / [[dis-8-7-ia32-arrays|Ch 8.7]]. Operationalizes [[CArray|C array]] access at [[ARM64]] width: `arr[i]` compiles to `*(arr+i)` via the **fourth [[ARM64AddressingMode|addressing-mode form]]** `[xN, xM, LSL, #s]` (`ldr w0, [x1, x2, LSL, #2]` — base + scaled register index; `LSL, #2` = ×4 for `int`, `LSL, #3` = ×8 for `long` / pointer). **Headline [[ARM64]]-distinctive feature**: scale as **explicit bit-count shift** (vs [[X86AddressingMode|`disp(base, index, scale)`]]'s numeric scale factor). Same source-level `arr[i]` ↔ `*(arr+i)` identity. Pointer width 64-bit (`x`-regs); element value 32-bit (`w`-regs); `ldrsw` for 32→64 sign-extend. **100th ingested DIS chapter — seventh leaf of Ch 9.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[AsmArrayAccess]] / [[ScaledIndexAddressing]] / [[CArray]] / [[ArrayIndexing]] / [[ArrayDecay]] / [[ARM64AddressingMode]].
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.6 Recursion (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-6-arm64-recursion.md) — **Sixth leaf** of Ch 9 of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-6-x86-64-recursion|Ch 7.6]] / [[dis-8-6-ia32-recursion|Ch 8.6]]. Applies [[dis-9-5-arm64-functions|Ch 9.5]]'s [[ARM64BranchAndLink|`bl`]] / [[ARM64Ret|`ret`]] + [[ARM64CallingConvention|AAPCS64]] self-referentially via `sumr`. Headline rule: *"Each recursive call creates new stack frames"* — recursion adds **no new instructions**, just a dynamic-call-chain pattern. **[[ARM64]]-specific delta**: because [[LinkRegister|`x30`]] is a **single register**, every recursive (and non-leaf) function **must** save `x30` to its frame via `stp x29, x30, [sp, #-32]!` — otherwise the nested `bl sumr` overwrites the outer caller's return address. [[X86_64|x86]] / [[IA32]] don't need this discipline ([[CallInstruction|`callq` / `call`]] auto-push). **99th ingested DIS chapter — sixth leaf of Ch 9.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[Recursion]] / [[CallStack]] / [[StackFrame]] / [[ExecutionStack]] / [[LinkRegister]] / [[ARM64FunctionPrologue]].
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.5 Functions in Assembly (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-5-arm64-functions.md) — **Fifth leaf** of Ch 9 of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]*, **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-5-x86-64-functions|Ch 7.5]] / [[dis-8-5-ia32-functions|Ch 8.5]]. Closes the per-ISA function-call mechanism at [[ARM64|AArch64]] width. Adds **two new control-flow instructions** — [[ARM64BranchAndLink|`bl`]] (`x30 = pc + 4; pc = addr`) / [[ARM64Ret|`ret`]] (`pc = x30`) — and the **[[ARM64CallingConvention|AAPCS64]] calling convention**: 8 argument registers `x0`–`x7` (vs [[SystemVCallingConvention|System V]]'s 6 and [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]]'s 0); return in `x0`; **[[LinkRegister|`x30`]] holds return address** (vs [[X86_64|x86]]'s stack-only); [[FramePointer|`x29`]] as frame pointer; [[StackPointer|`sp`]] 16-byte aligned. **No `push`/`pop`** — the [[ARM64FunctionPrologue|prologue/epilogue]] uses pre-/post-indexed [[ARM64DataMovement|`stp` / `ldp`]] from [[dis-9-2-arm64-common|Ch 9.2]] instead (`stp x29, x30, [sp, #-N]!` / `ldp x29, x30, [sp], #N`). **98th ingested DIS chapter — fifth leaf of Ch 9.** Mints **5 new concept pages** ([[ARM64CallingConvention]], [[ARM64FunctionPrologue]], [[LinkRegister]], [[ARM64BranchAndLink]], [[ARM64Ret]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.4.3 Loops in Assembly (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-4-3-arm64-loops.md) — **Third leaf** of [[dis-9-4-arm64-conditional-loops|Ch 9.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-4-3-x86-64-loops|Ch 7.4.3]] / [[dis-8-4-3-ia32-loops|Ch 8.4.3]]. Re-composes [[dis-9-4-1-arm64-preliminaries|Ch 9.4.1]]'s [[ARM64Cmp|`cmp`]] + [[ARM64ConditionalBranch|`b.cond`]] primitives into the **backward-branching shape** that implements [[CLanguage|C]]'s three loop forms ([[WhileLoop|`while`]] / [[ForLoop|`for`]] / [[DoWhileLoop|`do`–`while`]]). *"Like if statements, loops in assembly are also implemented using branch instructions"*; *"every for loop can be represented by a while loop"* — both forms produce identical [[ARM64]] assembly. Worked example `sumUp()`: `ldr w1, [sp, #28]` → `ldr w0, [sp, #12]` → `cmp w1, w0` → `b.le 0x73c` — the canonical four-instruction loop-test with [[LoadStoreArchitecture|load/store discipline]] visible at the loop boundary. **97th ingested DIS chapter — third leaf of Ch 9.4.** **No new concept pages** — reuses the four 9.4.1 mechanism pages.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.4.2 If Statements in Assembly (ARM64)](sources/dis-9-4-2-arm64-if-statements.md) — **Second leaf** of [[dis-9-4-arm64-conditional-loops|Ch 9.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-4-2-x86-64-if-statements|Ch 7.4.2]] / [[dis-8-4-2-ia32-if-statements|Ch 8.4.2]]. Operationalizes [[dis-9-4-1-arm64-preliminaries|Ch 9.4.1]]'s mechanism set into the canonical [[IfStatement|`if`]] / [[ElseStatement|`else`]] compilation pattern at the [[ARM64]] surface. **Two-form pattern**: (1) **branch-based** — `cmp` + `b.cond` on the **negated** source condition jumps over the body to the `else` arm (*"a 'jump' (to the `else`) occurs when conditions are not true"*); (2) **branch-free** — [[ARM64ConditionalSelect|`csel D, R1, R2, cond`]] performs `D = cond ? R1 : R2` in one instruction, eliminating the [[ControlHazard|control hazard]] / [[BranchPrediction|branch-prediction]] cost — the [[ARM64]] analog of [[X86ConditionalMove|x86 `cmov`]]. Same compiler-caution caveat as Ch 7.4.2: *"the compiler is very cautious about optimizing branch instructions into `csel` instructions, especially in cases where side effects and pointer values are involved"* — both arms must be safely pre-evaluable. **96th ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of Ch 9.4.** **No new concept pages**.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.4.1 Preliminaries (ARM64 Conditional Control)](sources/dis-9-4-1-arm64-preliminaries.md) — **First leaf** of [[dis-9-4-arm64-conditional-loops|Ch 9.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-4-1-x86-64-preliminaries|Ch 7.4.1]] / [[dis-8-4-1-ia32-preliminaries|Ch 8.4.1]]. Introduces the **four mechanisms** every [[ARM64]] conditional construct rests on: the **[[ARM64FlagsRegister|NZCV condition-flag register]]** (single-bit ALU side-channel inside `PSTATE` — **N**egative / **Z**ero / **C**arry / o**V**erflow), the **[[ARM64Cmp|`cmp` / `cmn` / `tst`]] comparison instructions** (flag-only aliases of `subs xzr` / `adds xzr` / `ands xzr` — sole purpose is to set NZCV; `cmn` = compare-negative add-and-discard has no direct [[X86_64|x86]] equivalent; `tst x0, x0` is the canonical zero-test idiom), the **[[ARM64ConditionalBranch|`b.cond` family]]** (`b.eq` / `b.ne` / `b.lt` / `b.gt` / `b.le` / `b.ge` / `b.hi` / `b.lo` / ...), and the **[[ARM64ConditionalSelect|`csel`]] conditional-select** (branch-free data conditional — [[ARM64]] analog of [[X86ConditionalMove|x86 `cmov`]]). **Headline distinctions from [[X86FlagsRegister|x86 FLAGS]]**: (1) flag-setting is **opt-in via `s` suffix** ([[dis-9-3-arm64-arithmetic|Ch 9.3]]) rather than default-on; (2) **inverted borrow polarity** — `cmp` sets C=1 when subtraction does *not* borrow (opposite of [[X86FlagsRegister|x86 CF]]); (3) `b.cond` has **±1 MB range** vs unconditional `b`'s ±128 MB — *"conditional branch instructions have a much more limited range (1 MB) than the `b` instruction"*; (4) signed/unsigned split lives in the **consumer suffix** (`lt`/`le`/`gt`/`ge` consume N+V; `lo`/`ls`/`hi`/`hs` consume C), not in the [[ARM64Cmp|comparison]] that preceded it. **95th ingested DIS chapter — first leaf of Ch 9.4.** Mints **4 new concept pages** ([[ARM64FlagsRegister]], [[ARM64Cmp]], [[ARM64ConditionalBranch]], [[ARM64ConditionalSelect]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.4 Conditional Control and Loops (ARMv8)](sources/dis-9-4-arm64-conditional-loops.md) — **Fourth leaf** of Ch 9 *64-bit ARM Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* and the **hub page** opening the three-subsection treatment of [[ControlFlow|control flow]] at the [[ARM64|AArch64]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level. **Non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]] / [[dis-8-4-ia32-conditional-loops|Ch 8.4]] — pivots from [[dis-9-3-arm64-arithmetic|Ch 9.3]]'s **straight-line arithmetic / shift / bitwise surface** to **branch-driven non-sequential execution**: how the compiler translates [[CLanguage|C]]'s [[IfStatement|`if` / `else`]] and [[WhileLoop|`while`]] / [[ForLoop|`for`]] / [[DoWhileLoop|`do`–`while`]] constructs into [[ARM64]] instructions that **modify the `pc` program counter** based on evaluated conditions. Three subsections deliver the mechanism set: 9.4.1 *Preliminaries* ([[ARM64FlagsRegister|NZCV]] + [[ARM64Cmp|`cmp`/`cmn`/`tst`]] + [[ARM64ConditionalBranch|`b.cond`]] + [[ARM64ConditionalSelect|`csel`]]), 9.4.2 *If Statements* (forward-branch + `csel` branch-free), 9.4.3 *Loops* (backward-branch). **94th ingested DIS chapter — fourth leaf of Ch 9.** Hub-only — no new concept pages.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.3 Arithmetic Instructions (ARMv8)](sources/dis-9-3-arm64-arithmetic.md) — **Third leaf of Ch 9 *64-bit ARM Assembly*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-3-x86-64-arithmetic|Ch 7.3]] / [[dis-8-3-ia32-arithmetic|Ch 8.3]]. Extends [[dis-9-2-arm64-common|Ch 9.2]]'s data-movement primitives with the three pure-register instruction families the [[LoadStoreArchitecture|load/store rule]] reserves for register-only operands: **integer arithmetic** (`add` / `sub` / `neg` + carry forms `adc` / `sbc` / `ngc` + multiply family `mul` / `madd` / `msub` / `mneg` + division `udiv` / `sdiv` — **no hidden `%rax`/`%rdx`** like [[X86MulInstruction|x86 `imul`]] / [[X86DivInstruction|x86 `idiv`]]; the four-operand fused **multiply-accumulate composites** `madd` / `msub` / `mneg` have **no [[CISC]] equivalent**), **bit-shift** (`lsl` / `lsr` / `asr` / `ror` — 6-bit shift count, peer `ror` rotate with no `rol` mnemonic), and **bitwise** (`and` / `orr` / `eor` / `mvn` plus three [[ARM64]]-specific inverted-operand composites `bic` = `A & ~B` / `orn` = `A | ~B` / `eon` = `A ^ ~B`). **Headline ISA-distinctive feature**: the **`s` suffix** (`adds`, `subs`, `ands`) toggles **flag-setting** at the instruction level — inlining what [[X86_64|x86-64]] requires as a separate [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] / [[TestInstruction|`test`]] instruction. Canonical anti-premature-optimization caveat restated: *"modern compilers automatically optimize arithmetic with bitwise operations when beneficial, so premature optimization in source code is discouraged."* **93rd ingested DIS chapter — third leaf of Ch 9.** Mints **3 new concept pages** ([[ARM64ArithmeticInstructions]], [[ARM64ShiftInstructions]], [[ARM64BitwiseInstructions]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.2 Common ARMv8 Instructions](sources/dis-9-2-arm64-common.md) — **Second leaf of Ch 9 *64-bit ARM Assembly*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **non-twin structural sibling** of [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]] / [[dis-8-2-ia32-common|Ch 8.2]]. Introduces the **data-movement primitives** of [[ARM64]]: `mov` (register-only, **no memory operand** — unlike [[X86MovInstruction|x86 `mov`]]), `ldr D, [addr]` (memory → register, *load*), `str S, [addr]` (register → memory, *store*) — **the only three instructions that touch memory** per the [[LoadStoreArchitecture|load/store rule]] from [[dis-9-1-arm64-basics|Ch 9.1]] — plus the **pair extensions** `ldp` / `stp` that move **two consecutive 64-bit values** in one instruction (no [[CISC]] equivalent), with **pre-indexed** (`[xN, #imm]!`) and **post-indexed** (`[xN], #imm`) addressing-mode forms that fold pointer-update into the load/store itself. **Canonical prologue/epilogue idiom**: `stp x29, x30, [sp, #-16]!` saves frame-pointer + link-register **and** advances `sp` by `-16` in one instruction — collapsing what [[X86_64|x86-64]] expresses as three instructions (`sub` + two `mov`s). The `adder2` worked example returns with full annotation of the `[sp, #12]` stack-slot access — the **store-then-immediately-reload** discipline made visible. **92nd ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of Ch 9.** Mints **1 new concept page** ([[ARM64DataMovement]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 9.1 ARMv8 Assembly Basics](sources/dis-9-1-arm64-basics.md) — **First leaf of Ch 9 *64-bit ARM Assembly*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* and the **third-ISA structural sibling** of [[dis-7-1-x86-64-basics|Ch 7.1]] / [[dis-8-1-ia32-basics|Ch 8.1]] — but **not** a structural twin: [[ARM64]] is a distinct [[RISC]] [[ISA]] with a meaningfully different instruction model. **Headline mechanism deltas**: (1) **[[LoadStoreArchitecture|load/store architecture]]** — *"Data cannot be read or written to memory directly; instead, ARM follows a load/store model, which requires data to be operated on in registers."* Memory operands appear only on `ldr` / `str`; arithmetic / logic / shift take registers + immediates only. (2) **31 general-purpose 64-bit registers** `x0`–`x30` with 32-bit `w0`–`w30` component aliases (low-32-bits, upper-32 zeroed on `wN` write) — vs Ch 7.1's 16 / Ch 8.1's 8. (3) Three special registers — [[StackPointer|`sp`]] / `pc` / `zr` (zero register, permanently 0). (4) **Destination-first** instruction format `opcode D, O1, O2` — mirrors [[IntelSyntax|Intel order]], not [[AtAndTSyntax|AT&T]]; bare register names (no `%`), `#`-prefixed immediates, bracketed memory forms. (5) **[[ARM64AddressingMode|Four addressing-mode forms]]** — `[xN]` / `[xN, #imm]` / `[xN, xM]` / `[xN, xM, LSL, #s]` with **explicit `LSL` shift mnemonic + bit count** instead of [[X86AddressingMode|`disp(base, index, scale)`]]'s numeric scale factor (`LSL, #2` = ×4 for `int` arrays; `LSL, #3` = ×8 for `long` / pointer arrays). Same `adder2(int a) { return a + 2; }` worked example as Ch 7.1 / Ch 8.1 compiles to **three instructions** unoptimized — `str w0, [sp, #12]` → `ldr w0, [sp, #12]` → `add w0, w0, #0x2` — store-then-reload makes the load/store discipline visible. **91st ingested DIS chapter — first leaf of Ch 9; opens the wiki's RISC-ISA coverage at the desktop/server surface (existing [[ARMCortexM]] is microcontroller-scope).** Mints **4 new concept pages** ([[ARM64]], [[AArch64Registers]], [[LoadStoreArchitecture]], [[ARM64AddressingMode]]).
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.11 Exercises (IA32)](sources/dis-8-11-ia32-exercises.md) — **Exercises section closing Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly*** of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — single-page redirect to the book's interactive exercises platform, no inline problems; drills the full Ch 8.1–Ch 8.10 [[IA32|IA32]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] surface (registers / [[X86AddressingMode|addressing modes]] / [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]] / [[X86MovInstruction|`mov`]] / arithmetic / [[AsmIfThenElse|if-else]] / [[AsmLoopPattern|loop]] / [[CallingConvention|function-call]] / [[Recursion|recursion]] / [[AsmArrayAccess|array]] / matrix / [[StructLayout|struct]] / [[StackSmashing|buffer-overflow]]); **90th ingested DIS chapter — fully completes Ch 8**, both x86-family assembly chapters of [[DiveIntoSystems]] (Ch 7 + Ch 8) now fully cataloged; **structural twin** of [[dis-7-11-x86-64-exercises|Ch 7.11]]; **no new concept pages** — pure problem-set close.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.10 Buffer Overflows (IA32)](sources/dis-8-10-ia32-buffer-overflow.md) — **Tenth leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* and the **security payoff** of the whole Ch 8 tour — **32-bit structural twin** of [[dis-7-10-x86-64-buffer-overflow|Ch 7.10]]. Inverts the [[dis-8-5-ia32-functions|Ch 8.5]] / [[dis-8-6-ia32-recursion|Ch 8.6]] [[CallStack|call-stack]] discipline — unbounded `scanf("%s", buf)` writes past a stack buffer, **overwriting saved-`%eip` at `4(%ebp)`** (4 bytes — vs 8-byte saved-`%rip` on Ch 7.10), redirecting [[RetInstruction|`ret`]] to attacker-chosen [[LittleEndian|little-endian]] address. **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) 4-byte saved-return-address payload (not 8-byte); (2) smaller buffer-to-saved-`%eip` distance per stack-word size; (3) attack mechanism, three-defense taxonomy ([[StackCanary]] / [[AddressSpaceLayoutRandomization|ASLR]] / [[ExecutableSpaceProtection|NX/W^X]]) and [[ReturnOrientedProgramming|ROP]] bypass are **structurally identical** to Ch 7.10. **Root cause**: *"the C language does not perform automatic array bounds checking"* — ISA-independent. **89th ingested DIS chapter — tenth leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[BufferOverflow]] / [[StackSmashing]] / [[ReturnAddressOverwrite]] / [[StackCanary]] / [[AddressSpaceLayoutRandomization]] / [[ExecutableSpaceProtection]] / [[ReturnOrientedProgramming]] from Ch 7.10.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.9 Structs in Assembly (IA32)](sources/dis-8-9-ia32-structs.md) — **Ninth leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **32-bit structural twin** of [[dis-7-9-x86-64-structs|Ch 7.9]]. Compiles the [[CLanguage|C]] [[CStruct|struct]] at IA32 width: fields stored **contiguously in declaration order**, accessed via fixed byte-offsets (`disp(base)` addressing). **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) [[AlignmentRule|alignment policy]] **caps at 4 bytes** — *"two-byte data types reside at a two-byte-aligned address whereas four-byte data types reside at four-byte-aligned addresses"* — vs Ch 7.9's 8-byte alignment for `double`/`long long`/pointer; (2) pointer fields 4 bytes wide and 4-byte-aligned (vs 8/8 on x86-64); (3) [[StructPadding|padding]] is typically smaller — `struct { int x; double d; }` wastes 0 bytes on IA32 (vs 4 on x86-64). Field-reordering minimizes wasted space. **88th ingested DIS chapter — ninth leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[StructLayout]] / [[StructPadding]] / [[AlignmentRule]] / [[CStruct]] / [[X86AddressingMode]] from Ch 7.9.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.8 Matrices in Assembly (IA32)](sources/dis-8-8-ia32-matrices.md) — **Eighth leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **32-bit structural twin** of [[dis-7-8-x86-64-matrices|Ch 7.8]]. Extends [[dis-8-7-ia32-arrays|Ch 8.7]]'s scaled-index array compilation to **2-D [[MultidimensionalArray|matrices]]**: **contiguous** (statically declared `int M1[4][3]` or single-`malloc` `int *M2`) indexed by `(i*cols+j)*4` from base, vs **non-contiguous** [[ArrayOfArrays|array-of-arrays]] (`int **M3`) requiring **two-stage dereferencing**. **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) row pointers 4 bytes wide (vs 8 on Ch 7.8) — at IA32 width pointer-stride and int-stride happen to coincide; (2) array base from `0x8(%ebp)` per [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]] (not `%rdi`); (3) [[X86ShiftInstructions|`shl`]] / [[X86MulInstruction|`imul`]] / [[LeaInstruction|`leal`]] do the scaled-multiply at 32-bit width. [[RowMajorOrder|Row-major]] memory layout invariant; `M[i][j]` bracket notation works on `int M[ROWS][COLS]` and `int **M` but **not** on single-`malloc` flat matrices. **87th ingested DIS chapter — eighth leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[MultidimensionalArray]] / [[RowMajorOrder]] / [[ArrayOfArrays]] / [[AsmArrayAccess]] / [[ScaledIndexAddressing]] from Ch 7.8.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.7 Arrays in Assembly (IA32)](sources/dis-8-7-ia32-arrays.md) — **Seventh leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **32-bit structural twin** of [[dis-7-7-x86-64-arrays|Ch 7.7]]. Operationalizes [[CArray|C array]] access at IA32 width: `arr[i]` compiles to pointer arithmetic `*(arr+i)`, emitted as a [[ScaledIndexAddressing|scaled-index]] [[X86AddressingMode|addressing-mode]] operand `disp(base, index, scale)` where `scale = sizeof(elem)` (4 for `int`/pointer at IA32, 2 for `short`, 1 for `char`, 8 for `double`). **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) [[LeaInstruction|`leal`]] (`l` suffix) for 32-bit effective-address computation — vs `leaq`; (2) base & index in 32-bit registers; (3) array base passed at `0x8(%ebp)` per [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]] (not `%rdi`); (4) scaled-index operand syntax `0x0(,%eax,4)` is **structurally identical** to Ch 7.7 (CISC-family invariant). Headline rules carry over: `arr[i]` ↔ `*(arr+i)`; `leal` for address arithmetic vs `movl` for value access. **86th ingested DIS chapter — seventh leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[AsmArrayAccess]] / [[ScaledIndexAddressing]] / [[LeaInstruction]] / [[X86AddressingMode]] / [[CArray]] from Ch 7.7.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.6 Recursion (IA32)](sources/dis-8-6-ia32-recursion.md) — **Sixth leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **32-bit structural twin** of [[dis-7-6-x86-64-recursion|Ch 7.6]]. Applies [[dis-8-5-ia32-functions|Ch 8.5]]'s [[CallInstruction|`call`]] / [[RetInstruction|`ret`]] / [[LeaveInstruction|`leave`]] + [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]] prologue/epilogue self-referentially — *"each function call generates a new stack frame"*, no new instruction required. **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) recursive `n` parameter read from `0x8(%ebp)` per cdecl (not `%edi`); (2) recursive [[CallInstruction|`call`]] pushes a **4-byte** saved-`%eip` (not 8-byte saved-`%rip`); (3) recursive argument re-push pattern — `mov 0x8(%ebp), %eax; sub $1, %eax; push %eax; call sumr` — argument is pushed (vs register-loaded on Ch 7.6); (4) frame-cleanup `add $0x4, %esp` after return (caller cleanup per cdecl). Saved-[[FramePointer|`%ebp`]] linked-list links frames backward along the [[CallStack|call stack]]; [[LeaveInstruction|`leave`]] unwinds each frame on return; return value chains via [[CalleeSavedRegister|`%eax`]]. **85th ingested DIS chapter — sixth leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[Recursion]] / [[CallStack]] / [[StackFrame]] / [[ExecutionStack]] from Ch 7.6.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.5 Functions in Assembly (IA32)](sources/dis-8-5-ia32-functions.md) — **Fifth leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — **32-bit structural twin** of [[dis-7-5-x86-64-functions|Ch 7.5]]. Adds the function-call instruction family — [[CallInstruction|`call`]] / [[RetInstruction|`ret`]] / [[LeaveInstruction|`leave`]] — and the [[CallStack|call-stack]] / [[StackFrame|stack-frame]] discipline at IA32 width under [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]]. **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) **all parameters pushed on stack** — IA32 cdecl has *no* six-argument-register fast path (vs Ch 7.5's [[SystemVCallingConvention|System V]] `%rdi`/`%rsi`/`%rdx`/`%rcx`/`%r8`/`%r9`); n-th parameter read inside callee from `%ebp+8+4*(n-1)`; (2) **return value in [[CalleeSavedRegister|`%eax`]]** (or `%edx:%eax` for 64-bit returns); (3) stack-frame anchors [[StackPointer|`%esp`]] / [[FramePointer|`%ebp`]]; (4) mnemonics drop `q` suffix — `call` / `ret` / `leave`; (5) [[CallInstruction|`call`]] pushes a **4-byte** saved-[[InstructionPointer|`%eip`]] (not 8-byte saved-`%rip`); (6) **caller cleanup** of arguments via `add $N, %esp` (vs callee-cleanup on Windows stdcall) — what makes cdecl naturally variadic-compatible ([[Printf|`printf`]] / [[Scanf|`scanf`]]). Headline rules carry over: prologue/epilogue pattern, [[CallerSavedRegister|caller-saved]] (`%eax`/`%ecx`/`%edx`) vs [[CalleeSavedRegister|callee-saved]] (`%ebx`/`%esi`/`%edi`/`%ebp`) partition. **84th ingested DIS chapter — fifth leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[CallInstruction]] / [[RetInstruction]] / [[LeaveInstruction]] / [[CallingConvention]] / [[CdeclCallingConvention]] / [[StackPointer]] / [[FramePointer]] / [[CallerSavedRegister]] / [[CalleeSavedRegister]] from Ch 7.5 + Ch 8.1.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.4.3 Loops in Assembly (IA32)](sources/dis-8-4-3-ia32-loops.md) — **Third and final leaf** of [[dis-8-4-ia32-conditional-loops|Ch 8.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **32-bit structural twin of [[dis-7-4-3-x86-64-loops|Ch 7.4.3]]**. Operationalizes the [[dis-8-4-1-ia32-preliminaries|Ch 8.4.1]] mechanism families ([[X86FlagsRegister|FLAGS]] + [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] + [[X86JumpInstructions|conditional jumps]]) into the **canonical jump-to-test compilation pattern** for [[CLanguage|C]]'s [[WhileLoop|`while`]] / [[ForLoop|`for`]] / [[DoWhileLoop|`do`–`while`]] constructs at the [[IA32]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] surface via the same `sumUp(int n)` worked example as [[dis-7-4-3-x86-64-loops|Ch 7.4.3]]. **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) local variables live in [[FramePointer|`%ebp`]]-relative **negative** stack slots — `total` at `-0x8(%ebp)`, `i` at `-0x4(%ebp)` — vs Ch 7.4.3's register / `%rbp`-relative storage; (2) parameter `n` is read from the stack at `0x8(%ebp)` per [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]], not `%edi` per [[SystemVCallingConvention|System V]]; (3) the unconditional `jmp` target is a 32-bit [[InstructionPointer|`%eip`]] address; (4) epilogue is `leave; ret` (IA32 mnemonics). Three jump-to-test pattern rules carry over **unchanged** from Ch 7.4.3: (a) the canonical `while`/`for` pattern is **jump-to-test** — unconditional `jmp` to the condition, conditional jump on the **un-negated** loop condition branches **back** to the body — the **inverse** of [[dis-8-4-2-ia32-if-statements|Ch 8.4.2]]'s if-pattern; (b) `for` and `while` produce **identical assembly** — *"every `for` loop can be represented by a `while` loop"*; (c) `do`–`while` **drops the leading `jmp`** because the body executes once unconditionally. **83rd ingested DIS chapter — third and final leaf of [[dis-8-4-ia32-conditional-loops|Ch 8.4]], closes the [[ControlFlow|control-flow]] section of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[AsmLoopPattern]], [[X86JumpInstructions]], [[CmpInstruction]], [[X86FlagsRegister]] from Ch 7.4.3 unchanged.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.4.2 If Statements in Assembly (IA32)](sources/dis-8-4-2-ia32-if-statements.md) — **Second leaf** of [[dis-8-4-ia32-conditional-loops|Ch 8.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **32-bit structural twin of [[dis-7-4-2-x86-64-if-statements|Ch 7.4.2]]**. Operationalizes the [[dis-8-4-1-ia32-preliminaries|Ch 8.4.1]] mechanism families ([[X86FlagsRegister|FLAGS]] + [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] + [[X86JumpInstructions|conditional jumps]]) into the **canonical compilation pattern** for [[CLanguage|C]]'s [[IfStatement|`if`]] / [[ElseStatement|`else`]] construct via the same `getSmallest(int x, int y)` worked example as [[dis-7-4-2-x86-64-if-statements|Ch 7.4.2]] — traced through both **unoptimized (branch-based)** and **`-O1`-optimized (branch-free, [[X86ConditionalMove|`cmov`]]-based)** [[IA32]] assembly. **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) parameters read from the stack via [[FramePointer|`%ebp`]]-anchored offsets (`mov 0x8(%ebp), %eax`; `cmp 0xc(%ebp), %eax`) per [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]] — **not** from `%edi`/`%esi` per [[SystemVCallingConvention|System V]]; (2) return value lives in `%eax` (not `%rax`); (3) the [[X86ConditionalMove|`cmovle`]] form is `cmovle 0x8(%ebp), %eax` — moves a 32-bit stack-memory operand vs Ch 7.4.2's register-to-register `cmovle %edi, %eax`. Two **branch-pattern rules** carry over unchanged: (a) the branch-based form jumps on the **negated** source condition — *"a 'jump' (to the `else`) occurs when conditions are not true"*; (b) the `-O1` substitution to [[X86ConditionalMove|`cmov`]] **eliminates** the [[ControlHazard|control hazard]] / [[BranchPrediction|branch-prediction]] dependency at the cost of pre-evaluating both arms — same safety constraint ([[NullPointerSafety|null-pointer dereference]] forces fallback). **82nd ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of Ch 8.4.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[X86ConditionalMove]], [[AsmIfThenElse]], [[BranchInstruction]], [[CmpInstruction]], [[X86JumpInstructions]] from Ch 7.4.2 unchanged.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.4.1 Preliminaries (IA32 Conditional Control)](sources/dis-8-4-1-ia32-preliminaries.md) — **First leaf** of [[dis-8-4-ia32-conditional-loops|Ch 8.4]] of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **32-bit structural twin of [[dis-7-4-1-x86-64-preliminaries|Ch 7.4.1]]**. Re-introduces the three mechanism families every conditional construct at the [[IA32]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level rests on: the **[[X86FlagsRegister|FLAGS condition-code register]]** (ZF / SF / OF / CF), the **comparison instructions [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]] and [[TestInstruction|`test`]]** (flag-only siblings of `sub` / `and`; the **`test %eax, %eax`** idiom is the canonical register-zero test — `x AND x = 0 iff x = 0`), and the **[[X86JumpInstructions|jump-instruction family]]** (`jmp` unconditional + signed `je`/`jne`/`jg`/`jge`/`jl`/`jle` and unsigned `ja`/`jae`/`jb`/`jbe`). **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) the canonical register-zero idiom is **`test %eax, %eax`** (not `test %rax, %rax`) — same accumulator bottom-32-bits; (2) jump targets are 32-bit ([[InstructionPointer|`%eip`]] is the destination, not `%rip`); (3) the FLAGS register itself is 32-bit `EFLAGS` (vs 64-bit `RFLAGS`) but the four bits read (ZF / SF / OF / CF) live in the bottom 16 bits and are architecturally identical. The signed/unsigned-mnemonic split (`g`/`l` consume SF + OF; `a`/`b` consume CF) carries over unchanged — same [[TwosComplement|two's-complement bit-pattern-interpretation-invariance]] from [[dis-4-3-signed|Ch 4.3]] / [[dis-4-5-overflow|Ch 4.5]] realized at the IA32 instruction surface. **81st ingested DIS chapter — first leaf of Ch 8.4.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[X86FlagsRegister]], [[ConditionCode]], [[CmpInstruction]], [[TestInstruction]], [[X86JumpInstructions]] from Ch 7.4.1 unchanged.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.4 Conditional Control and Loops (IA32)](sources/dis-8-4-ia32-conditional-loops.md) — **Fourth leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* and the **hub page** opening the three-subsection treatment of [[ControlFlow|control flow]] at the [[IA32]] [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] level — the **32-bit structural twin of [[dis-7-4-x86-64-conditional-loops|Ch 7.4]]**. Pivots from [[dis-8-3-ia32-arithmetic|Ch 8.3]]'s straight-line extended-arithmetic surface to **branch-driven non-sequential execution** — how the compiler translates [[CLanguage|C]]'s [[IfStatement|`if` / `else`]] and [[WhileLoop|`while`]] / [[ForLoop|`for`]] / [[DoWhileLoop|`do`–`while`]] constructs into instructions that **modify the [[InstructionPointer|`%eip`]] instruction pointer** based on evaluated conditions. **Headline 32-vs-64 delta**: the instruction pointer is **[[InstructionPointer|`%eip`]]** (32-bit) not `%rip` (64-bit) — the only ISA-surface change at this hub level; the three mechanism families ([[X86FlagsRegister|FLAGS]] / [[CmpInstruction|`cmp`]]–[[TestInstruction|`test`]] / [[X86JumpInstructions|jump family]]) are structurally identical to Ch 7.4. Three subsections (8.4.1 Preliminaries / 8.4.2 If Statements / 8.4.3 Loops) deliver the leaf mechanisms; this hub is intentionally short. **80th ingested DIS chapter — fourth leaf of Ch 8.** Hub-only — no new concept pages; all condition-code / conditional-jump / branch-pattern pages from Ch 7.4 reused unchanged at IA32 width.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.3 Additional Arithmetic Instructions (IA32)](sources/dis-8-3-ia32-arithmetic.md) — **Third leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **32-bit structural twin of [[dis-7-3-x86-64-arithmetic|Ch 7.3]]**. Re-presents the same extended-arithmetic surface — extended integer arithmetic ([[X86NegInstruction|`neg`]] / `inc` / `dec`, [[X86MulInstruction|`imul`]] / `mul`, [[X86DivInstruction|`idiv`]] / `div`), [[X86ShiftInstructions|bit-shifts]] (`shl` / `sal` / `shr` / `sar`), [[X86BitwiseInstructions|bitwise logic]] (`and` / `or` / `xor` / `not`), and [[LeaInstruction|`lea`]] — at the [[IA32]] 32-bit register width. **Headline 32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) operands default to 32-bit (`l`) width — no `q` form; (2) the [[X86MulInstruction|`mul` / `imul`]] one-operand form uses the **`%edx:%eax` pair** for the 64-bit product (high 32 bits in `%edx`, low 32 in `%eax`); (3) [[X86DivInstruction|`idiv` / `div`]] reads the dividend from `%edx:%eax`, lands quotient in `%eax`, remainder in `%edx` — IA32 dividend-setup idiom is `cltd` (sign-extend `%eax` into `%edx`); (4) shift count still in `%cl`. Headline rules carry over: `not` ≠ `neg` (`~x = -x - 1`); *"to compute `77 * 4`, most compilers will translate this operation to `77 << 2` to avoid the use of an `imul` instruction"*; [[LeaInstruction|`lea`]] *"performs arithmetic on the operand specified by the source S and places the result in the destination operand D"* without memory access. **79th ingested DIS chapter — third leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[X86MulInstruction]], [[X86DivInstruction]], [[X86NegInstruction]], [[X86ShiftInstructions]], [[X86BitwiseInstructions]], [[LeaInstruction]] from [[dis-7-3-x86-64-arithmetic|Ch 7.3]]; IA32 deltas (`%edx:%eax` pair, `cltd`, 32-bit width) noted on those pages.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.2 Common Instructions (IA32)](sources/dis-8-2-ia32-common.md) — **Second leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **32-bit structural twin of [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]]**. Re-presents the same five common [[IA32]] instructions — [[X86MovInstruction|`mov`]], [[X86ArithmeticInstructions|`add` / `sub`]], [[X86StackInstructions|`push` / `pop`]] — at the 32-bit register width. **32-vs-64 deltas**: (1) `l` (4-byte) is the default operand suffix — the `q` 64-bit suffix has no IA32 application; (2) [[StackPointer|`%esp`]] / [[FramePointer|`%ebp`]] replace `%rsp` / `%rbp`; (3) [[X86StackInstructions|`push` / `pop`]] adjust [[StackPointer|`%esp`]] by **4 bytes** (not 8) — matching the 32-bit register width; (4) function return value lives in `%eax` (not `%rax`) per [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]]. Instruction semantics (`mov S, D` = `D ← S`; `add S, D` = `D ← D + S`; `sub S, D` = `D ← D − S`), operand rules ([[Constant|constant]] / [[CpuRegister|register]] / [[MemoryOperand|memory]]; no constant destination, ≤ one memory operand), [[AtAndTSyntax|source-then-destination AT&T order]], and stack-grows-down convention are **structurally identical** to [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]]. **78th ingested DIS chapter — second leaf of Ch 8.** **No new concept pages** — reuses [[X86MovInstruction]], [[X86ArithmeticInstructions]], [[X86StackInstructions]] from [[dis-7-2-x86-64-common|Ch 7.2]]; the IA32-specific machinery ([[IA32]] register set, [[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]]) lives on the [[dis-8-1-ia32-basics|Ch 8.1]] / [[IA32]] pages.
- [Dive into Systems — Ch 8.1 IA32 Assembly Basics](sources/dis-8-1-ia32-basics.md) — **First leaf** of Ch 8 *32-bit IA32 Assembly* of *[[DiveIntoSystems]]* — the **32-bit structural twin of [[dis-7-1-x86-64-basics|Ch 7.1]]**. Re-runs the `adder2` C → [[AssemblyLanguage|assembly]] walkthrough in [[AtAndTSyntax|AT&T syntax]] but compiled with `gcc -m32` against the [[IA32]] [[ISA]]. Headline 32-vs-64 deltas: **eight** [[GeneralPurposeRegister|GPRs]] (`%eax`/`%ebx`/`%ecx`/`%edx`/`%edi`/`%esi`/`%esp`/`%ebp`) vs Ch 7.1's 16 (no `%r8`–`%r15`); **letter-substitution subregisters only** (`%eax` → `%ax` → `%al`/`%ah`); **stack-based parameter passing** ([[CdeclCallingConvention|cdecl]] — all args on stack, accessed as `8(%ebp)`, `12(%ebp)`, ...) vs Ch 7.1's [[SystemVCallingConvention|System V six-argument-register]] convention; **`l` suffix the default integer width** (the `q` 64-bit suffix has no IA32 application). The [[Operand|operand]] / [[X86AddressingMode|addressing-mode]] / instruction-structure framings carry over **unchanged** from Ch 7.1. **77th ingested DIS chapter — first leaf of Ch 8.** Mints **1 new concept page** ([[CdeclCallingConvention]]) + **expands** the existing [[IA32]] page from [[dis-2-9-7-c-to-assembly|Ch 2.9.7]]'s introduction.
