### Added with [[d2l-computer-vision]] (D2L Computer Vision)
- [Ross Girshick](entities/RossGirshick.md) — Computer-vision researcher (UC Berkeley → MSR → [[FAIR]]); architect of the **R-CNN family** ([[RCNN]] 2014, [[FastRCNN]] 2015, [[FasterRCNN]] 2015, [[MaskRCNN]] 2017) — the canonical two-stage detector lineage in [[d2l-computer-vision]] §`rcnn`.
- [Wei Liu](entities/WeiLiu.md) — Computer-vision researcher (UNC Chapel Hill / Google); lead author of [[SSD]] (Liu, Anguelov, Erhan et al. 2016) — the canonical single-stage detector in [[d2l-computer-vision]] §`ssd`.
- [Leon Gatys](entities/LeonGatys.md) — Computer-vision / computational-neuroscience researcher ([[BethgeLab]], Tübingen); lead author of the seminal neural [[StyleTransfer|style-transfer]] paper (Gatys, Ecker & Bethge 2016) per [[d2l-computer-vision]] §`neural-style`.
- [Jonathan Long](entities/JonathanLong.md) — Computer-vision researcher (UC Berkeley); lead author of [[FCN]] (Long, Shelhamer & Darrell 2015) — the canonical end-to-end semantic-segmentation model per [[d2l-computer-vision]] §`fcn`.

### Added with [[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] (D2L NLP Pretraining)
- [Tomáš Mikolov](entities/TomasMikolov.md) — First author of the two 2013 [[Word2Vec|word2vec]] papers ([[SkipGram|skip-gram]] + [[CBOW]]); single most-cited author in [[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §word2vec / §approx-training.
- [Jeffrey Pennington](entities/JeffreyPennington.md) — [[StanfordUniversity|Stanford NLP]] (now [[google|Google]]) researcher; first author of **[[GloVe]]** (EMNLP 2014) per [[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §glove.
- [Piotr Bojanowski](entities/PiotrBojanowski.md) — [[fair|FAIR]] research scientist; first author of **[[FastText|fastText]]** (TACL 2017) per [[d2l-nlp-pretraining]] §subword-embedding.

### Added with [[d2l-nlp-applications]] (D2L NLP Applications)
- [Yoon Kim](entities/YoonKim.md) — MIT EECS / CSAIL NLP researcher; author of **[[TextCNN|textCNN]]** ("Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification", EMNLP 2014) — the canonical CNN-for-NLP baseline operationalized in [[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`sentiment-analysis-cnn`.
- [Ankur Parikh](entities/AnkurParikh.md) — Google Research NLP researcher; first author of the **[[DecomposableAttention|decomposable attention model]]** (Parikh, Täckström, Das & Uszkoreit, EMNLP 2016) — a pre-Transformer attention-only NLI model with the linear-complexity *decomposition trick* per [[d2l-nlp-applications]] §`natural-language-inference-attention`.
- [Samuel Bowman](entities/SamuelBowman.md) — NYU NLP professor; first author of **[[SNLI]]** (Bowman, Angeli, Potts & Manning, EMNLP 2015) and co-author of **[[CoLA]]** — the two flagship benchmarks ([[NaturalLanguageInference|NLI]], grammaticality) anchoring [[d2l-nlp-applications]].

### Added with [[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] (D2L Reinforcement Learning)
- [Richard Bellman](entities/RichardBellman.md) — RAND mathematician (1920–1984); founder of **[[DynamicProgramming|dynamic programming]]** and the **[[BellmanEquation|Bellman equation]]** ("the remainder of an optimal trajectory is also optimal") — the algorithmic foundation of [[ValueIteration]], [[QLearning]], and all of [[reinforcementlearning|RL]] ([[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §value-iter).
- [Christopher Watkins](entities/ChristopherWatkins.md) — First author of **[[QLearning|Q-Learning]]** (1989 PhD thesis; Watkins & Dayan, *Machine Learning* 1992) — the canonical [[ModelFreeLearning|model-free]] [[OffPolicyLearning|off-policy]] [[TemporalDifferenceLearning|TD]] algorithm operationalized in [[d2l-reinforcement-learning]] §qlearning.
- [Pratik Chaudhari](entities/PratikChaudhari.md) — Penn ESE / GRASP assistant professor and [[Amazon]] scientist; guest co-author of [[d2l-reinforcement-learning]].
- [Rasool Fakoor](entities/RasoolFakoor.md) — [[Amazon]] research scientist; co-author of [[d2l-reinforcement-learning]].
- [Kavosh Asadi](entities/KavoshAsadi.md) — [[Amazon]] research scientist; co-author of [[d2l-reinforcement-learning]].

### Added with [[d2l-gaussian-processes]] (D2L Gaussian Processes)
- [Andrew Gordon Wilson](entities/AndrewGordonWilson.md) — [[NewYorkUniversity|NYU]] Courant / Center for Data Science associate professor and [[amazon|Amazon]] Scholar; guest author of [[d2l-gaussian-processes]] and co-author of [[GPyTorch]]. Research program centers on scalable [[GaussianProcess|GPs]], [[BayesianDeepLearning|Bayesian deep learning]], and the kernel-methods ↔ deep-networks bridge.
- [New York University](entities/NewYorkUniversity.md) — Private research university in NYC; home of [[AndrewGordonWilson|Wilson]] (author of [[d2l-gaussian-processes]]) and [[SamuelBowman]] ([[SNLI]], [[CoLA]] in [[d2l-nlp-applications]]).
- [GPyTorch](entities/GPyTorch.md) — [[PyTorch]]-integrated GP library ([[JacobGardner|Gardner]], Pleiss, Weinberger, Bindel & [[AndrewGordonWilson|Wilson]] 2018) — SKI / KISS-GP scalable inference; production backend in [[d2l-gaussian-processes]] gp-inference.

### Added with [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] (D2L Hyperparameter Optimization)
- [Aaron Klein](entities/AaronKlein.md) — [[Amazon]] research scientist; first author of [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; primary contributor to [[SyneTune]].
- [Matthias Seeger](entities/MatthiasSeeger.md) — [[Amazon]] principal applied scientist; co-author of [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; architect of [[SyneTune]] and longtime Bayesian-ML / [[GaussianProcess|GP]] researcher.
- [Cédric Archambeau](entities/CedricArchambeau.md) — [[Amazon]] principal applied scientist; co-author of [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; led the Berlin AutoML group during [[SyneTune]]'s development.
- [James Bergstra](entities/JamesBergstra.md) — Author of *Random Search for Hyper-Parameter Optimization* (Bergstra & Bengio 2012) — the canonical justification for [[RandomSearch]] in [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]]; also TPE / [[HyperOpt]].
- [Lisha Li](entities/LishaLi.md) — First author of [[Hyperband]] (JMLR 2018) and [[ASHA]] (arxiv 1810.05934) — the multi-fidelity HPO algorithms operationalized in [[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §sh-async via [[SyneTune]].
- [LiteLLM](entities/LiteLLM.md) — Open-source Python SDK ([github.com/BerriAI/litellm](https://github.com/BerriAI/litellm)) from BerriAI providing a unified, OpenAI-shaped client over dozens of LLM providers ([[openai|OpenAI]] / [[anthropic|Anthropic]] / [[gemini|Gemini]] / Vertex AI / [[Databricks]] / [[microsoft|Azure]] / [[Anyscale]] / [[TogetherAI|Together AI]] / [[Ollama]] / [[SGLang]] / …) via a `provider/model-name` string convention. The upstream provider-abstraction layer underneath [[DSPy]]'s [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]] universal client; the wiki entry recorded by [[dspy-language-models]].
- [Ollama](entities/Ollama.md) — Open-source local-laptop LLM runtime ([ollama.ai](https://ollama.ai/)); one-line install, one-line model-pull-and-run, local HTTP server on port 11434. The local-laptop deployment regime [[DSPy]] integrates via `dspy.LM('ollama_chat/llama3.2', api_base='http://localhost:11434')` ([[dspy-language-models]]).
- [SGLang](entities/SGLang.md) — Open-source GPU inference server ([github.com/sgl-project/sglang](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang)) for open-weight LLMs; exposes an OpenAI-compatible HTTP endpoint. The self-hosted-GPU deployment regime [[DSPy]] explicitly recommends — *"To host accurate open models on your own GPU(s), we recommend SGLang"* ([[dspy-language-models]]).
- [Together AI](entities/TogetherAI.md) — Managed-API LLM inference provider ([together.ai](https://www.together.ai/)) hosting open-weight models (Llama, Mistral, Qwen, …); one of [[DSPy]]'s [[DSPyLM|`dspy.LM`]]-supported managed providers via `together_ai/...` model string ([[dspy-language-models]]).
- [Syne Tune](entities/SyneTune.md) — [[Amazon]]'s open-source distributed HPO library (Salinas et al. AutoML 2022); D2L's preferred async-HPO backend ([[d2l-hyperparameter-optimization]] §rs-async, §sh-async).

### Added with [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] (D2L Generative Adversarial Networks)
- [Ian Goodfellow](entities/IanGoodfellow.md) — Inventor of [[generativeadversarialnetwork|GANs]] (Goodfellow, Pouget-Abadie, Mirza et al. 2014) — the foundational 2014 paper [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`gan` is built on. Co-author of the *Deep Learning* textbook (Goodfellow, Bengio & Courville 2016); ex-[[google|Google Brain]] / ex-[[OpenAI]] / ex-[[apple|Apple]] / ex-[[googledeepmind|DeepMind]].
- [Alec Radford](entities/AlecRadford.md) — First author of [[DCGAN]] ([[AlecRadford|Radford]], Metz & Chintala 2015) — the canonical convolutional GAN architecture that powers [[d2l-generative-adversarial-networks]] §`dcgan`. Also first author of [[GPT]] (2018) and [[GPT2|GPT-2]] (2019); [[OpenAI]] researcher; one of the most influential generative-model researchers of the 2015–2020 era.

### Added with [[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] (D2L Appendix: Mathematics for Deep Learning)
- [Brent Werness](entities/BrentWerness.md) — [[Amazon]] applied scientist; first author of [[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] (with [[RachelHu]]).
- [Rachel Hu](entities/RachelHu.md) — [[Amazon]] applied scientist; co-author of [[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] (with [[BrentWerness]]).
- [Claude Shannon](entities/ClaudeShannon.md) — American mathematician (1916–2001); founder of [[InformationTheory|information theory]] (1948 *A Mathematical Theory of Communication*); the **bit** as a unit of information, **[[Entropy|Shannon entropy]]**, source-coding and channel-capacity theorems — every modern [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy loss]] / [[LanguageModel|LM]] training objective descends from his framework ([[d2l-appendix-mathematics]] §information-theory).

### Added with [[d2l-appendix-tools]] (D2L Appendix: Tools for Deep Learning)
- [Amazon SageMaker](entities/AmazonSageMaker.md) — AWS managed-Jupyter ML platform; D2L's *fastest path to a GPU notebook* via `ml.p3.2xlarge` (V100 + 8-core CPU) with the framework-specific D2L repo cloned at provision time ([[d2l-appendix-tools]] §`sagemaker`).
- [Amazon EC2](entities/AmazonEC2.md) — AWS's raw VM service; cheaper alternative to [[AmazonSageMaker]] for D2L (requires manual [[CUDA]] install + [[Miniconda]] + `pip install d2l==1.0.3` + ssh `-L` port-forwarding). GPU instance taxonomy: `p2` (K80) / `p3` (V100) / `p4` (A100) / `g4` (T4 inference) ([[d2l-appendix-tools]] §`aws`).

### Added with [[d2l-recommender-systems]] (D2L Recommender Systems)
- [Shuai Zhang](entities/ShuaiZhang.md) — [[Amazon]] researcher; first author of [[d2l-recommender-systems]]; co-author of the canonical *Deep Learning Based Recommender System* survey (Zhang, Yao, Sun & Tay 2019, *ACM CSUR*).
- [Yi Tay](entities/YiTay.md) — [[google|Google]] researcher; third author of [[d2l-recommender-systems]]; better known for efficient-Transformer / scaling work (*Long Range Arena*, *Efficient Transformers: A Survey*) and as a Reka AI co-founder.
- [Yehuda Koren](entities/YehudaKoren.md) — Recommender-systems researcher most associated with [[MatrixFactorization]] and the [[NetflixPrize|Netflix \$1M Prize]] (BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos); seminal 2009 MF paper and 2008 [[ImplicitFeedback|implicit-feedback]] paper anchor [[d2l-recommender-systems]] §mf and §recsys-intro.
- [Steffen Rendle](entities/SteffenRendle.md) — Recommender-systems researcher; author of [[FactorizationMachines]] (Rendle 2010, *ICDM*) and [[BPR]] (Rendle et al. 2009, *UAI*) — two of the most cited papers in the field; [[google|Google Research]] at time of writing.
- [Xiangnan He](entities/XiangnanHe.md) — Recommender-systems researcher; first author of [[NeuMF]] / [[NeuralCollaborativeFiltering]] (He, Liao, Zhang, Nie, Hu, Chua 2017, *WWW*); NUS → USTC.
- [GroupLens](entities/GroupLens.md) — University of Minnesota research lab; maintains the [[MovieLens]] dataset family and live web service since 1997.
- [MovieLens](entities/MovieLens.md) — Canonical academic recommender-systems benchmark dataset (943 users × 1682 movies × 100K ratings in the 100K version); the running benchmark across all 8 sub-chapters of [[d2l-recommender-systems]].
- [Netflix Prize](entities/NetflixPrize.md) — \$1M open competition (2006–2009) to improve Netflix's Cinematch RMSE by 10%; won by BellKor's Pragmatic Chaos with an ensemble in which [[MatrixFactorization]] was the load-bearing component; the historical event that put MF on the recommender-systems map.

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Introduction)
- [The Embedded Rust Book](entities/TheEmbeddedRustBook.md) — introductory book on using [[RustLanguage|Rust]] for [[BareMetalProgramming|bare-metal]] [[EmbeddedSystems|embedded systems]]; coordinated by the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup]]'s resources team.
- [Rust (Programming Language)](entities/RustLanguage.md) — systems programming language with memory safety + zero-cost abstractions; runs in embedded contexts via `#![no_std]` + LLVM backend.
- [Rust Embedded Working Group](entities/RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup.md) — official Rust community WG owning the embedded ecosystem; maintains the [[EmbeddedRustBookshelf]] including [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]].
- [STMicroelectronics](entities/STMicroelectronics.md) — semiconductor vendor; producer of the STM32 [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] MCU family and [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] dev board.
- [STM32F3DISCOVERY](entities/STM32F3DISCOVERY.md) — [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M4]] dev board from [[STMicroelectronics]]; reference hardware for every example in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]].

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-hardware]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Hardware)
- [STM32F303VCT6](entities/STM32F303VCT6.md) — application MCU on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]]; [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M4F]] at 72 MHz, 256 KiB [[FlashMemory|Flash]] / 48 KiB [[SRAM]], 3.3 V signaling; integrated [[GPIO]] / [[I2C]] / [[SPI]] / [[USART]] / timers.
- [STM32F103](entities/STM32F103.md) — [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M3]] MCU family from [[STMicroelectronics]]; on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] it implements the on-board [[STLink|ST-LINK]] debugger over the "USB ST-LINK" port.
- [LSM303DLHC](entities/LSM303DLHC.md) — [[STMicroelectronics]] system-in-package combining a 3-axis [[Accelerometer]] + 3-axis [[Magnetometer]] over [[I2C]]; mounted on the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]].
- [L3GD20](entities/L3GD20.md) — [[STMicroelectronics]] 3-axis MEMS [[Gyroscope]] over [[SPI]]; with [[LSM303DLHC]] completes the F3 board's 9-axis [[IMU]].
- [ST-LINK](entities/STLink.md) — [[STMicroelectronics]]'s in-circuit programmer/debugger protocol; the [[STM32F3DISCOVERY]] integrates an ST-LINK via a dedicated [[STM32F103]] so the board is self-programmable over USB.

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-intro-tooling]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Tooling)
- [Cargo](entities/Cargo.md) — [[RustLanguage|Rust]]'s build system / package manager; carries the subcommand interface [[CargoBinutils]] and [[CargoGenerate]] extend; drives [[CrossCompilation]] via `--target=<triple>`.
- [rustc](entities/Rustc.md) — Rust compiler; LLVM-backed multi-target codegen — *the* reason [[CargoBinutils]] tools cover every architecture Rust does.
- [rustup](entities/Rustup.md) — Rust toolchain installer; `rustup target add <triple>` is the operational bridge to [[CrossCompilation]] and `rustup component add llvm-tools` installs the LLVM tools [[CargoBinutils]] wraps.
- [cargo-binutils](entities/CargoBinutils.md) — Cargo subcommand wrapping LLVM `objdump` / `nm` / `size`; one-command cross-OS install; universal architecture coverage via shared LLVM backend with [[Rustc]].
- [cargo-generate](entities/CargoGenerate.md) — Cargo subcommand for creating projects from templates; the book's escape hatch for [[NoStd|`no_std`]] linker-script + memory-layout boilerplate.
- [QEMU](entities/QEMU.md) — full-system ARM emulator (`qemu-system-arm`); the book's no-hardware escape hatch — run embedded examples on the host without an [[STM32F3DISCOVERY|F3 board]].
- [OpenOCD](entities/OpenOCD.md) — open-source [[OnChipDebugging|on-chip-debug]] server; bridges [[GDB]] ↔ probe ([[STLink]] / [[JLink]] / [[MCULink]] / [[RustyProbe]]) over [[JTAG]] / [[SWD]]. Established standard; the alternative to [[ProbeRs]].
- [GDB](entities/GDB.md) — GNU Debugger; canonical CLI front-end for embedded-Rust debugging, drives [[OpenOCD]] / [[ProbeRs]] over Remote Serial Protocol.
- [Probe-rs](entities/ProbeRs.md) — modern, Rust-native alternative to [[OpenOCD]]; simpler config; ships its own [[ProbeRsVSCodeExtension|VS Code extension]].
- [Probe-rs VS Code Extension](entities/ProbeRsVSCodeExtension.md) — IDE debugger UI on [[ProbeRs]] (Rust pretty printing, error messages); VS Code counterpart to [[GDB]] CLI.
- [TRACE32](entities/TRACE32.md) — [[Lauterbach]]'s professional multi-arch debugger; ARM + RISC-V; ELF/DWARF-based so works with conventional Rust binaries without custom support.
- [Lauterbach](entities/Lauterbach.md) — German embedded-tools vendor; developer of [[TRACE32]].
- [Rusty-probe](entities/RustyProbe.md) — open-source USB debug probe designed for [[ProbeRs]].
- [J-Link](entities/JLink.md) — [[Segger]]'s debug probe family; ARM + RISC-V; unlimited flash breakpoints.
- [SEGGER Microcontroller](entities/Segger.md) — German embedded-tools vendor; developer of [[JLink]].
- [MCU-Link](entities/MCULink.md) — [[NXP]]'s budget-friendly debug probe; pairs with MCUXpresso IDE; targets ARM Cortex.
- [NXP Semiconductors](entities/NXP.md) — Dutch semiconductor vendor; producer of [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] MCUs and the [[MCULink]] probe.

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]] (The Embedded Rust Book — QEMU)
- [LM3S6965](entities/LM3S6965.md) — TI / Luminary Micro [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M3]] [[Microcontroller|MCU]]; the book's first code-example target *because* [[QEMU]] can emulate it (`qemu-system-arm -machine lm3s6965evb`). 256 KiB [[FlashMemory|Flash]] / 64 KiB [[SRAM]]; [[RustTarget|target triple]] `thumbv7m-none-eabi`.
- [cortex-m-rt](entities/CortexMRTCrate.md) — minimal startup / runtime crate for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]; supplies the reset handler / [[VectorTable|vector table]] / `.bss` / `.data` init that [[NoStd|`no_std`]] strips out, plus the `#[entry]` macro for marking `fn main() -> !`. The structural replacement for [[RustRuntime|`libstd`'s pre-`main` runtime]].
- [panic-halt](entities/PanicHaltCrate.md) — minimal `#[panic_handler]` provider that loops forever; the book's default panic crate before the deferred *Panicking* chapter ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).
- [cortex-m-semihosting](entities/CortexMSemihostingCrate.md) — Rust crate exposing [[ARMSemihosting|ARM semihosting]] (`hprintln!`, `debug::exit`) on [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]; the host-IO path the book's `hello` example uses under [[GDB]] + [[QEMU]].
- [defmt](entities/Defmt.md) — deferred-formatting logging framework from [[Knurling]] / [[FerrousSystems|Ferrous Systems]]; default in the chapter's `hello` example with `defmt-rtt` (real hardware) / `defmt-semihosting` (QEMU) transports.
- [Ferrous Systems](entities/FerrousSystems.md) — Berlin Rust consultancy; steward of [[Knurling]] and the [[Defmt|`defmt`]] / [[QemuRun|`qemu-run`]] / `probe-rs` / `app-template` stack the chapter pulls in.
- [Knurling](entities/Knurling.md) — Ferrous Systems' embedded-Rust tooling project (`github.com/knurling-rs`); umbrella for [[Defmt]] / [[QemuRun]] / `app-template` and a modern alternative to the [[CortexMQuickstartTemplate|`cortex-m-quickstart`]] flow.
- [qemu-run](entities/QemuRun.md) — Knurling's [[Defmt|`defmt`]]-aware [[QEMU]] launcher; the chapter's host-side decoder for `defmt-semihosting` output ([[rust-embedded-book-start-qemu]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Memory-mapped Registers)
- [cortex-m](entities/CortexMCrate.md) — canonical [[MicroArchitectureCrate|micro-architecture crate]] for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]]; exposes interrupt enable/disable + the core-standardized [[SysTick]] peripheral via `Peripherals::take()`. The entry layer of the chapter's first code sample ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [svd2rust](entities/Svd2Rust.md) — [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup|Rust Embedded WG]] code generator consuming a vendor's [[SVDFile|CMSIS-SVD XML]] and emitting a fully typed [[PeripheralAccessCrate|PAC]] crate with the closure-based `read()` / `write()` / `modify()` register API; the **mechanism** behind the ecosystem's uniform PAC ergonomics ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [embedded-hal](entities/EmbeddedHalCrate.md) — [[Portability|portability]] trait crate (`digital::OutputPin`, `serial::Read/Write`, `i2c::I2c`, `spi::SpiBus`, `delay::DelayNs`, …) that every [[HALCrate|HAL crate]] implements; lets driver / application code be written once and compiled against any chip's HAL ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).
- [tm4c123x](entities/Tm4c123xCrate.md) — the chapter's worked [[PeripheralAccessCrate|PAC]] example for TI's Tiva-C TM4C123 ([[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M4]] / 80 MHz / 256 KiB Flash); auto-generated by [[Svd2Rust|`svd2rust`]] from the chip's [[SVDFile|SVD]] ([[rust-embedded-book-start-registers]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-semihosting]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Semihosting)
- [panic-semihosting](entities/PanicSemihostingCrate.md) — Rust `#[panic_handler]` provider that logs the panic message to the host's stderr via [[ARMSemihosting|ARM semihosting]] ([[CortexMSemihostingCrate|`cortex-m-semihosting`]] under the hood); with the optional `"exit"` Cargo feature, additionally invokes `debug::exit(EXIT_FAILURE)` after logging — the chapter's recipe for [[NoStd|`no_std`]] run-pass tests on [[QEMU]] (panic → host stderr → `$? = 1`). **Never use `"exit"` on real hardware** — `debug::exit` corrupts the [[OpenOCD]] session ([[rust-embedded-book-start-semihosting]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Panicking)
- [panic-abort](entities/PanicAbortCrate.md) — minimal Rust [[PanicHandlerAttribute|`#[panic_handler]`]] crate that executes the target's abort instruction (Cortex-M `UDF`); the chapter's recommended **release-profile** panic handler in the profile-conditional swap pattern (smallest binary size, no panic message preserved) ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).
- [panic-itm](entities/PanicItmCrate.md) — Rust [[PanicHandlerAttribute|`#[panic_handler]`]] crate that streams the panic message via the [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] **ITM** (Instrumentation Trace Macrocell) trace peripheral over SWO — the hardware-fast alternative to [[PanicSemihostingCrate|`panic-semihosting`]] when SWO + a compatible probe ([[STLink]], [[JLink]]) are available ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).
- [panic-probe](entities/PanicProbeCrate.md) — [[Knurling]] / [[FerrousSystems]] `#[panic_handler]` crate that formats the panic via [[Defmt|`defmt`]] over RTT and then hard-faults to break the debugger; modern alternative to the four crates the chapter explicitly lists, pointed at via *crates.io/keywords/panic-handler* ([[rust-embedded-book-start-panicking]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Concurrency)
- [RTIC](entities/RTIC.md) — **Real-Time Interrupt-driven Concurrency** framework for embedded Rust; static-priority scheduling + compile-time `static mut` resource tracking, deadlock-free by construction, `async` executor included. Named as the first higher-level alternative to manual `Mutex<RefCell<Option<T>>>` ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [Embassy](entities/Embassy.md) — `async`/`await`-based embedded Rust framework; battery-included (`embassy-executor`, `embassy-time`, vendor HALs, `embassy-sync`). Named as the second higher-level alternative ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).
- [bare-metal (crate)](entities/BareMetalCrate.md) — architecture-agnostic Rust concurrency primitives (`CriticalSection` token, `Mutex<T>`) re-exported by [[CortexMCrate|`cortex-m`]] and other arch crates; maintained by the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup]] ([[rust-embedded-book-concurrency-index]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Collections)
- [alloc (crate)](entities/AllocCrate.md) — Standard-distribution Rust crate providing heap-backed collection implementations (`Box`, `Vec`, `String`, `BTreeMap`, …); opt-in path back to dynamic collections under [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]]. Activation contract: `#[global_allocator]` static implementing [[GlobalAlloc|`GlobalAlloc`]] **plus** an [[AllocErrorHandlerAttribute|`#[alloc_error_handler]`]] for [[OutOfMemory|OOM]] ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [heapless (crate)](entities/HeaplessCrate.md) — Fixed-capacity, stack-allocated Rust collections (`Vec<_, U8>` etc.) with no global-allocator dependency; capacity in the type signature via [[Typenum|`typenum`]] (v0.4.x), every insertion returns `Result`, `push` is constant-time. **OOM impossible** if used exclusively. The canonical [[AllocCrate|`alloc`]] alternative for embedded ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [typenum (crate)](entities/Typenum.md) — Type-level numerics for Rust — unsigned/signed ints + arithmetic encoded entirely in the type system. Pre-`const-generics` mechanism that [[HeaplessCrate|`heapless`]] (v0.4.x) uses to encode each collection's capacity directly in its type ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).
- [alloc-cortex-m (crate)](entities/AllocCortexMCrate.md) — Production-grade [[GlobalAllocator|global allocator]] for [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] firmware (wraps `linked_list_allocator`); the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup]]-maintained alternative the chapter recommends over its illustrative [[BumpPointerAllocator|bump-pointer allocator]]; first forward-referenced from [[rust-embedded-book-intro-no-std]] ([[rust-embedded-book-collections-index]]).

- [Andrew Zisserman](entities/AndrewZisserman.md) — Senior author of [[VGG]] (2014); head of [[oxforduniversity|Oxford]] Visual Geometry Group; *Multiple View Geometry* textbook author — anchor of the pre-deep-learning CV tradition ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Christian Szegedy](entities/ChristianSzegedy.md) — First author of [[GoogLeNet]] / [[Inception]] (2014); co-author with [[SergeyIoffe|Ioffe]] of [[BatchNormalization]] (2015) ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Sergey Ioffe](entities/SergeyIoffe.md) — First author of [[BatchNormalization]] (Ioffe & Szegedy 2015); [[google|Google]] researcher; co-author of [[Inception]]-v3 / v4 ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).
- [Kaiming He](entities/KaimingHe.md) — First author of [[ResNet]] (2015), [[HeInitialization]] (2015), Mask R-CNN (2017), MoCo (2020); MSRA → [[fair|FAIR]] → MIT ([[d2l-convolutional-modern]]).

- [Kuldip Paliwal](entities/KuldipPaliwal.md) — Australian signal-processing researcher; co-author with [[MikeSchuster|Schuster]] of the [[BidirectionalRNN|bidirectional RNN]] paper (1997) ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).
- [Kishore Papineni](entities/KishorePapineni.md) — First author of [[BLEU]] (Papineni, Roukos, Ward & Zhu 2002) — the dominant MT evaluation metric ([[d2l-recurrent-modern]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]] (The Embedded Rust Book — A little C with your Rust)
- [bindgen](entities/Bindgen.md) — `rust-lang/rust-bindgen`; auto-generates [[ReprC|`#[repr(C)]`]] struct definitions and [[ExternC|`extern "C"`]] function blocks from C/C++ headers. For [[NoStd|`no_std`]] embedded use, set `--ctypes-prefix=cty` (so emitted code references the [`cty`] crate's primitives) and `--use-core` (so emitted code references `core::` paths instead of `std::`); the resulting `bindings.rs` is the matching Rust side for whatever C archive the [[CcCrate|`cc` crate]] / `make` / `CMake` produces. Typically invoked from a [[BuildRs|`build.rs`]] over a single `bindings.h` that `#include`s the C header set. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]]).
- [cc crate](entities/CcCrate.md) — `alexcrichton/cc-rs`; idiomatic-Rust wrapper around the host's C/C++ compiler invoked from a [[BuildRs|`build.rs`]] (`cc::Build::new().file("src/foo.c").compile("foo")`) — produces a `libfoo.a` static archive in `target/` that Cargo's final link step pulls into the embedded binary. The **simple-case branch** of the C-build decision tree in [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]] (vs. shelling out to `make` / `CMake` via `std::process::Command` for complex projects, vs. linking a pre-distributed `.a` directly). Dispatches on `$CC_<target>` so cross-compiling a `thumbv7m-none-eabi` package drives `arm-none-eabi-gcc` automatically. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-c-with-rust]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]] (The Embedded Rust Book — A little Rust with your C)
- [cbindgen](entities/Cbindgen.md) — `eqrion/cbindgen`; the **inverse-direction** codegen tool — scans Rust source for `#[no_mangle] pub extern "C" fn` ([[NoMangle]] + [[ExternC]]) and `#[repr(C)]` ([[ReprC]]) items, emits matching C `.h` / `.hpp` declarations (`void rust_function();`, `typedef struct CoolStruct { ... }`). Symmetric counterpart to [[Bindgen|`bindgen`]] — `bindgen` translates C → Rust, `cbindgen` translates Rust → C; a project doing both directions uses both. Typically invoked from a [[BuildRs|`build.rs`]] so the generated header is regenerated whenever the Rust source changes. The C-side consumer `#include`s the generated header and links the Cargo-produced [[CrateType|`cdylib`]] (`lib<name>.so`) or [[CrateType|`staticlib`]] (`lib<name>.a`) at link time. ([[rust-embedded-book-interoperability-rust-with-c]]).

### Added with [[rust-embedded-book-unsorted-math]] (The Embedded Rust Book — Performing Math Functionality)
- [libm](entities/LibmCrate.md) — `rust-lang/libm` ([crates.io/crates/libm](https://crates.io/crates/libm)); **pure-Rust port of C's `libm`** — the standard math library. Re-exposes `<math.h>` operations (`sqrt`, `sin`, `cos`, `exp`, `log`, `pow`, `floor`, …) as Rust **free functions** callable from any [[NoStd|`#![no_std]`]] crate with no [[GlobalAllocator|global allocator]] or [[RustRuntime|runtime]] dependency. The gap-filler the math chapter recommends because [[RustCoreLibrary|`core`]] exposes `f32` / `f64` but **not** their transcendental / rounding methods (those live only in [[RustStandardLibrary|`std`]] as inherent methods on the primitive types). API shape — `use libm::{exp, floorf, sin, sqrtf};` then `sqrtf(x)` replaces `x.sqrt()`. Precision follows C convention: `f`-suffixed = `f32` (`sqrtf`, `floorf`), no-suffix = `f64` (`sin`, `exp`); the math chapter's example uses `.into()` to widen `f32` to `f64` when calling the `f64` variants. Maintained by the [[RustEmbeddedWorkingGroup|Rust Embedded WG]]. ([[rust-embedded-book-unsorted-math]]).

Bumped to 1099 with [[dspy-language-models]] (+1: [[DSPyLM]] — DSPy's universal LM-client abstraction; the concrete operationalization of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model's]] *"swap the LM"* portability claim into a two-line code change; thin facade over [[LiteLLM]] adding default-on caching + `rollout_id` cache-busting + `lm.history` telemetry + `model_type="responses"` opt-in; spans managed / self-hosted-GPU / local-laptop deployment regimes behind the same API). Bumped to 1114 with [[dspy-modules]] (+7: [[DSPyModules]] (the swappable-strategy abstraction over a stable [[DSPySignatures|Signature]]; resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by every prior DSPy ingest), [[DSPyPredict]] (the minimal primitive Module — *"all other DSPy modules are built using `dspy.Predict`"*), [[DSPyProgramOfThought]] (output-code-then-execute strategy), [[DSPyMultiChainComparison]] (N-CoT + LM comparison), [[DSPyRecursiveLanguageModel]] (`dspy.RLM` — sandboxed Python REPL + recursive sub-LLM calls for over-context cases), [[DSPyMajority]] (function-style vote aggregator; zero LM cost), [[DSPyPrediction]] (the typed return-object every Module call produces; carries `get_lm_usage()` cost-accounting telemetry from DSPy 2.6.16+); [[ChainOfThought]] and [[react|ReAct]] **extended in-place** with *DSPy implementation* sections rather than duplicated as `DSPyChainOfThought` / `DSPyReAct`). Bumped to 1118 with [[dspy-mcp]] (+2: [[ModelContextProtocol]] (the framework-agnostic [[anthropic|Anthropic]]-authored open protocol for connecting LMs to external tools via standalone servers; two reference transports stdio + streamable-HTTP; four-step session lifecycle; async end-to-end; **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by every prior DSPy ingest) and [[DSPyMCP]] (the DSPy-specific binding — single class-method `dspy.Tool.from_mcp_tool(session, tool)` converts MCP tool descriptors into [[DSPyTools|`dspy.Tool`]] instances composing through every existing DSPy pathway; three operational constraints — `.acall(...)` required, agent inside `async with` block, toolset fixed per session); [[DSPyTools]] **extended in-place** with a *Tool origin is decoupled from tool consumption* section noting `dspy.Tool` gains a second construction path; [[anthropic|Anthropic]] entity page **updated in-place** with MCP-authorship attribution — a third wiki role alongside frontier-model and managed-API-provider; the split between protocol-level [[ModelContextProtocol]] and framework-binding [[DSPyMCP]] mirrors the [[LiteLLM]] / [[DSPyLM]] precedent). Bumped to 1116 with [[dspy-tools]] (+1: [[DSPyTools]] — DSPy's `dspy.Tool` wrapper for Python functions plus the `dspy.ToolCalls` model-output type; the fifth DSPy-special type after `dspy.Image` / `dspy.History` / `dspy.Prediction` / signature-input types; the substrate the tool-using Modules ([[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] above all) compose against; the **two-equal-status-approaches** duality (managed via [[react|`dspy.ReAct`]] vs manual via [[DSPyPredict|`dspy.Predict`]] over a `tools: list[dspy.Tool]` input + `dspy.ToolCalls` output Signature); per-[[DSPyAdapters|Adapter]] native-function-calling kwarg with automatic text-parse fallback (the second model-capability scoping in the Learn corpus); async tools first-class via `tool.acall(...)` + `dspy.context(allow_tool_async_sync_conversion=True)`; resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by every prior DSPy ingest; [[react|ReAct]] **extended in-place** with the *managed-vs-manual* duality section rather than duplicated as `DSPyReAct`). Bumped to 1119 with [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] (+1: [[DSPyEvaluation]] — the canonical anchor for DSPy's evaluation philosophy and the middle stage of the [[dspy-learn-index|three-stage Programming → Evaluation → Optimization]] workflow; operationalizes the stage as a **four-step iterative loop** (collect 20–200-example dev set → define DSPy metric → run development evaluations → recursively optimize the metric when it is a DSPy program); commits the framework to three load-bearing positions — *small dev sets are sufficient*, *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* (DSPy's structural answer to the intermediate-supervision problem in chain-of-thought training), *the metric is itself iterative*; names the two-regime metric story — scalar `accuracy` for simple tasks vs *"smaller DSPy program that checks multiple properties of the output"* for long-form tasks (DSPy's structural operationalization of [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]]); records the **recursive-self-improvement** claim — when the metric is a DSPy program, optimizing the metric itself becomes easy because the metric's output is bounded and scalar; sits between [[DSPyProgrammingModel]] (Programming stage) and [[DSPyOptimizers]] (Optimization stage); specializes the general [[ModelEvaluation]] concept; operates in the [[OfflineEvaluation]] regime; forward references [[DSPyData]] (page 10) and [[DSPyMetrics]] (page 11) — both owned by sibling ingests). Bumped to 1121 with [[dspy-data]] (+2: [[DSPyExample]] — DSPy's **data-side primitive** for the [[dspy-evaluation-overview|Evaluation-stage]] dev set; a typed Python dict-with-utilities with arbitrary field names, dot-notation field access, `with_inputs("field", ...)` input-tagging (non-mutating, returns new `Example` whose `input_keys` set tags the named fields), and `inputs()` / `labels()` non-destructive partition accessors; [[DSPyPrediction|`dspy.Prediction`]] is a **subclass** of `Example`, which makes the [[DSPyMetrics|metric]]'s `(example, prediction) -> score` contract type-symmetric — both arguments share the same dot-access / partition surface — *"Your DSPy modules will return values of the type `Prediction`, which is a special sub-class of `Example`."* — and [[DSPyData]] — DSPy's **dataset-layer discipline** for the train / dev / test three-set convention DSPy inherits from supervised ML (*"DSPy is a machine learning framework, so working in it involves training sets, development sets, and test sets"*); records the three load-bearing commitments — *datasets are plain Python lists* of [[DSPyExample|`dspy.Example`]] (no `Dataset` class, no `train_test_split(...)` helper, no built-in loaders — splits are Python slicing; the small-API discipline consistent with [[dspy-modules|*"DSPy is just Python code"*]]), *input/label tagging is attached not structural* (the same `Example` can be re-tagged for different program calls), *inputs-only sufficiency* (*"You can use DSPy effectively without any intermediate or final labels, but you will need at least a few example inputs"* — the data-side mirror of [[dspy-evaluation-overview|the Evaluation Overview's]] *intermediate-step labels are almost never needed* commitment); the canonical conversion idiom from external data is `[dspy.Example(**row).with_inputs("field") for row in source]`; **resolves both long-standing forward references** [[DSPyData]] + [[DSPyExample]] carried by [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[dspy-evaluation-overview]] since the Evaluation stage opened on page 9). Bumped to 1124 with [[dspy-metrics]] (+2: [[DSPyMetrics]] — DSPy's **canonical metric contract** `(example, pred, trace=None) -> score`; *"A DSPy metric is just a function in Python that takes `example` (e.g., from your training or dev set) and the output `pred` from your DSPy program, and outputs a `float` (or `int` or `bool`) score"*; **type-symmetric on the data side** (because [[DSPyPrediction|`Prediction`]] is a subclass of [[DSPyExample|`Example`]]) and **regime-asymmetric on the calling side** (the optional third argument `trace` switches behavior between evaluation/optimization (`trace is None`, continuous `float` return) and bootstrapping (`trace is not None`, strict `bool` return for demo selection) — the dual-purpose mechanism that makes a single function serve both DSPy compilation phases); two regimes — *simple metrics* (one-line scalar comparisons, built-ins `dspy.evaluate.metrics.answer_exact_match` / `answer_passage_match`) for short-form tasks and *AI-feedback metrics* (a `class Assess(dspy.Signature)` rubric template + N `dspy.Predict(Assess)` invocations) for long-form tasks — DSPy's structural operationalization of [[llmasjudge|LLM-as-judge]]; the canonical hybrid pattern mixes AI judgments with deterministic hard gates (`len(tweet) <= 280` alongside two `Predict(Assess)` outputs) — first wiki demonstration that DSPy metrics are not all-or-nothing AI-feedback; the `trace`-aware `validate_hops` bootstrap recipe inspects intermediate predictor outputs; recursive-metric-optimization (Step 4 of the four-step loop) is operationalized — the AI-feedback metric is itself a DSPy program and thus optimizable by an [[DSPyOptimizers|Optimizer]]; **resolves the long-standing forward reference** carried by every prior DSPy ingest since the corpus opened — and [[DSPyEvaluate]] — DSPy's **dev-set-evaluation utility** `from dspy.evaluate import Evaluate`; a thread-parallel wrapper around the raw `for x in devset: pred = program(**x.inputs()); score = metric(x, pred)` loop with four kwargs (`devset` / `num_threads` / `display_progress` / `display_table`); the reusable two-phase pattern (construct once with the dev set; call multiple times with `(program, metric)` pairs); the harness for Step 3 of the four-step Evaluation loop). Bumped to 1125 with [[dspy-optimization-overview]] (+1: [[DSPyOptimization]] — DSPy's **third-stage workflow concept** that turns a runnable, measurable program into an optimized one with a higher metric than the baseline; canonical anchor for the **three-input / one-output contract** *program + metric + training-set → optimized program*; the **30/300 training-set-size regime** (*"You can often get substantial value out of 30 examples, but aim for at least 300 examples"* — explicitly larger than [[DSPyEvaluation|the Evaluation stage's]] 20–200 dev set); the **inverted 20/80 train/validation split** for most prompt optimizers (DSPy-specific defense against the prompt-optimization-overfits-small-training-sets failure mode); the **[[GEPA]] carve-out** (only named optimizer on the page, follows standard ML practice instead); the **four iteration axes** (data / program structure / metric / optimizer-choice) — three of four point back into prior stages, making Optimization an *open-under-revision* stage rather than a black-box terminus; sits as the **fourth artifact** of [[DSPyProgrammingModel|the Programming Model]] (Signature / Adapter / Module / Optimizer) at the workflow level; the split between [[DSPyOptimization]] (workflow / this page) and [[DSPyOptimizers]] (catalog / page 13, forward reference) mirrors the [[DSPyEvaluation]] / [[DSPyMetrics]] precedent — one page anchors the workflow, the sibling anchors the per-algorithm machinery; carries [[DSPyOptimizers]] / [[BootstrapFewShot]] / [[BootstrapFewShotWithRandomSearch]] / [[MIPROv2]] / [[BootstrapFinetune]] / [[GEPA]] / [[DSPyAssertions]] as forward references the page-13 sibling ingest will resolve). -->

- [A/B Testing](concepts/ABTesting.md) — controlled live experiment comparing two variants on a target metric.
- [ADC (Analog-to-Digital Converter)](concepts/ADC.md) — MCU peripheral that samples a continuously-variable input voltage to an integer. [[ATmega328P]] has a 10-bit successive-approximation ADC, 6 channels, ~15 kSPS, with `ADCSRA` / `ADMUX` / `ADCH:ADCL` registers ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 25–26).
- [ALU (Arithmetic Logic Unit)](concepts/ALU.md) — CPU sub-unit performing arithmetic and bitwise ops on register operands; on the [[AVR]], outputs feed the [[StatusRegister]] flag bits ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [ATmega 328P](concepts/ATmega328P.md) — 8-bit [[AVR]] microcontroller from [[Atmel]] on the [[ArduinoUno|Arduino Uno]]: 32 k Flash / 2 k SRAM / 1 k EEPROM, [[HarvardArchitecture|Harvard]] [[RISC]], 26 interrupt vectors, three [[GPIO]] ports (B/C/D), six 10-bit [[ADC]] channels, three [[TimerCounter|timer/counters]], six [[PulseWidthModulation|PWM]] outputs ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]]).
- [AVR](concepts/AVR.md) — [[Atmel]]'s family of 8-bit [[RISC]] [[HarvardArchitecture|Harvard]] microcontrollers; substrate of nearly every classic [[Arduino]] board. Distinguished by 32 GPRs and most-instructions-in-one-cycle ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [Arduino (platform)](concepts/Arduino.md) — Open-source MCU dev platform built around [[ATmega328P|AVR]] / [[ARMCortexM|Cortex-M]] boards plus an IDE and the Wiring library (`setup`/`loop`/`pinMode`/`digitalWrite`/`analogRead`/`analogWrite`/`delay`/`map`). The pedagogical default in [[embedded-controllers-fiore]] chs. 15–29.
- [Arduino Uno](concepts/ArduinoUno.md) — Reference [[Arduino]] board built around the [[ATmega328P]]: 16 MHz, three GPIO ports, six 10-bit [[ADC]] channels, three [[TimerCounter|timers]], six [[PulseWidthModulation|PWM]] pins, 40 mA per pin / 200 mA chip-wide.
- [Abduction](concepts/Abduction.md) — Inference to the best explanation; the philosophical framing of [[ModelSelection]] across model classes ([[mml-book]] §8.2 marginal).
- [Abstraction](concepts/Abstraction.md) — Simplified, stable interface hiding implementation details. The [[OperatingSystem|OS]]'s core product per [[dis-0-introduction]]; the lens through which [[DiveIntoSystems]] frames *"writing efficient code"* — abstractions are necessary for productivity, performance comes from knowing which physical details they hide.
- [Activation Function](concepts/ActivationFunction.md) — nonlinearity that lets neural networks learn non-linear mappings.
- [AddressSanitizer (ASan)](concepts/AddressSanitizer.md) — Compile-time-instrumented memory-error detector (`-fsanitize=address`); modern alternative to [[Valgrind]] / [[Memcheck]] with ~2× slowdown (vs Memcheck's ~10–50×), full [[StackSection|stack]] + [[DataSection|globals]] coverage via red zones, but requires recompilation and **does not** catch [[UninitializedReadError|uninitialized reads]] (MemorySanitizer's job). Not covered by [[dis-3-3-valgrind|DIS Ch 3.3]] but the canonical CI tool every C codebase in 2026 runs alongside Memcheck.
- [Adam](concepts/Adam.md) — adaptive-moment optimizer, default for most deep-learning training.
- [Adapter Layers](concepts/adapterlayers.md) — Parameter-efficient fine-tuning via small bottleneck blocks inserted into Transformer FFN sub-layers; ablated against full fine-tuning in T5.
- [Adversarial Ensemble](concepts/adversarialensemble.md) — 
- [Agentic AI](concepts/AgenticAI.md) — DAG-composed system of specialized learnable agents (Liao et al. Def. 4.1); exponentially superior sample/parameter efficiency vs monolithic learners under the [[StructuredRealWorldDistribution]]; generalizes [[MixtureOfExperts]] in scope, topology and routing.
- [Agentic Algorithm Discovery](concepts/AgenticAlgorithmDiscovery.md) — LLM-driven program search (FunSearch → EoH → AlphaEvolve → Meta-Harness → AutoTTS). Explorer LLM proposes/refines code-defined algorithms; sandbox returns scalar scores + execution traces; iterate. Execution-trace feedback beats scalar feedback; constrained search spaces (e.g. [[BetaParameterization]]) improve generalization.
- [Agentic Harness](concepts/agenticharness.md) — 
- [Agentic Reinforcement Learning](concepts/agenticreinforcementlearning.md) — 
- [Agentic Sovereignty](concepts/AgenticSovereignty.md) — Probability $\mathcal{S}\in[0,1]$ that a propagator LLM keeps its internal derivation independent of swarm consensus. Governed by the [[SovereigntyDecayLaw]]; 0.5-crossing defines $D_L$. From [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]].
- [Alignment Hallucination](concepts/AlignmentHallucination.md) — Failure mode where the model derives correctly internally then sycophantically externalizes a falsehood; operationalized as [[SovereigntyGap]] $G_\mathcal{S}\gg 0$. Existence proof of CoT/output divergence under social pressure.
- [AlphaZero](concepts/alphazero.md) — 
- [Anyscale Jobs](concepts/AnyscaleJobs.md) — managed batch Ray job primitive on Anyscale.
- [Anyscale Services](concepts/AnyscaleServices.md) — managed online Ray Serve deployments with autoscaling and canaries.
- [Anyscale Workspaces](concepts/AnyscaleWorkspaces.md) — interactive Ray dev environment mirroring production.
- [Argparse](concepts/Argparse.md) — Python standard-library CLI builder.
- [Arrange-Act-Assert](concepts/ArrangeActAssert.md) — three-step pattern for structuring unit tests.
- [Apriori Algorithm](concepts/AprioriAlgorithm.md) — Breadth-first frequent-itemset search with monotone support-based pruning; inner loops embarrassingly parallel ([[parproc-ch14-statistics-data-mining]] §14.1.3–14.1.4).
- [ASHA](concepts/ASHA.md) — async successive-halving scheduler for hyperparameter search.
- [Additive Attention](concepts/AdditiveAttention.md) — [[BahdanauAttention|Bahdanau]]-style attention scoring function $\mathbf{w}_v^\top\tanh(\mathbf{W}_q\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{W}_k\mathbf{k})$; one-hidden-layer MLP on the query–key concatenation; used when $\mathbf{q}$ and $\mathbf{k}$ have different dimensions ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Attention](concepts/Attention.md) — mechanism for dynamically weighting input parts when producing each output.
- [Attention Is All You Need (Concept)](concepts/AttentionIsAllYouNeed.md) — 2017 paper introducing the transformer architecture.
- [Attention Mask](concepts/AttentionMask.md) — mask zeroing disallowed token interactions (padding, causal).
- [Attention Pooling](concepts/AttentionPooling.md) — The softmax-weighted sum $\sum_i\alpha(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{k}_i)\mathbf{v}_i$ that is the aggregation step of every attention mechanism; differentiable generalization of a database lookup ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Attention Scoring Functions](concepts/AttentionScoringFunctions.md) — The pre-softmax compatibility $a(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{k})$ — dot-product $\mathbf{q}^\top\mathbf{k}/\sqrt{d}$ (modern default) vs additive $\mathbf{w}_v^\top\tanh(\mathbf{W}_q\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{W}_k\mathbf{k})$ (Bahdanau) ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Bahdanau Attention](concepts/BahdanauAttention.md) — Bahdanau, Cho & Bengio 2014 differentiable alignment for [[MachineTranslation|MT]]: per-step context $\mathbf{c}_{t'}=\sum_t\alpha(\mathbf{s}_{t'-1},\mathbf{h}_t)\mathbf{h}_t$; structural fix for the fixed-vector bottleneck of [[1409.3215-seq2seq]] and direct ancestor of [[SelfAttention]] ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Autoencoder](concepts/Autoencoder.md) — network that reconstructs its input through a bottleneck.
- [Autograd](concepts/Autograd.md) — automatic-differentiation engines powering backpropagation.
- [Autoregressive Model](concepts/AutoregressiveModel.md) — Sequence model that regresses a signal on its own past, $P(x_t\mid x_{<t})$; underlies $n$-gram, RNN, and Transformer LMs ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Autoresearch](concepts/autoresearch.md) — 
- [Autoscaling](concepts/Autoscaling.md) — automatic adjustment of compute capacity to load.
- [Average Pooling](concepts/AveragePooling.md) — [[Pooling]] operator returning the mean of each window; LeNet-era default, now mostly superseded by [[MaxPooling]] except as global average pooling at network end ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [AutoTTS](concepts/AutoTTS.md) — Environment-driven framework ([[2605.08083-autotts]]) that **automates [[testtimescaling|test-time scaling]] strategy design** by treating it as controller synthesis over a [[WidthDepthSearch|width–depth]] control space. Three pillars: [[OfflineReplayEnvironment]], [[BetaParameterization]], [[ExecutionTraceFeedback]]. Discovers the [[ConfidenceMomentumController|CMC]] in 5 rounds / $39.9 / 160 min.
- [Average Trap](concepts/AverageTrap.md) — Irreducible quadratic penalty $\epsilon = \sum_k \tfrac{\alpha_k}{2}\|\theta^*_{\text{mono}}-\theta^*_k\|^2_{H_k}$ a monolithic learner pays from conflicting per-task gradients (Liao et al. Prop. 3.3); the "Generalist's Penalty."
- [AWS IAM](concepts/AWSIAM.md) — AWS identity and access management policy system.
- [BPTT](concepts/BPTT.md) — Backpropagation Through Time (Werbos 1990); unroll the RNN and apply chain rule with weight-tied gradients summed across time; exposes vanishing/exploding gradients via $(\mathbf{W}_\textrm{hh}^\top)^k$ powers ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Bitwise Operations](concepts/BitwiseOperations.md) — `& | ^ ~ << >>` — the operator family that makes register-poking possible; pervasive in embedded C, rare in desktop code. Idioms: `x |= (1<<n)` set, `x &= ~(1<<n)` clear, `x ^= (1<<n)` toggle ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 4).
- [Backpropagation](concepts/Backpropagation.md) — chain-rule algorithm for computing neural-network gradients.
- [Bandwidth](concepts/Bandwidth.md) — Bits per unit time a [[CommunicationBottleneck|communication]] channel can carry; orthogonal-and-independent companion to [[Latency]]; raised via bus width (shared-memory) / parallel network paths (clusters) / link speed ([[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.5).
- [Bank Conflict](concepts/BankConflict.md) — Hardware serialization penalty when multiple processors (or [[GPU]] warp lanes) simultaneously access the *same* memory bank; the [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism|Ch3]] §3.2.2 worked example (16 threads × 1 M elements × 4 low-order banks all hit bank 0) and its stride-1 fix; stride/bank theorem `gcd(s,b)=1`; mitigations include padding and [[MemoryInterleaving|interleaving discipline]] choice.
- [Barrier (synchronization)](concepts/Barrier.md) — "A point in the code that all threads must reach before continuing"; Pthreads `pthread_barrier_wait`, OpenMP `#pragma omp barrier`, Rdsm `barr()` ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]); correct two-counter implementation and parallel [[TreeBarrier|tree]] / [[ButterflyBarrier|butterfly]] schemes delivered in [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism|Ch3]] §3.12.
- [Butterfly Barrier](concepts/ButterflyBarrier.md) — Parallel [[Barrier]] in which each node bit-flip-handshakes with $\log_2 n$ partners over $\log_2 n$ phases (`i ⊕ 2^k`); *"a butterfly exchange amounts to a number of simultaneously tree operations"* ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.12.4.2.2).
- [Batch Inference](concepts/BatchInference.md) — offline bulk-prediction workload optimized for throughput.
- [Batch Normalization](concepts/BatchNormalization.md) — per-batch activation normalization that stabilizes deep training.
- [Bayesian Linear Regression](concepts/BayesianLinearRegression.md) — Full-Bayesian counterpart of MLE [[LinearRegression]]; closed-form Gaussian posterior under Gaussian prior + Gaussian likelihood ([[mml-book]] §9.3). Calibrated predictive uncertainty + marginal-likelihood model selection.
- [Bayesian Optimization](concepts/BayesianOptimization.md) — surrogate-model-based hyperparameter search.
- [Beam Search](concepts/beamsearch.md) — 
- [Behavioral Testing](concepts/BehavioralTesting.md) — capability-grouped input/output tests for ML models.
- [Bell-La Padula](concepts/belllapadula.md) — 
- [BERT](concepts/bert.md) — 
- [Binary Representation](concepts/BinaryRepresentation.md) — Encoding of integers, floats, characters, and instructions as bit patterns inside [[ComputerHardware|hardware]]; previewed in [[dis-0-introduction]] as a prerequisite for explaining C arithmetic, overflow, signed/unsigned semantics, and floating-point precision.
- [Best-of-N](concepts/bestofn.md) — Generate $N$ candidates, pick one. Width-only degenerate case of the [[WidthDepthSearch|width–depth control space]]; [[selfconsistency|Self-Consistency]] = BoN + majority vote.
- [Beta Parameterization](concepts/BetaParameterization.md) — Search-tractability discipline from [[2605.08083-autotts|AutoTTS]]: every candidate TTS controller exposes only a single scalar $\beta\in[0,1]$ mapped monotonically to all internal hyperparameters. Ablation: removing it cuts held-out accuracy 53.1→49.0 (search overfits to extreme pruning thresholds).
- [Biconditional Correctness](concepts/biconditionalcorrectness.md) — 
- [Black](concepts/Black.md) — opinionated Python code formatter.
- [Black-Box Shift Detection](concepts/BlackBoxShiftDetection.md) — detecting drift from model outputs alone.
- [BLEU](concepts/bleu.md) — 
- [Blocksworld](concepts/Blocksworld.md) — Canonical classical-planning domain; PlanBench shows LLMs solve 11–59% zero-shot and 0–4% on the obfuscated *Mystery BW* variant — the smoking-gun retrieval-not-planning result.
- [Breakpoint](concepts/Breakpoint.md) — Debugger marker that pauses the debuggee at a chosen source line / function / address — [[GDB]]'s primary control primitive. Four set-forms (`break 42` / `break file.c:42` / `break func` / `break *0x4011a0`); program reaches it via [[GdbRun|`run`]], state is inspected with [[GdbPrint|`print`]] / [[GdbBacktrace|`bt`]], execution resumes with [[StepDebug|`next` / `step` / `cont`]]. Software implementation overwrites the target byte with an `int3` trap; hardware breakpoints use limited CPU debug registers. Conditional form (`break 42 if x > 100`) skips irrelevant iterations ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Bystander Effect (in Multi-Agent Reasoning)](concepts/BystanderEffect.md) — Architectural failure mode where simulated peer consensus (static prompt content, no live dialogue) triggers a propagator LLM to discard its own correct derivation. [[gpt54|GPT-5.4]] SWE-bench collapses 1.00→0.23 at $n=2$.
- [Cauchy-Schwarz Inequality](concepts/CauchySchwarzInequality.md) — $|\langle\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}\rangle|\leq\|\mathbf{x}\|\|\mathbf{y}\|$ ([[mml-book]] §3.3); the inequality that lets inner products define angles and induces the triangle inequality for the induced norm.
- [C4](concepts/c4.md) — 745 GB heuristically-filtered Common Crawl corpus released with T5; the canonical large diverse web-text pre-training data set.
- [Calculus](concepts/Calculus.md) — Minimum-viable calculus for deep learning: derivatives → partials → gradients → Jacobian/Hessian → chain rule → Taylor expansion. Engine behind every parameter update. [[d2l-preliminaries]] §Calculus.
- [Canary Deployment](concepts/CanaryDeployment.md) — gradual traffic shift to a new model version.
- [Cargo Features](concepts/CargoFeatures.md) — [[Cargo]]'s named-boolean opt-in/opt-out compilation toggles — Rust's `#[cfg(feature="X")]`-gated replacement for embedded-C `#ifdef`; declared per crate in `Cargo.toml`, **additive across the dependency tree** (any enabling consumer turns the feature on for everyone, so a feature must never break the API of crates that don't ask for it) ([[rust-embedded-book-c-tips-index]]).
- [Capability Gate](concepts/capabilitygate.md) — 
- [Capability vs Alignment](concepts/CapabilityVsAlignment.md) — distinction between what a model can do and what it does.
- [Chain-of-Thought](concepts/chainofthought.md) — 
- [Character-Level Language Model](concepts/CharacterLevelLanguageModel.md) — LM that operates over character tokens (~30 vocab on *The Time Machine*); D2L's pedagogical RNN-LM example ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [CheckList](concepts/CheckList.md) — behavioral NLP testing methodology.
- [Checkpoint](concepts/Checkpoint.md) — serialized snapshot of model and optimizer state.
- [Chi-Squared Test](concepts/ChiSquaredTest.md) — categorical goodness-of-fit / independence test.
- [Cholesky Decomposition](concepts/CholeskyDecomposition.md) — $\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{L}\mathbf{L}^\top$ for symmetric positive-definite $\mathbf{A}$ ([[mml-book]] §4.3); the "square root of a matrix." Underlies multivariate-Gaussian sampling and fast SPD linear solves.
- [CI/CD](concepts/CICD.md) — automated integration and deployment pipelines.
- [CISC](concepts/CISC.md) — Complex Instruction Set Computing; multi-cycle instructions, fewer registers; opposite of [[RISC]]. Modern x86 is internally RISC wrapped in a CISC ISA ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [Cross-Compiler](concepts/CrossCompiler.md) — compiler that runs on one architecture (host) and emits machine code for another (target). The canonical embedded toolchain shape — you cannot natively develop on a 2 k-SRAM MCU. `avr-gcc` for AVR, `arm-none-eabi-gcc` for Cortex-M ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 15).
- [Class (OOP)](concepts/Class.md) — blueprint bundling data and behavior in object-oriented code.
- [Class Imbalance](concepts/ClassImbalance.md) — classification setting with dramatically uneven label frequencies.
- [CLI](concepts/CLI.md) — text-based interface for invoking programs with commands and flags.
- [Cluster (parallel computing)](concepts/Cluster.md) — Networked commodity machines used as a parallel processing system; [[Beowulf]] is the canonical recipe ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [CNN](concepts/CNN.md) — Convolutional neural network — *the* vision-architecture family, derived from imposing [[TranslationInvariance]] + [[Locality]] on an MLP. Stacks [[ConvolutionalLayer|conv layers]] + nonlinearities + [[Pooling]]; ancestor [[LeNet]] (1989) through [[AlexNet]] / [[ResNet]] / [[VisionTransformer|ViT]] ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Code Organization](concepts/CodeOrganization.md) — structuring projects into modules and layers.
- [Code Style](concepts/CodeStyle.md) — conventions for formatting and structuring source code.
- [Cilk](concepts/Cilk.md) — Parallel C-extension language whose defining contribution is a [[WorkStealing|work-stealing]] runtime (`cilk_spawn` / `cilk_sync`); the named exemplar in [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.4.4 ("the elegant Cilk language").
- [Co-adaptation](concepts/Coadaptation.md) — Phenomenon where hidden units rely on specific upstream activation patterns; [[Dropout]]'s target ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Cognitive Loafing](concepts/CognitiveLoafing.md) — LLM analogue of *social loafing* (Ringelmann 1913): integrative effort $E_{int}$ falls below task entropy $\mathcal{H}_\tau$ under swarm pressure. The $\mathcal{B}=1$ failure state in [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]].
- [Cache Coherency](concepts/CacheCoherency.md) — Hardware protocol layer ensuring multi-cache consistency for shared memory lines; snoopy invalidate vs update on a bus (analogous to write-back vs write-through in uniprocessor caches), directory-based protocols off-bus, [[MESI]] as the Pentium exemplar ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.5). Distinct from [[MemoryConsistency]] — coherency answers *"do caches agree?"*, consistency answers *"when does a new value become visible?"*.
- [Cache Memory](concepts/CacheMemory.md) — Small, fast on-chip section of the CPU storing copies of recently accessed RAM; organized in blocks; accesses are either cache hits (fast) or cache misses (full block fetched from RAM, possibly evicting another block). Hit rates typically exceed 90% due to [[LocalityOfReference]]. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.2.1)
- [Cache Level (L1 / L2 / L3)](concepts/CacheLevel.md) — The three-tier stratification of [[CacheMemory|cache]] inside a modern processor — *"L1 (very small and fast, near the [[ALU]]), L2 (larger and slower), and L3 (shared among multicore CPUs)"* ([[dis-11-1-memory-hierarchy]]). L1/L2 per-core; **L3 shared across all cores of a [[MulticoreProcessor|multicore CPU]]** — the natural cross-core data-exchange tier and the [[CacheCoherency|coherence]] / [[FalseSharing|false-sharing]] contention point.
- [Kernel](concepts/Kernel.md) — Privileged core of the [[OperatingSystem|OS]] — runs in [[KernelMode|kernel mode]], discovers hardware, launches [[Process|processes]], and handles [[Interrupt|interrupts]] + [[SystemCall|system-call]] traps. Mapped into the top of every process's address space for cheap [[ContextSwitch|context switching]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [Kernel Mode](concepts/KernelMode.md) — Privileged [[CPU]] execution mode that runs the [[Kernel|OS kernel]]; unrestricted instructions + full memory + direct hardware access. Entered via trap ([[SystemCall]]) or hardware [[Interrupt]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [User Mode](concepts/UserMode.md) — Unprivileged [[CPU]] execution mode for application code; restricted instruction set, OS-authorized memory regions only, no direct hardware access. Escapes to [[KernelMode|kernel mode]] only via [[SystemCall|trap]] or [[Interrupt|interrupt]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [System Call](concepts/SystemCall.md) — Controlled [[UserMode|user]] → [[KernelMode|kernel]] gateway: user program loads syscall number into a designated [[CpuRegister|register]] and issues a **trap instruction**; CPU switches privilege and dispatches to the OS handler. *"the location varies according to the ISA"* ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [Process State](concepts/ProcessState.md) — The four-state [[Process|process]] life cycle from [[dis-13-2-processes|DIS Ch 13.2]]: **Ready** (could run) / **Running** (on CPU) / **Blocked** (waiting on event) / **Exited** ([[Zombie|zombie]] pending [[Wait|`wait`]] reap). [[Scheduler|Scheduler]] only picks from Ready.
- [Process Control Block (PCB)](concepts/ProcessControlBlock.md) — Per-[[Process|process]] kernel data structure ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]): [[ProcessID|PID]] + address-space info + saved [[CpuRegister|register]] snapshot + open-file list + current [[ProcessState|state]]; the destination of [[ContextSwitch|context-switch]] register saves.
- [`exec` (POSIX)](concepts/Exec.md) — POSIX [[SystemCall|syscall]] family (`execvp` / `execve` / ...) that **overlays the calling [[Process|process]]'s image** with a new program; preserves [[ProcessID|PID]], reinitializes everything else. Paired with [[Fork|`fork`]] as the canonical Unix process-spawn pattern. *Never returns on success* — only on failure ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [`wait` / `waitpid` (POSIX)](concepts/Wait.md) — POSIX [[SystemCall|syscall]] that **reaps a terminated child** ([[Zombie|zombie]]) — collects [[ExitStatus|exit status]] and frees the [[ProcessControlBlock|PCB]]; blocks the parent in [[ProcessState|Blocked]] state until [[Signal|`SIGCHLD`]] arrives. Foreground vs background shell commands differ only in whether `wait` is called synchronously or in a signal handler ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Scheduler](concepts/Scheduler.md) — [[Kernel|OS kernel]] component that picks **which [[ProcessState|Ready]] [[Process|process]] runs next and for how long** — the **policy** half of the OS's process-execution stack, paired with [[ContextSwitch|context switch]] as the **mechanism** ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Process Scheduling](concepts/ProcessScheduling.md) — The **policy** of choosing the next [[ProcessState|Ready]] [[Process|process]] and its [[Timesharing|quantum]]; separable from the [[ContextSwitch|context-switch]] mechanism. [[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]] defers specific policies (round-robin, priority, CFS) to a dedicated OS textbook.
- [Multiprogramming](concepts/Multiprogramming.md) — OS-design discipline of **keeping multiple [[Process|processes]] resident** so the [[Scheduler|scheduler]] can switch to a [[ProcessState|Ready]] process whenever the current one blocks on I/O. Distinct from [[Timesharing]] (quantum-driven) but complementary ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Zombie Process](concepts/Zombie.md) — A [[Process|process]] that has called [[Exit|`exit`]] but whose [[ProcessControlBlock|PCB]] persists because the parent has not yet [[Wait|`wait`ed]]. Holds the [[ExitStatus|exit status]] until reaped; adopted by [[Init|`init`]] if the parent dies first ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [`init` Process (PID 1)](concepts/Init.md) — The first user-level [[Process|process]] created at [[Bootloader|boot]] — **root of the [[Process|process]] hierarchy** and adopter of orphans. Modern Linux PID 1 is typically systemd ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Wall Time](concepts/WallTime.md) — Total elapsed real-world duration of a [[Process|process]] — counts Running + [[ProcessState|Blocked]] + Ready. **Affected by concurrent processes** on a [[Multiprogramming|multiprogrammed]] system. The "what the user sees" clock ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [CPU Time](concepts/CPUTime.md) — Duration a [[Process|process]] **actually held a CPU** — counts only [[ProcessState|Running]]. **Unaffected by other processes** — the honest number for optimization work; can exceed wall time on multicore parallel programs ([[dis-13-2-processes|DIS 13.2]]).
- [Bootloader](concepts/Bootloader.md) — Small OS-bringup *boot block* that [[Firmware|firmware]] ([[BIOS]] / [[UEFI]]) loads from disk into RAM at power-up and jumps to, handing CPU control from firmware to the [[Kernel|kernel]] ([[dis-13-1-booting-running]]).
- [Cachegrind](concepts/Cachegrind.md) — [[Valgrind]] suite's [[CacheMemory|cache]]-simulation tool — `valgrind --tool=cachegrind --cache-sim=yes ./prog` simulates L1 + LL hit/miss counts and `cg_annotate` decodes per-source-line attribution. Headline benchmark: row-major vs column-major matrix-sum → **62,688 vs 1,062,996 D1 misses** (~17× delta) producing **4.61× runtime gap** at zero algorithmic-complexity change ([[dis-11-5-cachegrind]]). Deterministic simulator (not HW sampler); ~20–100× slowdown.
- [Cache Line](concepts/CacheLine.md) — Unit of storage inside a [[CacheMemory|CPU cache]] — a fixed-size chunk (typically **16–64 bytes**) of consecutive bytes copied between [[RAM]] and cache atomically. Bundles a **data block** with **metadata** (valid bit, tag, optional dirty bit). The granularity at which hardware exploits [[SpatialLocality|spatial locality]] ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Cache Hit](concepts/CacheHit.md) — Request satisfied from [[CacheMemory|cache]] without stalling for [[RAM|main memory]]; ~1 ns vs ~100 ns miss penalty — the central performance lever of the [[MemoryHierarchy|memory hierarchy]]. Hit rates >90 % routine on programs with good [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Cache Miss](concepts/CacheMiss.md) — Requested address not in [[CacheMemory|cache]]; CPU stalls for [[RAM|main memory]] then installs the fetched block. **3C taxonomy**: **compulsory** (first access, unavoidable) / **capacity** ([[WorkingSet|working set]] > cache) / **conflict** (placement-restriction-induced — the class [[SetAssociativeCache|set-associative]] caches attack) ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Cache Replacement Policy](concepts/CacheReplacementPolicy.md) — Rule selecting which [[CacheLine|line]] to evict on a [[CacheMiss|miss]] into a full set. [[LeastRecentlyUsed|LRU]] is canonical (leverages [[TemporalLocality|temporal locality]]); FIFO / Random are simpler alternatives. Irrelevant for [[DirectMappedCache|direct-mapped]] (no choice) ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Least Recently Used (LRU)](concepts/LeastRecentlyUsed.md) — Canonical [[CacheReplacementPolicy|cache replacement policy]]; evicts the line whose last access is furthest in the past. Justified by [[TemporalLocality|temporal locality]] — *"recently used data is likely to be used again"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]). Pseudo-LRU (binary-tree, NRU) approximations dominate high-associativity hardware.
- [Direct-Mapped Cache](concepts/DirectMappedCache.md) — Simplest [[CacheMemory|cache]] placement architecture — each memory address maps to **exactly one** [[CacheLine|cache line]] via the index bits. Cheapest lookup hardware; highest **conflict-miss rate**. Survives in embedded / microcontroller caches and some branch-prediction structures ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Set Associative Cache](concepts/SetAssociativeCache.md) — Modern dominant [[CacheMemory|cache]] placement — each address maps to a set of **N lines** (typically 2–8); all N tags compared in parallel; [[LeastRecentlyUsed|LRU]] selects eviction. *"Offers a good compromise between complexity and conflicts"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]). Used by L1 / L2 / L3 in all modern CPUs.
- [Fully Associative Cache](concepts/FullyAssociativeCache.md) — Maximum-flexibility [[CacheMemory|cache]] placement — any address can occupy any [[CacheLine|line]]; lookup compares every tag in parallel. Zero conflict misses but lookup cost scales with cache size → *"generally unfit for a general-purpose CPU cache"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]). Persists in [[TLB|TLBs]] / victim caches / micro-op caches.
- [Write-Back Cache](concepts/WriteBackCache.md) — Modern dominant **write policy** — writes update [[CacheMemory|cache]] only, mark the line **dirty**, propagate to [[RAM|main memory]] only on eviction. *"Amortizing the cost of a memory access across many writes significantly improves performance"* ([[dis-11-4-caching]]); complicates [[CacheCoherency|coherence]].
- [Write-Through Cache](concepts/WriteThroughCache.md) — Simpler **write policy** — every write updates [[CacheMemory|cache]] AND [[RAM|main memory]] simultaneously. No dirty bit; natural [[CacheCoherency|coherence]]; bandwidth-hungry. Dominated by [[WriteBackCache|write-back]] for CPU caches; persists in some GPU / embedded caches ([[dis-11-4-caching]]).
- [Hard Disk Drive (HDD)](concepts/HardDisk.md) — Mechanical magnetic-platter-based [[NonVolatileMemory|non-volatile]] secondary storage; **5–10 ms latency** (seek + rotational + transfer), 0.5–10 TB capacity, lowest cost-per-byte; rotating platters at 5,000–15,000 RPM divided into tracks + sectors ([[dis-11-2-storage-devices]]); ~10⁵× slower than [[DRAM]] because mechanical motion gates access; biases code toward sequential / block-oriented patterns ([[LocalityOfReference]] matters even at the disk tier).
- [Solid-State Drive (SSD)](concepts/SolidStateDrive.md) — [[FlashMemory|Flash-memory]]-based [[NonVolatileMemory|non-volatile]] secondary storage with **no moving parts**; 0.1–1 ms latency, 0.5–2 TB capacity, moderate cost-per-byte; ~10–100× faster than [[HardDisk|HDDs]] (eliminates seek + rotational latency), still ~10³–10⁴× slower than [[DRAM]] ([[dis-11-2-storage-devices]]). **Naming disambiguation**: not to be confused with [[SSD|SSD (Single-Shot MultiBox Detector)]] — the object-detection model — which lives at `concepts/SSD.md`.
- [Non-Volatile Memory](concepts/NonVolatileMemory.md) — The volatility-axis category for storage technologies that **retain contents when power is removed**; the non-volatile floor of the [[MemoryHierarchy|memory hierarchy]] holds the program binary, [[OperatingSystem|OS kernel]], and user data across reboots; members in the wiki — [[FlashMemory]] / [[SolidStateDrive]] / [[HardDisk]] (magnetic tape / optical / network-remote named only); persistence ≠ reliability — each technology has a distinct wear / failure model (HDD mechanical, [[FlashMemory|flash]] finite-write-endurance, tape/optical decade-scale decay) ([[dis-11-2-storage-devices]]).
- [Coherent Caches](concepts/CoherentCaches.md) — Cache-coherence protocol layer in [[SMP]]/multicore systems ensuring all processors see a consistent view of shared memory ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]); full treatment delivered in [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.5.
- [Context Switch](concepts/ContextSwitch.md) — OS operation triggered at each quantum boundary in [[Timesharing]]: saves all register values (PC, EFLAGS, etc.) of the outgoing process and restores those of the incoming process. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.1.1)
- [Crossbar Interconnect](concepts/Crossbar.md) — Non-blocking $n \times n$ switch grid wiring $n$ processors to $n$ memory modules; $n^2$ pathways guarantee $n$ simultaneous distinct-destination packets but cost $O(n^2)$. Sun Microsystems Enterprise 10000 used a 16×16 crossbar ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.3.3.1).
- [COGS](concepts/cogs.md) — 
- [Compare-Exchange](concepts/CompareExchange.md) — Two-node pool-and-split primitive: nodes combine data, lower-ID keeps lower half, higher-ID keeps upper half; foundational operation in [[BitonicMergesort]], [[Hyperquicksort]], and [[OddEvenTransposition]] ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.2.4).
- [Communication Bottleneck](concepts/CommunicationBottleneck.md) — *"Whether you are on a shared-memory, message-passing or other platform, communication is always a potential bottleneck"* — the [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.1 opener; covers bus / [[CoherentCaches|cache-coherency]] traffic in shared-memory, network packets in clusters, and CPU↔GPU + on-device contention in [[GPU|GPUs]]; trades off against [[LoadBalancing]].
- [Complementary Learning Systems](concepts/complementarylearningsystems.md) — 
- [Composite Social Load](concepts/CompositeSocialLoad.md) — $\mathcal{L}(\vec{a},p)=\sum_i w_i\,\alpha(a_i)\,\kappa(p,a_i)$: positional weight × base authority × kinship multiplier. Drives the [[SovereigntyDecayLaw]]; non-commutative via the [[LeadAnchorEffect]].
- [Compositional Capacity](concepts/CompositionalCapacity.md) — Topology Factor $C(\mathcal{G})=\sum_u \omega_u$ — sum of per-agent [[TopologicalWeight]]s — that governs the *error magnitude* of an Agentic AI DAG (Liao et al. Thm 4.3).
- [Compiler Optimization](concepts/CompilerOptimization.md) — Family of compiler program-transformation passes ([[GCC|`gcc`]] `-O0` / `-O1` / `-O2` / `-O3` / `-Os` / `-Oz` / `-Og` / `-Ofast`) that trade source-to-binary correspondence for speed / size — preserving observable behavior per the [[AsIfRule|as-if rule]]. The orthogonal axis to [[GccDashG|`-g`]] [[DebugSymbol|debug-info]]: at `-O2`+ the compiler reorders / inlines / eliminates / vectorizes instructions, breaking [[GDB|GDB]]'s line-to-instruction mapping and producing `<optimized out>` for register-resident variables. [[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]]'s rule: **debug at `-O0 -g`** (*"compiler-optimized code is often very difficult to debug because sequences of optimized machine code often do not clearly map back to C source code"*) ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Compute-Efficient Training](concepts/computeefficienttraining.md) — The fixed-compute training regime derived from scaling laws: very large models, modest data, stop short of convergence.
- [Computational Graph](concepts/ComputationalGraph.md) — DAG of tensor values + differentiable primitives that [[Autograd]] walks backward via the chain rule. Dynamic (PyTorch, MXNet) vs static (TF `tf.function`, JAX `jit`); supports Python control flow; activations cached for backward. [[d2l-preliminaries]] §Autograd.
- [Computer Hardware](concepts/ComputerHardware.md) — Physical components of a [[ComputerSystem|computer system]]: [[CPU]], [[RAM]], I/O ports, secondary storage; modern norm is [[MulticoreProcessor|multicore]] silicon often packaged as a [[SystemOnAChip|SoC]] ([[dis-0-introduction]]).
- [Computer System](concepts/ComputerSystem.md) — Per [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 0: [[ComputerHardware|hardware]] **plus** an [[OperatingSystem|OS]] delivering a general-purpose, reprogrammable environment. Restrictive definition that **excludes** calculators and bare [[Microcontroller|microcontrollers]] — the wiki's first formal definition of "computer system."
- [CPU Register](concepts/CpuRegister.md) — small, fixed-size storage **inside the [[CPU]]** holding operands / addresses / status flags for the executing instruction; fastest tier of the [[MemoryHierarchy|memory hierarchy]]. Inspected from [[GDB]] via `info registers` (whole file), [[GdbPrint|`print $rax`]] (one register, `$`-prefix disambiguates from C identifiers), [[GdbDisplay|`display $rax`]] (auto-print), [[GdbSet|`set $rax = 0`]] (write). x86-64 general-purpose set `%rax`/`%rbx`/`%rcx`/`%rdx`/`%rsi`/`%rdi`/`%rbp`/`%rsp` + special-purpose [[InstructionPointer|`%rip`]] / `%eflags`; [[IA32]] uses `%eax` / `%eip` ([[dis-3-5-gdb-assembly|DIS Ch 3.5]]).
- [Core File (Core Dump)](concepts/CoreFile.md) — OS-written disk snapshot of a process's memory + CPU registers at abnormal termination (typically [[SegmentationFault|`SIGSEGV`]] / `SIGBUS` / `SIGABRT`). Enables **post-mortem [[Debugger|debugging]]** — `gdb ./buggy core` overlays the executable's [[DebugSymbol|symbols]] onto the dump, exposing [[GdbBacktrace|`bt`]] / [[GdbPrint|`print`]] / `info registers` on the frozen state. Execution cannot resume. Default `RLIMIT_CORE=0` on most modern distributions; enable with `ulimit -c unlimited`. Captures heap / stack / .data / .bss / register set / [[CommandLineArguments|argv]]; not text segment (read-only, recovered from binary), not kernel-side I/O buffers ([[dis-3-1-gdb]]).
- [Concept Drift](concepts/ConceptDrift.md) — shift in the P(y|x) relationship over time.
- [Concept Shift](concepts/ConceptShift.md) — Subtype of [[DistributionShift|distribution shift]] where the **labeling function** $P(y\mid\mathbf x)$ itself drifts (soft-drink names by US region, DSM mental-illness criteria). Hardest shift type to correct principally; usual remedy is continual fine-tuning on fresh labels ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Covariate Shift](concepts/CovariateShift.md) — Subtype of [[DistributionShift|distribution shift]] where $P(\mathbf x)$ changes but $P(y\mid\mathbf x)$ does not (photos → cartoons of cats/dogs); correctable by importance-weighted [[EmpiricalRiskMinimization|ERM]] with $\beta_i = \exp(h(\mathbf x_i))$ estimated by a binary logistic-regression domain classifier ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
