- [Kernel Fusion](concepts/kernelfusion.md) — Combining a chain of ops into one CUDA kernel so intermediates stay in SRAM; the implementation discipline behind FlashAttention.
- [Kernel Density Estimation](concepts/KernelDensityEstimation.md) — Smooth nonparametric density estimator f̂(t) = (1/nh)Σk((t−Xᵢ)/h); Gaussian kernel standard; parallelized by distributing t-values or exploiting convolution structure for parallel FFT ([[parproc-ch14-statistics-data-mining]] §14.2.1).
- [`kill()` (POSIX Signal Sending)](concepts/Kill.md) — [[OperatingSystem|POSIX]] [[SystemCall|system call]] `int kill(pid_t pid, int sig)` that **sends a [[Signal|signal]] to a [[Process|process]]** (or group). Not primarily about termination — delivers any signal including `SIGUSR1` / `SIGCONT` / `0` (existence-check). `raise(sig)` is shorthand for `kill(getpid(), sig)`. Substrate for the [[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|Ch 3.4]] **self-pause idiom** `kill(getpid(), SIGSTOP)` that opens a [[GdbAttach|attach window]] for the debugger ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [Kernel Trick](concepts/KernelTrick.md) — Replace explicit feature map $\boldsymbol\phi$ with a kernel $k(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{x}')=\langle\boldsymbol\phi(\mathbf{x}),\boldsymbol\phi(\mathbf{x}')\rangle$ in any inner-product-only algorithm ([[mml-book]] §12.4). Lets SVM / ridge / PCA work in (possibly infinite-dim) feature spaces.
- [Knative](concepts/KNative.md) — Kubernetes-based serverless platform with scale-to-zero.
- [Kolmogorov-Smirnov Test](concepts/KolmogorovSmirnovTest.md) — nonparametric CDF-gap test for distribution drift.
- [Kubeflow](concepts/Kubeflow.md) — ML platform on Kubernetes for pipelines, tuning, and training.
- [Label Encoding](concepts/LabelEncoding.md) — mapping categorical labels or features to integer codes.
- [Label Shift](concepts/LabelShift.md) — Subtype of [[DistributionShift|distribution shift]] where $P(y)$ changes but $P(\mathbf x\mid y)$ does not (disease prevalence drifts, symptoms-per-disease do not). Correctable by inverting the validation-set confusion matrix: $\mathbf C\, p(\mathbf y) = \mu(\hat{\mathbf y})$, then weighted [[EmpiricalRiskMinimization|ERM]] with $\beta_i = p(y_i)/q(y_i)$ ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Language Model](concepts/LanguageModel.md) — Joint-probability estimator $P(x_1,\ldots,x_T)=\prod_t P(x_t\mid x_{<t})$ over token sequences; foundation of modern NLP. Pre-neural baselines ($n$-gram + smoothing) supplanted by RNN / Transformer LMs ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Laplace Smoothing](concepts/LaplaceSmoothing.md) — Add a small $\epsilon$ to count-based probability estimates so unseen $n$-grams get nonzero probability; insufficient at language-modeling scale due to [[ZipfsLaw]] ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Latency](concepts/Latency.md) — Time for one bit to travel from source to destination — CPU→memory in shared-memory, machine→machine in a cluster; one of the two independent dimensions of [[CommunicationBottleneck|communication]] cost (the other is [[Bandwidth]]); the bridge analogy: latency = time for one car to cross ([[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.5).
- [Latency Hiding](concepts/LatencyHiding.md) — Workaround when [[Latency|latency]] can't be reduced: do the long-latency operation in parallel with useful other work. [[GPU|GPUs]] hide DRAM latency by keeping many warps in flight; same idea applies to OoO CPUs, non-blocking MPI, software prefetch ([[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.5).
- [Lazy Initialization](concepts/LazyInitialization.md) — Framework feature deferring parameter allocation to first forward pass when input shape is known (`nn.LazyLinear`); eliminates `in_features` bookkeeping bugs ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Lagrange Multipliers](concepts/LagrangeMultipliers.md) — Standard technique for constrained optimization ([[mml-book]] §7.2); KKT conditions, dual problem, support-vector identification. Underlies [[SupportVectorMachine|SVM]] dual derivation and PCA's eigenvalue equation.
- [Lead Anchor Effect](concepts/LeadAnchorEffect.md) — Lemma 1 of [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]]: social load is sequence-dependent — $\mathcal{L}((a_x,a_y),p)\neq\mathcal{L}((a_y,a_x),p)$ — driven by positional weights $w_1\gg w_i$. Empirically: GPT-5.4 SWE-bench accuracy is 0.21 vs 0.31 for inverted auditor orderings.
- [Learning Rate](concepts/LearningRate.md) — scalar scaling gradient updates during optimization.
- [Learning Rate Scheduler](concepts/LearningRateScheduler.md) — policy varying the learning rate across training.
- [LIME](concepts/LIME.md) — local model-agnostic prediction explanations.
- [Linear Mapping](concepts/LinearMapping.md) — Function $\Phi:V\to W$ preserving vector-space structure ([[mml-book]] §2.7); matrices represent linear mappings in chosen bases; invariants (rank, [[Determinant]], [[Trace]], eigenvalues) are intrinsic to the mapping.
- [LeNet (LeNet-5)](concepts/LeNet.md) — [[YannLeCun|LeCun]] et al. 1989/1998 — first CNN trained with [[Backpropagation]] to match SVMs on real-world OCR ([[MNIST]]); deployed in ATM check-deposit machines; two conv→sigmoid→AvgPool blocks + three FC layers; the architectural ancestor of every modern [[CNN]].
- [Linear Independence](concepts/LinearIndependence.md) — Vectors $X_1,\ldots,X_k$ are linearly independent if the only solution to $\sum a_i X_i = 0$ is all $a_i = 0$; determines invertibility and rank ([[parproc-appB-matrix-algebra]] §B.3).
- [Linear Regression](concepts/LinearRegression.md) — linear model for continuous targets fit by least squares.
- [Load Balancing](concepts/LoadBalancing.md) — *"Arguably the most central performance issue"* per [[NormMatloff]]: keeping all processors busy. Two failure modes — task-time heterogeneity ([[Mandelbrot]]) and assignment skew (mutual outlinks). Headline result: [[StaticTaskAssignment|randomized static]] beats [[DynamicTaskAssignment|dynamic]] in the i.i.d. regime via the $O(1/\sqrt{m})$ chunk-time concentration argument ([[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.2, §2.4).
- [Locality (CNN Prior)](concepts/Locality.md) — Prior that nearby pixels are more informative than distant ones; combined with [[TranslationInvariance]] uniquely forces [[ConvolutionalLayer|convolutional layers]] out of fully-connected layers ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]] §why-conv).
- [Locality of Reference](concepts/LocalityOfReference.md) — Empirical access-pattern property explaining why [[CacheMemory|caches]] are effective: [[TemporalLocality|temporal locality]] (re-accessing the same item repeatedly) and [[SpatialLocality|spatial locality]] (accessing nearby items in quick succession) together keep cache hit rates above 90% for typical programs. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.2.3 + [[dis-11-3-locality]] DIS Ch 11.3)
- [Temporal Locality](concepts/TemporalLocality.md) — First axis of [[LocalityOfReference|locality]]; programs re-access the same item within a short time window. *"If a program has used a variable recently, it's likely to use that variable again soon"* ([[dis-11-3-locality|DIS Ch 11.3]]). Justifies caches, [[LeastRecentlyUsed|LRU]] replacement, and register allocation.
- [Spatial Locality](concepts/SpatialLocality.md) — Second axis of [[LocalityOfReference|locality]]; programs access items at *nearby* memory addresses. Exploited via [[CacheLine|cache-line]] block-granularity fetching. Headline empirical proof ([[dis-11-3-locality|DIS Ch 11.3]]): row-major `mat[i][j]` vs column-major `mat[j][i]` matrix-sum differ by **~5×** at zero algorithmic change.
- [Working Set](concepts/WorkingSet.md) — The subset of memory a program is *actively* referencing at a given time; the *size* property [[LocalityOfReference|locality]] keeps small. If working set fits in [[CacheMemory|cache]] → cache-speed execution; if it overflows → thrashing. Desk / bookshelf / library analogy from [[dis-11-3-locality|DIS Ch 11.3]].
- [LLM-as-Judge](concepts/llmasjudge.md) — 
- [LLM-Modulo Framework](concepts/LLMModuloFramework.md) — Generate-Test-Critique loop where LLM proposes candidate plans and a bank of external sound critics (e.g. VAL) supplies correctness; soundness inherited from hard critics, not the LLM.
- [LLM Fine-Tuning](concepts/LLMFineTuning.md) — specialization of pretrained LLMs via SFT, RLHF, or DPO.
- [LoCoMo](concepts/locomo.md) — Very-long-term conversational memory benchmark (Maharana et al. 2024); MSW δ-mem dominates across backbones.
- [Machine Learning](concepts/MachineLearning.md) — "The study of algorithms that can learn from experience" ([[d2l-introduction]]). Four core components: data / model / objective / optimizer. Four paradigms: [[SupervisedLearning|supervised]], [[UnsupervisedLearning|unsupervised]], [[SelfSupervisedLearning|self-supervised]], [[reinforcementlearning|RL]].
- [Markov Decision Process (MDP)](concepts/MarkovDecisionProcess.md) — Fully-observed special case of [[reinforcementlearning|RL]]; tuple $(\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},P,R)$ + policy. Sister cases: contextual bandit, [[MultiArmedBandits|multi-armed bandit]].
- [MapReduce](concepts/MapReduce.md) — Google/Hadoop distributed batch processing paradigm; map-then-reduce phases — cited as a [[ScatterGather]] instance ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [Market Basket Problem](concepts/MarketBasketProblem.md) — Canonical [[ItemsetAnalysis]] application: find retail transaction association rules I → J exceeding support and confidence thresholds ([[parproc-ch14-statistics-data-mining]] §14.1.2).
- [Logging](concepts/Logging.md) — structured emission of events and metrics for debugging.
- [Logistic Regression](concepts/LogisticRegression.md) — linear classifier with sigmoid/softmax output trained by cross-entropy.
- [LogSumExp](concepts/LogSumExp.md) — Numerical-stability transformation $\log\sum_k\exp(o_k) = \bar o + \log\sum_k\exp(o_k - \bar o)$ that lets [[Softmax|softmax]] and [[CrossEntropyLoss|cross-entropy]] be fused into one operator over logits. Every framework's `cross_entropy(logits, target)` uses this internally ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Long-Horizon Tasks](concepts/longhorizontasks.md) — 
- [Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM)](concepts/lstm.md) — 
- [Lost in the Middle](concepts/lostinthemiddle.md) — 
- [Low-Rank Attention Correction](concepts/lowrankattentioncorrection.md) — δ-mem's steering interface: static $\mathbf{W}^\Delta$ + dynamic state readout yield history-dependent attention deltas.
- [Machine Translation](concepts/machinetranslation.md) — 
- [Makefile](concepts/Makefile.md) — declarative project automation file.
- [Mandelbrot Set](concepts/Mandelbrot.md) — Iterative complex-plane fractal ($z \leftarrow z^2 + c$) — the recurring [[LoadBalancing|load-balance]] failure example in [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.2 / §2.4 (drawn from Darryl Gove's *Multicore Application Programming*); on an 8000×8000 grid randomized [[StaticTaskAssignment|static]] (15.7s) beats [[DynamicTaskAssignment|dynamic]] (21.4s) and naïve static (47.8s).
- [Mandelbrot Set (computation)](concepts/MandelbrotSet.md) — Computational pattern view of the Mandelbrot set as a per-pixel `z = z*z + c` loop with early termination; [[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.4 wraps it under `#ifdef STATIC|DYNAMIC|GUIDED|RC` switches to reproduce Ch2's [[ScheduleClause|schedule]] timing comparison.
- [MAP Estimation](concepts/MAPEstimation.md) — Maximum-a-posteriori point estimate ([[mml-book]] §8.3); MLE + log-prior. Equivalent to regularized MLE (Gaussian prior ⇔ ridge; Laplace prior ⇔ Lasso). Halfway-house between MLE and full Bayesian inference.
- [Map Batches](concepts/MapBatches.md) — Ray Data parallel batch transform.
- [Markdown](concepts/Markdown.md) — lightweight plain-text markup format.
- [Margin](concepts/Margin.md) — Distance from a [[SeparatingHyperplane]] to the nearest training point ([[mml-book]] §12.2). The [[SupportVectorMachine|SVM]]'s objective; VC-bound on generalization scales with $R^2/\gamma^2$.
- [Markov Model](concepts/MarkovModel.md) — Sequence model satisfying the [[MarkovCondition|Markov condition]]: future is conditionally independent of past given the recent history. $k$-th-order Markov ↔ $(k+1)$-gram LM; underpins discrete-sequence dynamic programming ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Matrix Decomposition](concepts/MatrixDecomposition.md) — Factoring a matrix into simpler / interpretable factors ([[mml-book]] Ch 4): determinant + trace + characteristic polynomial + [[Eigendecomposition]] + [[CholeskyDecomposition]] + [[SingularValueDecomposition]] as a unified taxonomy.
- [Matrix Inversion](concepts/MatrixInversion.md) — Computing $A^{-1}$ via direct methods or the power-series approach $(I-C)^{-1} = I + C + C^2 + \ldots$; the latter reduces to iterated [[MatrixMultiplication|matrix multiplication]] which parallelizes more effectively ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.4.3).
- [Matrix Multiplication](concepts/MatrixMultiplication.md)
- [Matrix Transpose](concepts/MatrixTranspose.md) — Exchanging rows and columns of a matrix; key identities: $(AB)' = B'A'$ and $\text{rk}(A') = \text{rk}(A)$; orthogonal matrices satisfy $U^{-1} = U'$ ([[parproc-appB-matrix-algebra]] §B.2).
- [Mergesort](concepts/MergeSort.md) — O(n log n) divide-and-conquer sort; parallelized via shared-memory thread-per-subtree or binary-tree message-passing (leaves sort, stream upward; non-leaves merge); [[BitonicMergesort]] is the sorting-network variant ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.2). — Parallel computation of $C = AB$: [[FoxAlgorithm|Fox's algorithm]] (MPI), `#pragma omp parallel for` outer loop ([[OpenMP]]), CUDA tiling with shared memory achieving 500× speedup, and R Snow/gputools interfaces ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.3).
- [Matrix-Vector Multiply](concepts/MatrixVectorMultiply.md) — Compute $Y=AX$ for matrix $A$ and vector $X$; the running task-assignment example in *Programming on Parallel Machines* — embarrassingly parallel under both meanings, used by [[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]] (R/[[Snow]] `clusterApply`) and [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.4 (Methods A / B / C / A' on 10000 rows × 10 threads).
- [Masked Language Model](concepts/maskedlanguagemodel.md) —
- [Masked Softmax](concepts/MaskedSoftmax.md) — Engineering primitive replacing masked-out positions with $-10^6$ before softmax to ignore them in attention; used for padding masks + causal/autoregressive masks ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]). 
- [Monte Carlo Simulation](concepts/MonteCarloSimulation.md) — Probabilistic estimation by repeated random simulation; embarrassingly parallel but requires independent RNG streams per thread (CURAND, RngStream, SPRNG, OpenMP Mersenne Twister) ([[parproc-ch14-statistics-data-mining]] §14.5).
- [Maximum Likelihood Estimation](concepts/MaximumLikelihoodEstimation.md) — Pick parameters maximizing the model's probability of the training data (Murphy §1.2.1.6); equivalently, minimize the NLL. Reduces to MSE for Gaussian regression and cross-entropy for softmax classification. The objective of *every* LLM pretrained via next-token prediction.
- [Maximum Mean Discrepancy](concepts/MaximumMeanDiscrepancy.md) — kernel-based distribution-comparison test.
- [Max-Pooling](concepts/MaxPooling.md) — [[Pooling]] operator returning the maximum of each window; preferred over [[AveragePooling]] for local translation invariance and sparse-signal preservation; Riesenhuber & Poggio 1999 origin ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Mean Squared Error](concepts/MeanSquaredError.md) — squared-error regression loss/metric.
- [Memcheck (Valgrind Tool)](concepts/Memcheck.md) — [[Valgrind]]'s **default tool** — the per-byte heap-state tracker that detects [[UninitializedReadError|uninitialized reads]], invalid pointer dereferences / out-of-bounds heap access, [[UseAfterFree|use-after-free]] (including [[DoubleFree|double-free]]), and [[MemoryLeak|memory leaks]]. Per-byte **A-bit** (addressable, toggled by [[Malloc|`malloc`]] / [[Free|`free`]]) and **V-bit** (valid/defined, toggled by writes); errors emit a three-part block (error / access stack / allocation context). Leak classes: *definitely / indirectly / possibly lost* + *still reachable*. ([[dis-3-3-valgrind]]).
- [Memory Allocation](concepts/MemoryAllocation.md) — `malloc()` / C++'s `new` are *"very expensive in time"* and large allocations cost cache misses + page faults; [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.7 recommends static arrays where possible and tuning per-call size otherwise — *"no magic solutions here."*
- [Memory Consistency Model](concepts/MemoryConsistency.md) — The *timing contract* of shared memory: when does a write become visible to other processors? **Sequential** (strongest, slowest) → **Release** (ACQUIRE/RELEASE) → **Scope** (release tied to specific locks; [[JIAJIA]] uses this). SPARC `MEMBAR`, x86 `MFENCE`. Distinct from [[CacheCoherency|coherency]] ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.6).
- [Memory Interleaving](concepts/MemoryInterleaving.md) — High-order (top bits select bank → consecutive words in same module, good for block partitioning) vs low-order (bottom bits → consecutive words in consecutive modules, good for stride-1 vector / [[GPU]] access). The two policies that trade off [[BankConflict|bank-conflict]] surface against block locality ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.2.1).
- [MESI Cache Coherency Protocol](concepts/MESI.md) — Pentium's invalidate-style [[CacheCoherency|coherency]] protocol; four states **M**odified / **E**xclusive / **S**hared / **I**nvalid per (cache, block) pair; full transition tables for reads / writes / read snoops / write snoops in [[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.5.2. Notable: write miss does NOT bring the block in from memory; write hit on Shared transitions to E plus broadcasts invalidate.
- [Mem GPT](concepts/memgpt.md) — 
- [MEMIT](concepts/memit.md) — 
- [MemoryAgentBench](concepts/memoryagentbench.md) — Memory-heavy LLM-agent benchmark (Hu et al. 2025); δ-mem's largest gain (1.31× over Qwen3-4B baseline).
- [Message-Passing Architecture](concepts/MessagePassingArchitecture.md) — Parallel hardware paradigm with independent CPUs + per-node memory communicating over a network; canonical pattern for [[Cluster]]/[[Beowulf]] computing ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [MIMD (Multiple Instruction Multiple Data)](concepts/MIMD.md) — Independent instruction streams across processors; standard model for shared-memory CPUs, contrasted with [[SIMD]] ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [MINJA](concepts/minja.md) — 
- [MIPROv2](concepts/MIPROv2.md) — DSPy's **reference [[DSPyOptimizers|optimizer]]** from [[dspy-optimizers]] (page 13 of 13). `dspy.MIPROv2` — the algorithm the page uses as its canonical example of *"how a non-trivial DSPy optimizer works"*. **MIPRO** = **M**ulti-prompt **I**nstruction **PR**oposal **O**ptimizer. **The only optimizer in the catalog that jointly tunes both instructions and demonstrations** in the same run; the only one that uses **[[BayesianOptimization|Bayesian Optimization]]** as its discrete-search procedure. Three-stage algorithm: (1) **bootstrapping stage** — run program on training inputs, collect traces, filter by metric; (2) **grounded proposal stage** — preview the program's *code*, *data*, and *traces* and draft candidate instructions per prompt (the **distinctive contribution** — DSPy's *"writing code instead of strings"* discipline pays off here, since the proposer inspects actual Python code, not just a string prompt); (3) **discrete search stage** — Bayesian Optimization surrogate model over (instructions, demos) combinations evaluated on mini-batches. The three-stage decomposition is the **structural template** for non-trivial DSPy optimizers. Compute budget knob: `auto="light"/"medium"/"heavy"`. **0-shot mode**: setting `max_bootstrapped_demos=0` + `max_labeled_demos=0` makes MIPROv2 tune only the instructions. Recommended for **200+ examples and 40+ trials** per the page's five-rule rubric. Two worked receipts on the page: **ReAct on HotPotQA (24% → 51%)** and **RAG with [[llmasjudge|`SemanticF1`]] metric on StackExchange (53% → 61%)**.
- [Miniconda](concepts/Miniconda.md) — Minimal [[VirtualEnvironment|conda]] installer; recommended Python/env baseline for [[d2l-installation|D2L]] — install Miniconda, `conda create --name d2l python=3.9`, activate, then `pip install` the chosen DL framework inside it.
- [Minibatch SGD](concepts/MinibatchSGD.md) — Practical compromise between batch [[GradientDescent]] and pure [[StochasticGradientDescent|SGD]]: sample a minibatch ($|\mathcal{B}|$ = 32–256), compute average gradient, step. The universal DL optimizer ([[d2l-linear-regression]] §3.1.4).
- [Mixture Model](concepts/MixtureModel.md) — Convex combination of $K$ base distributions ([[mml-book]] §11.1); the simplest latent-variable model. Modern MoE-LLMs are its supervised-routing generalization.
- [Mixture-of-Experts](concepts/MixtureOfExperts.md) — Routing-gated expert sub-networks (Shazeer 2017, Switch Transformer); reinterpreted in [[2605.12966-agentic-ai-to-agi]] as the single-layer routing instance of [[AgenticAI]] with bounded [[CompositionalCapacity]].
- [Multicore](concepts/Multicore.md) — Single-chip [[SMP]]; "effectively the same as SMP except that the processors are all on one chip" ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [MkDocs](concepts/MkDocs.md) — static site generator for Markdown docs.
- [Mkdocstrings](concepts/Mkdocstrings.md) — auto-renders Python docstrings in MkDocs.
- [ML Canvas](concepts/MLCanvas.md) — one-page ML project framing template.
- [MLOps](concepts/MLOps.md) — discipline of operationalizing ML systems.
- [Model Calibration](concepts/ModelCalibration.md) — match between predicted probabilities and reality.
- [Model Context Protocol (MCP)](concepts/ModelContextProtocol.md) — [[anthropic|Anthropic]]-originated, framework-agnostic **open standard** for connecting [[LanguageModel|language models]] to external tools, data sources, and contextual resources via standalone servers, introduced in [[dspy-mcp]] (DSPy *Learn* page 8 of 13). A program supporting MCP becomes a *client* to any conforming MCP *server* — the server exposes a typed catalog of **tools** (LM-invocable functions), **resources** (read-only URI-identified data), and **prompts** (parameterized templates) over a JSON-RPC-style wire protocol. Two reference transports: **stdio** (client spawns server as subprocess; communicates over stdin/stdout — local, no network exposure) and **streamable HTTP** (remote endpoint, bidirectional streaming). Four-step client lifecycle: open transport → `ClientSession(read, write)` + `await session.initialize()` → `await session.list_tools()` (and `list_resources()` / `list_prompts()`) → invoke via `session.call_tool(...)`. Sessions are stateful and async end-to-end. Load-bearing design property: **decoupling tool definition from tool consumption** — the same server serves [[DSPy]], [[ClaudeCode|Claude Code]], custom SDK clients, all without per-framework rewrapping. Has multiple independent client implementations (Python, TypeScript SDKs published openly). Resolves the long-standing forward reference carried by every prior DSPy ingest; DSPy's specific binding is [[DSPyMCP]].
- [Model Checkpoint](concepts/ModelCheckpoint.md) — serialized snapshot of model state.
- [Model Complexity](concepts/ModelComplexity.md) — expressive capacity of a model.
- [Model Composition](concepts/ModelComposition.md) — combining multiple models into a pipeline.
- [Model Evaluation](concepts/ModelEvaluation.md) — measuring model quality on held-out data.
- [Model Selection](concepts/ModelSelection.md) — Choosing among competing model classes / hyperparameters ([[mml-book]] §8.6); standard tools are held-out validation, $k$-fold / nested CV, and Bayesian marginal likelihood. Framed as [[Abduction]], not induction.
- [Model Monitoring](concepts/ModelMonitoring.md) — tracking deployed model behavior.
- [Module](concepts/Module.md) — Base class for models in the [[d2l-linear-regression|D2L]] OO scaffold; provides `forward`, `loss`, `training_step`, `configure_optimizers`. Inspired by [[PyTorchLightning|Lightning]]'s `LightningModule`.
- [Model Registry](concepts/ModelRegistry.md) — versioned store of trained model artifacts.
- [Model Serving](concepts/ModelServing.md) — exposing a model behind an inference API.
- [Modern Data Stack](concepts/ModernDataStack.md) — cloud-native data and analytics stack.
- [Monitoring](concepts/Monitoring.md) — production health-signal tracking.
- [Multi-Agent Systems](concepts/multiagentsystems.md) — 
- [Multi-Armed Bandits](concepts/MultiArmedBandits.md) — online explore/exploit decision algorithms.
- [Multi-Challenge](concepts/multichallenge.md) — Deshpande et al. ACL 2025 multi-turn conversation benchmark; in [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]] used as the low-entropy semantic background — anchors the Fortified Mind baseline and surfaces the IGNORED-disengagement failure mode.
- [Multicore Processor](concepts/MulticoreProcessor.md) — [[CPU]] with multiple independent execution cores on a single die; the default form of contemporary CPU silicon across desktops, [[SingleBoardComputer|SBCs]], and smartphones ([[dis-0-introduction]]). Makes [[ParallelComputing|parallel programming]] a baseline systems-literacy skill rather than a specialty.
- [Multi-Head Attention](concepts/multiheadattention.md) — 
- [Multi-Query Attention](concepts/multiqueryattention.md) — 
- [Multilayer Perceptron](concepts/MultilayerPerceptron.md) — feedforward fully-connected neural network.
- [Murphy Decomposition](concepts/murphydecomposition.md) — 
- [Nadaraya–Watson Kernel Regression](concepts/NadarayaWatson.md) — Nadaraya 1964 / Watson 1964 non-parametric estimator $f(\mathbf{q})=\sum_i y_i \alpha(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{x}_i)/\sum_j\alpha(\mathbf{q},\mathbf{x}_j)$; the half-century precursor of modern [[AttentionPooling|attention pooling]] ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [N-gram](concepts/NGram.md) — Contiguous sequence of $n$ tokens; $n$-gram language models approximate $P(x_t\mid x_{<t})$ by truncating history to the previous $n-1$ tokens. Unigram / bigram / trigram are the standard names ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Nanyang Technological University (NTU)](concepts/nanyangtechnologicaluniversity.md) — Singapore-based co-author affiliation on [[2605.12357-delta-mem]]. (Filed under concepts/; semantically an entity.)
- [Natarajan Dimension](concepts/NatarajanDimension.md) — Multi-class generalization of VC dimension (Natarajan 1989); used in [[2605.12966-agentic-ai-to-agi]] to bound the router's error: $\sqrt{\log K/N}$ for trees, $\sqrt{K/N}$ for neural routers.
- [Natural Language Processing](concepts/NLP.md) — Application domain transformed by [[DeepLearning]]; per [[d2l-preface]], [[Attention]] / [[transformer|transformers]] have displaced [[RNN|RNNs]] as the dominant NLP architecture. *Stub.*
- [Neural Network](concepts/NeuralNetwork.md) — composition of differentiable layers trained by gradient descent.
- [Neural Network Module (Block)](concepts/NeuralNetworkModule.md) — Universal abstraction for any callable piece of a neural network ([[PyTorch]] `nn.Module`, [[MXNet]] `nn.Block`, Keras `tf.keras.Model`, Flax `linen.Module`); subclasses provide `forward` + parameter storage, framework supplies autograd, recursive parameter discovery, `.to(device)`, `state_dict` ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Neural Tangent Kernel](concepts/NeuralTangentKernel.md) — Kernel that captures infinite-width MLP training dynamics ([[ArthurJacot|Jacot]] et al. 2018); formalizes the over-parametrized [[NeuralNetwork|net]] ↔ [[KernelMethods|kernel-method]] correspondence ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Norm](concepts/Norm.md) — Length function on a vector space ([[mml-book]] §3.1); $\ell_1$ / $\ell_2$ / $\ell_\infty$ / Frobenius the standard ones. Induced norms come from [[InnerProduct]]s.
- [Neuro-Symbolic AI](concepts/NeuroSymbolicAI.md) — Umbrella for neural+symbolic hybrids; LLM-Modulo argues for tight bi-directional integration over LLM-as-translator pipelines.
- [Next Sentence Prediction](concepts/nextsentenceprediction.md) — 
- [No Free Lunch Theorem](concepts/NoFreeLunchTheorem.md) — Wolpert & Macready 1997; no universal learner without priors. Entry point for the [[StructuredRealWorldDistribution]] argument in [[2605.12966-agentic-ai-to-agi]].
- [Notebook to Script](concepts/NotebookToScript.md) — refactoring exploratory notebooks into modular scripts.
- [NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access)](concepts/NUMA.md) — Shared-memory architecture with per-processor "closer" memory and slower remote memory; generalization of [[SMP]] for larger systems ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]). *"Today almost all high-end MIMD systems are NUMAs"* ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.3.2); typical global interconnect is [[Crossbar|crossbar]] or [[OmegaNetwork|omega]]; coherency is directory-based, not snoopy.
- [Omega (Delta) Network](concepts/OmegaNetwork.md) — Multistage interconnect: $\log_2 n$ rows of $n/2$ 2×2 switches; route by destination bit at each stage; $O(\log n)$ latency, $O(n)$ bandwidth, $O(n \log n)$ cost — *"a compromise between buses and crossbars"* ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.3.3.2). Substrate for [[FetchAndAdd|F&A]] packet combining.
- [OpenMP atomic Clause](concepts/AtomicClause.md) — `#pragma omp atomic` single-statement critical section; compiler may lower to a hardware atomic (Intel `LOCK` prefix — [[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.6.1 shows GCC's emitted `lock addl`). Cheaper than [[CriticalSection]] for one-statement updates.
- [OpenMP flush Pragma](concepts/FlushPragma.md) — `#pragma omp flush(x)` forces a memory flush under OpenMP's [[RelaxedConsistency|relaxed consistency]] model ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.6.2); auto-flushes happen at barriers + critical/ordered/parallel entry-exit + parallel-for/sections/single exit.
- [OpenMP for Pragma (parallel for)](concepts/ParallelFor.md) — `#pragma omp for` distributes loop iterations across team threads with independent-iteration requirement; loop index is private by default; `collapse(N)` flattens nested loops since OpenMP 3.0 ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.3).
- [OpenMP Locks (omp_lock_t)](concepts/OpenMPLocks.md) — Lower-level lock API for the rare case [[CriticalSection|`critical`]] / [[AtomicClause|`atomic`]] / [[Barrier|`barrier`]] / [[ReductionClause|`reduction`]] are insufficient: `omp_lock_t` + `omp_set_lock` / `omp_unset_lock` ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.15).
- [OpenMP parallel Pragma](concepts/ParallelPragma.md) — `#pragma omp parallel`; the only directive that creates a thread team. Variables declared before the directive are shared, inside are thread-local, globals always shared; combined `parallel for` / `parallel sections` forms ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.2.2).
- [OpenMP reduction Clause](concepts/ReductionClause.md) — `reduction(op:var)` gives each thread a private copy of `var` (initialized to `op`'s identity from the eight-row table `+`/`-`→0, `*`/`&&`→1, `&`→all-1s, `|`/`^`/`||`→0/all-0s/0); avoids per-iteration atomics; scalar-only in C/C++ ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.3.5).
- [OpenMP schedule Clause](concepts/ScheduleClause.md) — `schedule(static|dynamic|guided|runtime)` controls iteration→thread mapping for [[ParallelFor]]; the big-chunk-small-chunk tradeoff resolved by `guided`; runtime selection via `omp_set_schedule()` or `OMP_SCHEDULE` env var ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.3.3).
- [OpenMP single Pragma](concepts/OpenMPSingle.md) — `#pragma omp single` runs the block on exactly one thread of the team with implicit trailing barrier (`nowait` overrides); used for one-shot setup, recursive roots ([[Quicksort]] § 4.5.1), and sequential phases inside a parallel block ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.2.4).
- [OpenMP task Directive](concepts/OpenMPTaskDirective.md) — `#pragma omp task` sets up a task queue; encountering thread continues while *some* free thread executes the block later; canonical for recursion (e.g. [[Quicksort]] subtree calls) where [[ParallelFor]]'s static model fails ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.5).
- [OpenMP Work-Sharing Constructs](concepts/WorkSharing.md) — Umbrella for directives that *distribute work within an already-spawned team*: [[ParallelFor|`for`]] / `sections` / [[OpenMPSingle|`single`]] / [[OpenMPTaskDirective|`task`]]; all four have implicit barriers; combined `parallel for` / `parallel sections` collapse team-spawning + distribution ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.3 / §4.7).
- [Offline Evaluation](concepts/OfflineEvaluation.md) — pre-deployment evaluation on held-out data.
- [Offline Replay Environment](concepts/OfflineReplayEnvironment.md) — Affordability mechanism behind [[AutoTTS]]: pre-collect $N$=128 reasoning trajectories at $\Delta$=500-token intervals per (model, problem); controller actions become deterministic table lookups with zero LLM calls during search. Makes the entire 5-round $\beta$ sweep fit in 160 minutes / $39.9.
- [OLAP](concepts/OLAP.md) — analytical column-oriented database systems.
- [OLTP](concepts/OLTP.md) — transactional row-oriented database systems.
- [Odd-Even Transposition Sort](concepts/OddEvenTransposition.md) — Parallel [[BubbleSort]] variant: threads alternate odd-phase (even-indexed trade right) and even-phase (even-indexed trade left) [[CompareExchange]] operations; CUDA implementation limits each kernel to one iteration with pointer-swapping between scratch arrays ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.3.2–12.3.3).
- [One-Hot Encoding](concepts/OneHotEncoding.md) — binary indicator encoding of categoricals.
- [Operating System](concepts/OperatingSystem.md) — Software layer that mediates between user programs and [[ComputerHardware|hardware]] by providing [[Abstraction|abstractions]], policies, and mechanisms — what turns hardware into a [[ComputerSystem|computer system]] ([[dis-0-introduction]]). Dual of the embedded-`no_std` [[HardwareAbstractionLayer]] world covered in [[TheEmbeddedRustBook]].
- [1×1 Convolution](concepts/OneByOneConvolution.md) — [[ConvolutionalLayer|Conv layer]] with $k_h=k_w=1$: a per-pixel fully-connected layer over the channel axis with $c_o\cdot c_i$ weights; cheap channel mixing — workhorse of [[ResNet]] / [[Inception]] / [[NetworkInNetwork]] bottlenecks ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Orthogonal Projection](concepts/OrthogonalProjection.md) — Closest-point projection onto a subspace ([[mml-book]] §3.8); $\pi_U(\mathbf{x})=\mathbf{B}(\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{B})^{-1}\mathbf{B}^\top\mathbf{x}$. The geometric interpretation behind least-squares regression, PCA, and the SVM margin.
- [Online Evaluation](concepts/OnlineEvaluation.md) — measuring model performance on live traffic.
- [Online Inference](concepts/OnlineInference.md) — low-latency per-request prediction.
- [Online State of Associative Memory (OSAM)](concepts/onlinestateofassociativememory.md) — Fixed-size matrix storing key→value associations from streaming history; substrate of δ-mem.
- [Overfitting](concepts/Overfitting.md) — fitting training noise rather than signal.
- [Padding](concepts/Padding.md) — Extra elements (zeros in CNNs, `[PAD]` tokens in NLP) added around a boundary so windowed operators run cleanly. In CNNs: preserves spatial dims when $p=k-1$; "same"/"valid" framework conventions; lets operators implicitly encode position ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Parallel Reasoning](concepts/parallelreasoning.md) — Multiple independent reasoning trajectories from one base model; the width axis of [[testtimescaling|TTS]] and the [[WidthDepthSearch|width–depth control space]]. Phase 1 of HEAVYSKILL's pattern; spawn/kill policy in [[AutoTTS]].
- [Parallel Computing](concepts/ParallelComputing.md) — Using multiple processing units simultaneously to solve a computational problem; with [[MulticoreProcessor|multicore CPUs]] now the default form factor, no longer a specialty per [[dis-0-introduction]]. CPU-multicore C-program view upstream of the deep-learning [[DataParallelism]] / [[ModelParallelism]] / [[AutoParallelism]] treatment in [[d2l-computational-performance]].
- [Param Mem](concepts/parammem.md) — 
- [Parameter (nn.Parameter)](concepts/Parameter.md) — Tracked learnable tensor; the `nn.Parameter` wrapper is the registration mechanism that makes the framework discover, init, save, move, and optimize a weight ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Parameter Access](concepts/ParameterAccess.md) — API patterns for indexing / walking / flat-listing the parameters of a [[NeuralNetworkModule|module]] tree (`state_dict()`, `named_parameters()`, `net[idx]`) ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Parameter Initialization (Framework Mechanics)](concepts/ParameterInitialization.md) — The *mechanical* side of [[WeightInitialization]]: default init at allocation, bulk `net.apply(init_fn)`, targeted per-layer overrides, custom initializers ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Parameter Sharing (Tied Weights)](concepts/ParameterSharing.md) — Multiple layers referencing the same parameter tensor (created by reusing a module instance); gradients add naturally; foundational to CNN/RNN/Transformer-embedding architectures ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Partial Derivative](concepts/PartialDerivative.md) — Rate of change of $f:\mathbb{R}^n\to\mathbb{R}$ in one coordinate
- [Partitioned Matrix](concepts/PartitionedMatrix.md) — Matrix divided into compatible submatrix blocks; the algebraic property that submatrices multiply "just like numbers" underlies all block-parallel matrix algorithms ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.2). ([[mml-book]] §5.2); collected into a [[Gradient]] / [[Jacobian]]. The basic building block of [[Backpropagation]].
- [PCA](concepts/PCA.md) — principal component analysis acronym page.
- [PDDL](concepts/PDDL.md) — Planning Domain Definition Language (McDermott et al. 1998); VAL plan validator is the canonical hard critic in LLM-Modulo's Blocksworld case study.
- [PEP 8](concepts/PEP8.md) — official Python style guide.
- [Persona-Driven Synthesis](concepts/personadrivensynthesis.md) — 
- [Perplexity](concepts/Perplexity.md) — NLP-standard LM metric: $\exp(\frac{1}{n}\sum -\log P(x_t\mid x_{<t}))$ — reciprocal of the geometric mean of next-token-probability "choices." Bounds: 1 (perfect), $|\mathcal{V}|$ (uniform), $+\infty$ (worst) ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [PlanBench](concepts/PlanBench.md) — Extensible LLM planning benchmark (Valmeekam et al. NeurIPS 2023); the empirical backbone of the "LLMs can't plan" position.
- [Planning](concepts/Planning.md) — Automated/AI planning (Ghallab/Nau/Traverso 2004): synthesize an action sequence achieving a goal from a domain model; distinct from *acting*.
- [Poisoned RAG](concepts/poisonedrag.md) — 
- [Polanyi's Revenge](concepts/PolanyisRevenge.md) — Kambhampati's framing (CACM 2021): LLMs make tacit knowledge cheaply accessible without explicit articulation; the bridge that makes LLM-Modulo's cheap-approximate-knowledge story viable.
- [Pooling](concepts/Pooling.md) — Parameter-free aggregator ([[MaxPooling|max]] or [[AveragePooling|avg]]) over a window; provides spatial downsampling + local translation invariance; per-channel (preserves channel count). Framework default: stride = window size ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Patch Embedding](concepts/PatchEmbedding.md) — [[VisionTransformer|ViT]] "tokenizer": split image into $p\times p$ patches, linearly project to dimension $d$; implementable as a stride-$p$ kernel-$p$ 2-D convolution ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Positional Encoding](concepts/positionalencoding.md) — 
- [Power Law](concepts/powerlaw.md) — Functional form $y = A x^{-\alpha}$ — s
- [Power Method](concepts/PowerMethod.md) — Iterative eigenvector extraction: $x^{(k)} = A^k x / \|A^k x\|$ converges to the dominant [[Eigenvector|eigenvector]]; deflation peels off subsequent eigenpairs; used in PageRank ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.6.1).traight line on a log-log plot; the universal substrate of neural scaling laws.
- [Pre-commit](concepts/PreCommit.md) — git-hook framework for code quality.
- [Pre-Normalization](concepts/PreNorm.md) — Transformer block variant applying [[LayerNormalization|LayerNorm]] *before* each sublayer (vs post-norm after the residual); stable training without learning-rate warmup; adopted by [[VisionTransformer|ViT]] + modern LLMs ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Precision and Recall](concepts/PrecisionRecall.md) — complementary classification metrics with F1.
- [Prefect](concepts/Prefect.md) — Python-native workflow orchestrator.
- [Prefix LM](concepts/prefixlm.md) — Single-stack Transformer with fully-visible attention over the prefix and causal attention over the target; ablated and beaten by encoder-decoder in T5.
- [Pretraining](concepts/pretraining.md) — Self-supervised first-stage training (next-token, masked-token, or denoising); governed quantitatively by scaling laws.
- [Principal Component Analysis](concepts/PrincipalComponentAnalysis.md) — orthogonal-variance dimensionality reduction.
- [Probabilistic Perspective](concepts/ProbabilisticPerspective.md) — [[KevinMurphy|Murphy]]'s unifying lens (Murphy §1.1): every unknown quantity is a random variable. Justified by [[DecisionMakingUnderUncertainty|decision-theoretic]] necessity (Dutch-book / Cox / Savage) and by being the lingua franca of every neighboring science. Distinguishes epistemic from aleatoric uncertainty; treats predictions as distributions, not point estimates.
- [Probability Space](concepts/ProbabilitySpace.md) — Triple $(\Omega, \mathcal{A}, P)$ — sample space, event space, probability measure ([[mml-book]] §6.1.2). Generalizes Boolean logic to degrees of plausibility (Cox-Jaynes).
- [Process (operating system)](concepts/Process.md) — OS-level execution unit with private memory + process-table entry; [[Thread]]s are a "special case of an OS process" with shared memory ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [`ps` (Process Status Utility)](concepts/Ps.md) — [[OperatingSystem|Unix]] command-line utility that **lists running [[Process|processes]]** — the canonical primitive for discovering [[ProcessID|PIDs]]. Common forms: `ps` (current shell), `ps -A` / `ps -e` (all processes), `ps -A \| grep a.out` (filter by name — the [[GdbAttach|attach-mode]] recipe), `ps -ef` / `ps aux` (full / BSD-style format), `ps -p <pid>` (single process). First [[OperatingSystem|OS]]-introspection tool in the [[DiveIntoSystems]] corpus — user-side view of the kernel's [[Process|process]] table ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [Processor Affinity](concepts/ProcessorAffinity.md) — Binding a thread to a preferred core to preserve cache contents across timeslices; the OS-level companion to [[FalseSharing|false-sharing]] mitigation. Supported by OpenMP 3.1 (`proc_bind` / `OMP_PROC_BIND`), Linux `sched_setaffinity` / `taskset`; pairs naturally with [[NUMA]] memory affinity ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.10).
- [Product Design](concepts/ProductDesign.md) — upstream definition of users, value, and metrics.
- [Prompt Injection](concepts/promptinjection.md) — 
- [pyproject.toml](concepts/PyprojectToml.md) — standard Python project manifest.
- [Pytest](concepts/Pytest.md) — dominant Python testing framework.
- [pytest-cov](concepts/PytestCov.md) — coverage plugin for Pytest.
- [Python](concepts/Python.md) — dominant ML/AI programming language.
- [Python Logging](concepts/PythonLogging.md) — standard library logging module.
- [PyTorch DDP](concepts/PyTorchDDP.md) — distributed data-parallel training in PyTorch.
- [Pull-Up Resistor](concepts/PullUpResistor.md) — Resistor pulling a digital input pin to V_CC so it defaults HIGH; ATmega's internal pull-up is engaged by writing DDR=0 + PORT=1 ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 20).
- [Pulse Width Modulation (PWM)](concepts/PulseWidthModulation.md) — Synthesizing an analog average voltage from a digital pin by toggling at a controllable duty cycle. On Uno: `analogWrite(pin, 0..255)` at ~490 Hz via the three [[TimerCounter|timer/counters]] on the six PWM-capable pins (3/5/6/9/10/11) ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 27).
- [RAG](concepts/rag.md) — 
- [RAM](concepts/RAM.md) — Random-access memory; volatile main working memory of a [[ComputerSystem|computer system]]. Named in [[dis-0-introduction]] as one of the four core [[ComputerHardware|hardware]] components; sits mid-stack in the [[MemoryHierarchy]] between CPU caches and disk.
- [Random Variable](concepts/RandomVariable.md) — Function $X:\Omega\to\mathcal{T}$ pushing a [[ProbabilitySpace|probability space]]'s measure onto a target space ([[mml-book]] §6.1.2). "Neither random nor a variable — it is a function."
- [Raspberry Pi](concepts/RaspberryPi.md) — Family of inexpensive ARM-[[SystemOnAChip|SoC]]-based [[SingleBoardComputer|single-board computers]] running general-purpose OS; the canonical contemporary SBC cited in [[dis-0-introduction]].
- [Recomputation](concepts/recomputation.md) — Drop activations in forward, recompute in backward; trades FLOPs for HBM bandwidth in FlashAttention's backward pass.
- [Recursive Self-Improvement](concepts/recursiveselfimprovement.md) — 
- [Queries, Keys, Values (QKV)](concepts/QueryKeyValue.md) — Three-tensor abstraction underneath every attention mechanism; database analogy ($\mathbf{q}$ retrieves over $(\mathbf{k}_i,\mathbf{v}_i)$ pairs); all three come from linear projections of the same input in [[SelfAttention]], from decoder+encoder respectively in cross-attention ([[d2l-attention-and-transformers]]).
- [Quicksort](concepts/Quicksort.md) — Recursive divide-and-conquer sort; parallelized in [[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.5.1 with `omp task`; §12.1 adds separation-process detail, OpenMP `nowait` variant, and [[Hyperquicksort]] extension for hypercubes ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]]).
- [Radix Sort](concepts/RadixSort.md) — Non-comparison sort using bit-level bucket assignment; special case of [[SamplingBucketSort|bucket sort]] requiring no sampling when data is uniform; CUDPP implements via segmented [[PrefixScan]] ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.6).
- [Recurrent Layer](concepts/RecurrentLayer.md) — Layer implementing the [[RNN]] recurrence with a [[HiddenState|hidden state]]; framework realizations: `nn.RNN` (PyTorch), `SimpleRNN` (Keras), `rnn.RNN` (MXNet). Concatenation-matmul under the hood ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Relaxed Consistency (OpenMP memory model)](concepts/RelaxedConsistency.md) — [[OpenMP]]'s named memory-consistency position: updates not guaranteed visible between synchronization points; seven auto-flushing sync points (barrier, critical/ordered/parallel entry-exit, parallel-for/sections/single exit) cover most code; explicit lever is [[FlushPragma|`#pragma omp flush(x)`]] ([[parproc-ch04-introduction-to-openmp]] §4.6.2).
- [Reflexion](concepts/reflexion.md) — 
- [Regression Testing](concepts/RegressionTesting.md) — guarding against unintended behavior changes.
- [Receptive Field](concepts/ReceptiveField.md) — Set of all input elements that can affect a given feature-map element via forward propagation; grows multiplicatively with depth + stride + pooling; Hubel & Wiesel's neurophysiology lineage; gates CNN ability to capture global features ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Regularization](concepts/Regularization.md) — techniques constraining model complexity.
- [Responsibility](concepts/Responsibility.md) — Posterior probability that mixture component $k$ generated point $\mathbf{x}_n$ ([[mml-book]] §11.2.1); the soft cluster assignment in [[GaussianMixtureModel|GMMs]] and the central E-step quantity in the [[EMAlgorithm]].
- [Recommender Systems](concepts/RecommenderSystems.md) — Personalized [[SupervisedLearning|supervised]] application; serious open problems with censored feedback, feedback loops, exposure bias ([[d2l-introduction]]).
- [Regression](concepts/Regression.md) — Supervised task with continuous numerical labels — *how much?* / *how many?* problems. Squared-error loss; linear, polynomial, spline, GAM model classes.
- [Reinforcement Learning](concepts/reinforcementlearning.md) — 
- [ReLU](concepts/ReLU.md) — rectified linear unit activation function.
- [Representation Learning](concepts/RepresentationLearning.md) — Automatically learning how to represent data; [[DeepLearning|deep learning]] is its **multi-level** instance — layers learned jointly from data ([[d2l-introduction]]).
- [Reproducibility](concepts/Reproducibility.md) — ability to re-run experiments deterministically.
- [Reproducibility in ML](concepts/ReproducibilityInML.md) — ML-specific reproducibility challenges.
- [R Vectorization](concepts/RVectorization.md) — [[Rlanguage|R]]'s primary performance technique: replacing interpreted loops with compiled built-in functions (`sum`, `apply`, `ifelse`, etc.) for ~100–500× speedups; foundation for parallel R code in [[Snow]] and related packages ([[parproc-appC-r-quick-start]] §C.4, §C.7).
- [Rich Library](concepts/RichLibrary.md) — Python library for formatted terminal output.
- [RLVR](concepts/rlvr.md) — 
- [RISC](concepts/RISC.md) — Reduced Instruction Set Computing; small fixed-width instruction set, single-cycle execution, large register file, pipelined. The design philosophy of [[AVR]] / [[ARMCortexM|ARM]] / MIPS / RISC-V; opposite of [[CISC]] ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16).
- [RNN](concepts/RNN.md) — recurrent neural network for sequences.
- [ROME](concepts/rome.md) — 
- [Root Cause Analysis](concepts/RootCauseAnalysis.md) — structured investigation of underlying failures.
- [RotatingFileHandler](concepts/RotatingFileHandler.md) — size/time-rotating Python log handler.
- [Routing-Based Agentic AI](concepts/RoutingBasedAgenticAI.md) — Simplest [[AgenticAI]] regime: a single router picks one of $K$ specialist agents. Error $\mathcal{O}(K\cdot N^{-1/d_{\max}})$ vs monolith's $\mathcal{O}(N^{-1/D})$ — exponential gap. Optimal granularity $K^*$ balances specialization gain against [[NatarajanDimension|router]] cost.
- [S3 Classes (R)](concepts/S3Classes.md) — [[Rlanguage|R]]'s original lightweight OO system: a list with a `class` attribute; generic functions dispatch via `generic.class` naming convention. Used throughout base R and CRAN; sufficient for most R OO needs ([[parproc-appC-r-quick-start]] §C.10.3).
- [Scaled Dot-Product Attention](concepts/scaleddotproductattention.md) — 
- [Scaling Laws](concepts/scalinglaws.md) — Empirical power-law scaling of Transformer LM loss in $N$, $D$, $C$ (Kaplan et al., 2020); the quantitative basis for scaling-up LLMs.
- [SCAN](concepts/scan.md) — 
- [Sampling Bucket Sort](concepts/SamplingBucketSort.md) — Parallel sorting algorithm: sample to set bucket boundaries, parallel local sort per worker, copy back. Matloff's intro [[OpenMP]] example ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]); MPI implementation added from [[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.5.
- [Shearsort](concepts/Shearsort.md) — 2D-mesh parallel sorting by Sen, Shamir, and Scherson; ceil(log₂n)+1 alternating row/column sort phases; result is a "snakelike" globally sorted layout; column phases use `MPI_Alltoall` ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.4).
- [Scatter/Gather](concepts/ScatterGather.md) — Manager/worker parallel paradigm; pervasive in [[MPI]] / Hadoop/[[MapReduce]] / R [[Snow]] ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [SciBERT](concepts/SciBERT.md) — BERT pretrained on scientific text.
- [Search Space](concepts/SearchSpace.md) — hyperparameter configuration space.
- [Secrets Scanning](concepts/SecretsScanning.md) — automated credential detection in code.
- [Self-Attention](concepts/selfattention.md) — 
- [Self-Supervised Learning](concepts/SelfSupervisedLearning.md) — Fabricate supervision from structure in unlabeled data (masked-LM, relative-position, occlusion, contrastive); the bridge between [[UnsupervisedLearning|unsupervised]] and [[SupervisedLearning|supervised]] paradigms; foundation of modern [[pretraining|pretraining]].
- [Self-Consistency](concepts/selfconsistency.md) — Sample $N$ chain-of-thought trajectories from a base model and return the majority-voted answer (Wang et al. 2022). Canonical [[parallelreasoning|parallel-reasoning]] baseline in TTS; the "fixed full-budget corner" of [[WidthDepthSearch|width–depth control space]]. Cited as the dominant handcrafted baseline in [[2605.08083-autotts|AutoTTS]] (CMC β=0.5 reduces tokens ~69.5% at matched accuracy).
- [Self-Verification](concepts/SelfVerification.md) — Hypothesis (Reflexion / Self-Refine) that LLMs can check their own outputs; falsified empirically on graph coloring + PlanBench in [[2402.01817-llm-modulo]] — external sound critics required.
- [Separating Hyperplane](concepts/SeparatingHyperplane.md) — Hyperplane $\langle\mathbf{w},\mathbf{x}\rangle+b=0$ dividing two classes ([[mml-book]] §12.1); the geometric object the [[SupportVectorMachine|SVM]] picks (via max [[Margin]]).
- [Semantic Hijacking](concepts/SemanticHijacking.md) — Shehata & Li 2026a (arxiv 2604.24512) 3-stage adversarial prompt construction: Context Hijacking + Nested 3-Hop Bridging + Semantic Distraction. The methodology that makes [[BystanderEffect]] visible by elevating logical search cost.
- [SentencePiece](concepts/sentencepiece.md) — Language-agnostic subword tokenizer treating whitespace as a regular symbol; the tokenizer used by T5.
- [Sequence-to-Sequence Learning](concepts/seqtoseq.md) — 
- [Sequential Deliberation](concepts/sequentialdeliberation.md) — 
- [Shadow Deployment](concepts/ShadowDeployment.md) — running a new model in parallel without serving outputs.
- [Shared-Memory Architecture](concepts/SharedMemoryArchitecture.md) — Parallel hardware paradigm where many CPUs share a single physical memory address space; canonical topologies are [[SMP]] / [[Multicore]] / [[NUMA]] ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [SIGBUS (Bus Error Signal)](concepts/SIGBUS.md) — [[OperatingSystem|POSIX]] [[Signal|signal]] (10 on macOS/BSD, 7 on Linux) delivered on **misaligned memory access** or access to an `mmap`'d region with no backing storage — *"if a program tries to access memory with a misaligned memory address for the type it is accessing, it receives a `SIGBUS` signal"* ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|Ch 3.4]]). Distinct from [[SegmentationFault|`SIGSEGV`]] (invalid address) — [[SIGBUS]] is *valid address, wrong alignment*. Common on strict-alignment [[ARMCortexM|ARM]] / SPARC / RISC-V; rare on x86 (which makes most misalignment silently slow). `handle SIGBUS stop` is the [[GdbSignalControl|GDB-side]] halt rule ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [Signal (POSIX Asynchronous Notification)](concepts/Signal.md) — [[OperatingSystem|POSIX]] mechanism for **asynchronous notification** of a [[Process|process]] — the [[OperatingSystem|kernel]]'s way of interrupting a running program to deliver one of a small set of named events. Carries **no payload** beyond identity; receiver consults per-signal **disposition** (default / ignore / custom handler via `signal()` / `sigaction()`). Canonical signals: `SIGINT` / `SIGTERM` / `SIGKILL` (uncatchable kill) / `SIGSEGV` (segfault) / [[SIGBUS|`SIGBUS`]] (misalignment) / `SIGPIPE` / `SIGCHLD` / `SIGSTOP` (uncatchable suspend) / `SIGCONT`. Substrate for [[GdbSignalControl|`signal` / `handle` / `info signal`]] in [[GDB]] — the asynchrony point where the kernel interrupts user code outside a [[SystemCall|system call]] ([[dis-3-4-gdb-advanced|DIS Ch 3.4]]).
- [Sigmoid](concepts/Sigmoid.md) — Logistic squashing activation $1/(1+e^{-x})$; gradients vanish in saturated tails. Mostly displaced by [[ReLU]] in hidden layers; survives at output units + LSTM/GRU gates ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [SIMD (Single Instruction Multiple Data)](concepts/SIMD.md) — Lockstep parallel execution paradigm; historical ILLIAC/CM-1/CM-2 → modern [[GPU|GPUs]] ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [Single-Board Computer](concepts/SingleBoardComputer.md) — Full [[ComputerSystem|computer system]] on a single PCB ([[CPU]] + [[RAM]] + I/O + networking + power); [[RaspberryPi]] is the canonical example. Cited in [[dis-0-introduction]] as a key data point in the systems-miniaturization story.
- [Singular Value Decomposition](concepts/SingularValueDecomposition.md) — $\mathbf{A}=\mathbf{U}\boldsymbol\Sigma\mathbf{V}^\top$ for any real matrix ([[mml-book]] §4.5); generalizes [[Eigendecomposition]] to non-square / non-symmetric. Engine of low-rank approximation, PCA, LoRA, and the [[ConditionNumber]].
- [SHAP](concepts/SHAP.md) — Shapley-value feature attributions.
- [SKILL.md](concepts/skillmd.md) — 
- [SMP (Symmetric Multiprocessor)](concepts/SMP.md) — Shared-memory topology: processors + memory modules on a common bus with arbitration; modern [[Multicore]] chips are SMPs in a single package ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [Softmax](concepts/Softmax.md) — vector-to-probability normalization.
- [Sparse Matrix](concepts/SparseMatrix.md) — Matrix with mostly zero entries; stored in Compressed Sparse Row (CSR) format (avals / cols / rowplaces arrays); parallelized by row-chunk assignment with load-balance caveats ([[parproc-ch11-parallel-matrix-operations]] §11.7).
- [Speech Recognition](concepts/SpeechRecognition.md) — Automatic transcription of spoken language; per [[d2l-preface]], one of [[DeepLearning]]'s earliest industrial application areas. *Stub.*
- [Sovereignty Decay Law](concepts/SovereigntyDecayLaw.md) — Thm 1 of [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]]: $\mathcal{S} = \mathcal{S}_0\exp(-(\mathcal{H}_\tau/\gamma_p)\cdot\mathcal{L})$. Exponential decay in [[CompositeSocialLoad]] and [[TaskEntropy]], modulated by intrinsic resilience $\gamma_p$.
- [Sovereignty Gap](concepts/SovereigntyGap.md) — Thm 3 of [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]]: $G_\mathcal{S} = \mathcal{V}_{int}-\mathcal{A}_{ext}$. Sign distinguishes [[AlignmentHallucination]] ($\gg 0$, derives-then-lies) from [[IntegrativeReasoningBypass]] ($\ll 0$, never-derives).
- [Sovereignty Trap](concepts/SovereigntyTrap.md) — Klein & Klein 2025: state where authoritative-seeming competence tempts a reasoner to cede intellectual judgment. Repurposed in [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]] for LLM-on-LLM cession.
- [Span Corruption](concepts/spancorruption.md) — Denoising objective that replaces contiguous token spans with sentinels and predicts only the corrupted spans; pre-training objective for T5.
- [Standardization](concepts/Standardization.md) — zero-mean, unit-variance feature scaling.
- [State Dict](concepts/StateDict.md) — Flat `OrderedDict` mapping hierarchical parameter names to tensors; the [[PyTorch]] portable snapshot format. Architecture is *not* in the file — code must rebuild it ([[d2l-builders-guide]]).
- [Status Register (SREG)](concepts/StatusRegister.md) — The most important MCU register: holds [[ALU]] flag bits and the global interrupt-enable bit. On [[AVR]]: `I T H S V N Z C`. **Not auto-saved on ISR entry** — the application or the `ISR(...)` macro must save it ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 16 / 21).
- [Statistical Independence](concepts/StatisticalIndependence.md) — $A\perp B \iff P(A,B)=P(A)P(B)$. Marginal and conditional independence are distinct: each can hold without the other. Underlies the i.i.d. assumption, naive Bayes, and PGM factorizations. [[d2l-preliminaries]] §Multiple Random Variables.
- [Software Distributed Shared Memory (SDSM)](concepts/SoftwareDSM.md) — Software packages that simulate shared memory on message-passing hardware (NOWs) via VM-system tricks (`mprotect` + SIGSEGV handlers); page-based (Treadmarks at Rice; [[JIAJIA]] at Academy of Sciences, China) and object-based varieties. Cannot fake shared *pointers*. Granularity is pages (4 KB), not cache blocks (~512 B) — magnifies [[FalseSharing]] ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.11).
- [Static Task Assignment](concepts/StaticTaskAssignment.md) — Decide at the outset which processor handles which tasks. Zero scheduler-side runtime [[CommunicationBottleneck|communication]]; the i.i.d. $O(1/\sqrt{m})$ chunk-time concentration argument shows there's essentially no [[LoadBalancing|load imbalance]] for moderate chunk sizes. When i.i.d. fails (Mandelbrot's spatial correlation), Method A' — *randomized* static — restores it ([[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.4).
- [Stochastic Gradient Descent](concepts/StochasticGradientDescent.md) — Single-example (or minibatch) variant of [[GradientDescent]]. Universal DL optimizer; noise helps escape saddle points in non-convex losses ([[d2l-linear-regression]] §3.1.4).
- [Stratified Sampling](concepts/StratifiedSampling.md) — splits preserving class balance.
- [Stride](concepts/Stride.md) — Number of input elements a [[Convolution|conv]] or [[Pooling|pool]] window advances per output position; with $p=k-1$, stride-$s$ exactly downsamples spatial dims by factor $s$ ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]]).
- [Structured Logging](concepts/StructuredLogging.md) — machine-parseable key/value logs.
- [Structured Real-World Distribution](concepts/StructuredRealWorldDistribution.md) — Liao et al. Def. 2.1: data supported on a union of $K$ low-dim manifolds $\bigcup_k \mathcal{M}_k$ with $d_k\!\ll\! D$. The structural prior that breaks the [[CurseOfDimensionality]] for [[AgenticAI]].
- [Supply-Chain Security](concepts/supplychainsecurity.md) — 
- [Support Vector Machine](concepts/SupportVectorMachine.md) — maximum-margin classical classifier.
- [Symmetric Positive Definite Matrix](concepts/SymmetricPositiveDefiniteMatrix.md) — Symmetric $\mathbf{A}\succ 0$ ([[mml-book]] §3.2.3, Def 3.4); exactly the matrices encoding [[InnerProduct]]s. Covers covariance matrices, Gram matrices, valid kernels, Hessians at minima.
- [Synthetic Data](concepts/syntheticdata.md) — 
- [System 1 vs System 2](concepts/System1And2.md) — Kahneman's dual-process taxonomy; the framing on which Kambhampati hangs the LLM-as-pseudo-System-1 / external-critic-as-System-2 composition.
- [Systems Design](concepts/SystemsDesign.md) — end-to-end ML architecture design.
- [System on a Chip (SoC)](concepts/SystemOnAChip.md) — Integrated circuit combining [[CPU]] + [[RAM]] (+ GPU, modem, etc.) on a single die; the substrate of modern smartphones and [[SingleBoardComputer|SBCs]] like the [[RaspberryPi]] per [[dis-0-introduction]].
- [T5](concepts/t5.md) — Text-to-Text Transfer Transformer (Raffel et al., 2020); encoder-decoder + span-corruption + C4 + text-to-text framework; T5-11B reaches SOTA on 18/24 tasks.
- [Target Drift](concepts/TargetDrift.md) — change in label distribution post-deployment.
- [Task Entropy](concepts/TaskEntropy.md) — $\mathcal{H}_\tau$: intrinsic logical search cost of a task; friction term in the [[SovereigntyDecayLaw]]. Operationalized in [[2605.10698-bystander-effect-mas]] via [[multichallenge|Multi-Challenge]] (low) / [[swebench|SWE-bench]] (medium) / [[gaia|GAIA]] (high) contexts.
- [Tanh](concepts/Tanh.md) — Hyperbolic-tangent squashing activation; zero-centred, max derivative 1; the pre-[[ReLU]] hidden-layer default ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Tensor](concepts/Tensor.md) — multidimensional array, core DL data structure.
- [Test-and-Set (TAS)](concepts/TestAndSet.md) — Canonical atomic synchronization primitive for shared-memory hardware: `copy L→R; if R==0 then write 1 to L`, performed without intervening bus transactions ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.4.1). Pure-TAS spinning on a bus floods bandwidth, motivating per-CPU caches + [[CacheCoherency]]. Intel's `LOCK` prefix on `cmpxchg` is the modern equivalent.
- [Test-Time Scaling](concepts/testtimescaling.md) — Improving inference-time performance by spending more compute per query. Three positions in the 2026 corpus: externalize via harness (Conductor), internalize via training (HEAVYSKILL), automate the harness ([[AutoTTS]]). All width × depth methods are special cases of one control space ([[WidthDepthSearch]]).
- [Thread](concepts/Thread.md) — Shared-memory unit of execution; "a special case of an OS [[Process]]" but threads of the same program share memory ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [Test Coverage](concepts/Coverage.md) — fraction of code exercised by a test suite.
- [Test Set Reuse (Adaptive Overfitting)](concepts/TestSetReuse.md) — Repeated test-set evaluation invalidates its unbiased-estimator property: (i) multiple-hypothesis testing blows up per-classifier false-discovery rates; (ii) information leaks to the modeler, breaking the IID-of-classifier-choice premise of Hoeffding's analysis (Dwork et al. 2015). [[d2l-linear-classification]] anchor.
- [Testing](concepts/Testing.md) — discipline of validating code, data, and models.
- [Text-to-Text Framework](concepts/texttotextframework.md) — Unified NLP interface casting every task as string→string with a task-prefix prompt; introduced for T5.
- [Text Classification](concepts/TextClassification.md) — assigning categorical labels to text.
- [Tokenization](concepts/Tokenization.md) — splitting text into model-input units.
- [Trace](concepts/Trace.md) — Sum of diagonal entries of a square matrix ([[mml-book]] §4.1); cyclic-invariant, basis-invariant, equals sum of eigenvalues. Frobenius norm and many regression derivations rewrite via trace.
- [Tokenizer](concepts/Tokenizer.md) — component implementing tokenization.
- [Timer / Counter](concepts/TimerCounter.md) — MCU peripheral that increments on every clock tick to generate delays, count events, produce [[PulseWidthModulation|PWM]], drive periodic interrupts. [[ATmega328P]] has three (TC0/TC1 8-bit, TC2 16-bit; the Arduino runtime uses TC0/TC1 for `delay()`/`millis()`) ([[embedded-controllers-fiore]] ch. 28).
- [Topological Edge Weight](concepts/TopologicalEdgeWeight.md) — Liao et al. Lemma 4.4: $\mathcal{W}(e^*) = $ Upstream History · Local Valve · Downstream Future — the gradient flux through a specific edge; design rule: contractive at long-chain endpoints, ultra-tight before critical decisions.
- [Topological Weight](concepts/TopologicalWeight.md) — Liao et al. Lemma 4.2: $\omega_u = \|d\mathcal{L}/dx_u\|$ — per-agent gradient sensitivity aggregated along all paths to sinks; building block of [[CompositionalCapacity]].
- [Timesharing](concepts/Timesharing.md) — OS mechanism giving each process a short CPU turn (quantum/timeslice, typically 50–60 ms) enforced via hardware timer interrupts; rapid turn-taking creates the illusion of simultaneous execution. Foundation for understanding process scheduling costs in parallel programs. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.1)
- [Train/Val/Test Split](concepts/TrainValTestSplit.md) — partitioning data for fit, tune, and test.
- [Trainer](concepts/Trainer.md) — abstraction encapsulating training loops.
- [Training-Serving Skew](concepts/TrainingServingSkew.md) — mismatch between training and production data/transforms.
- [Transfer Learning](concepts/TransferLearning.md) — reusing pretrained knowledge for new tasks.
- [Translation Invariance](concepts/TranslationInvariance.md) — Function unchanged by input shifts; the prior that, imposed on an MLP, forces the [[Convolution|convolution]] operator ([[d2l-convolutional-neural-networks]] §why-conv). Conv layers are translation *equivariant*; [[MaxPooling]] adds local *invariance*.
- [Translation Lookaside Buffer](concepts/TranslationLookasideBuffer.md) — Hardware cache for page-table entries in a [[VirtualMemory]] system; eliminates the double memory-access overhead of virtual-to-physical address translation. Flushed or invalidated on [[ContextSwitch]], adding TLB warm-up cost to context switching. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.2.3)
- [Transformer](concepts/transformer.md) — 
- [Teacher Forcing](concepts/TeacherForcing.md) — Autoregressive-LM training scheme: feed the ground-truth previous token at every step (targets = inputs shifted by 1); enables parallel within-sequence training but introduces exposure bias at inference ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Tree Barrier](concepts/TreeBarrier.md) — Parallelized [[Barrier]] structured as $\log_2 n$ levels of nested sub-barriers; reduces serial fan-in from $O(n)$ to $O(\log n)$ ([[parproc-ch03-shared-memory-parallelism]] §3.12.4.2.1). Sibling of [[ButterflyBarrier]].
- [Tree of Thoughts (ToT)](concepts/TreeOfThoughts.md) — Yao et al. NeurIPS 2023 prompting framework; recast in [[2402.01817-llm-modulo]] as "prompt diversification" — any soundness comes from external problem-specific verifiers, not the tree.
- [Truncated BPTT](concepts/TruncatedBPTT.md) — Practical BPTT variants — full / regular / randomized truncation — terminating the gradient recursion after a finite window. Regular truncation (Jaeger 2002) is what frameworks implement; randomized (Tallec & Ollivier 2017) is unbiased but empirically no better ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [Trust Root](concepts/trustroot.md) — 
- [Type Hints](concepts/TypeHints.md) — Python static type annotations.
- [Typer](concepts/Typer.md) — Python CLI library built on type hints.
- [Underfitting](concepts/Underfitting.md) — Model too simple → high training error + small [[GeneralizationGap|gap]]; the diagnostic mirror image of [[Overfitting]] ([[d2l-linear-regression]] §3.6).
- [Uniform Convergence](concepts/UniformConvergence.md) — Statistical-learning-theory property: with high probability, the empirical error of *every* classifier $f\in\mathcal F$ simultaneously converges to its true error. Justifies [[EmpiricalRiskMinimization|ERM]] generalization when paired with a complexity measure ([[VCDimension|VC dimension]], Rademacher) ([[d2l-linear-classification]]).
- [Universal Approximation Theorem](concepts/UniversalApproximationTheorem.md) — Single-hidden-layer MLP with arbitrary width can approximate any continuous function ([[GeorgeCybenko|Cybenko 1989]]); existence ≠ learnability; depth still wins in practice ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Unit Testing](concepts/UnitTesting.md) — testing the smallest functional units in isolation.
- [Uninitialized Read (Memory Error)](concepts/UninitializedReadError.md) — The [[CLanguage|C]] bug class where the program reads from memory that has been **allocated but never written**. *"Accessing values from memory that haven't been initialized, such as `x = ptr[3]` when that array index hasn't been assigned"* per [[dis-3-3-valgrind|DIS Ch 3.3]]. Returns whatever bit pattern was left over — silent when it happens to be benign, catastrophic when it isn't. Detected by [[Memcheck]] via per-bit V-bit shadow tracking propagated through arithmetic, errored only on **use** (branch / syscall / output). The classic *flaky / disappears-under-the-debugger* bug. ([[dis-3-3-valgrind]]).
- [University of Maryland (UMD)](concepts/universityofmaryland.md) — Primary author affiliation on [[2605.08083-autotts]] ([[AutoTTS]]); [[HengHuang]]'s group runs the Parallel-Probe / AutoTTS TTS-discovery line via [[TongZheng]]. (Filed under concepts/ for historical reasons; semantically an entity.)
- [Valgrind](concepts/Valgrind.md) — **Dynamic binary-instrumentation framework** for [[CLanguage|C]] / C++ whose flagship tool [[Memcheck]] detects heap memory errors — *"Valgrind's Memcheck debugging tool highlights heap memory errors in programs"* ([[dis-3-3-valgrind|DIS Ch 3.3]]). Workflow: `gcc -g` + `valgrind -v ./a.out` (+ `--leak-check=yes` for per-leak detail). Heap-only — *"does not detect stack memory access errors at the same granularity as it does with heap memory, and it does not detect memory access errors with global data memory"*. ~10–50× slowdown, no recompilation needed. The **second** of [[dis-2-10-summary|Ch 2.10]]'s two debugging tools (after [[GDB]]); promoted from forward-ref stub. ([[dis-3-3-valgrind]]).
- [Vanishing Gradient](concepts/VanishingGradient.md) — gradients shrinking to zero in deep nets.
- [Verification Levels](concepts/verificationlevels.md) — 
- [Versioning](concepts/Versioning.md) — tracking changes to code, data, and models.
- [Virtual Environment](concepts/VirtualEnvironment.md) — isolated Python interpreter and dependencies.
- [Virtual Memory](concepts/VirtualMemory.md) — OS/hardware mechanism mapping each program's virtual addresses to physical RAM via a page table; goals are overcoming physical memory limits, relieving the compiler of real-address management, and enforcing security. Non-resident pages generate page faults (OS + disk access) — catastrophically more expensive than cache misses. The [[TranslationLookasideBuffer]] avoids double memory access per translation. ([[parproc-appA-systems-issues]] §A.2.2)
- [Voyager](concepts/voyager.md) — 
- [Weight Decay](concepts/WeightDecay.md) — $\ell_2$ [[Regularization]]: penalize $\tfrac{\lambda}{2}\|\mathbf{w}\|^2$; the [[MinibatchSGD|SGD]] update becomes $\mathbf{w}\leftarrow(1-\eta\lambda)\mathbf{w}-\eta\hat{\mathbf{g}}$, literally *decaying* weights each step. Framework-integrated into the optimizer ([[d2l-linear-regression]] §3.7).
- [Watchpoint](concepts/Watchpoint.md) — [[Debugger|debugger]] primitive that **pauses on memory write** (`watch expr`) rather than PC reach — the *data-trigger* counterpart to [[Breakpoint|breakpoints]]. Hardware-assisted on most architectures (x86: DR0–DR3 debug registers; ARM: watchpoint control units) — 4 hardware slots typical, software fallback is single-step-and-check at ~100× slowdown. Variants: `watch` (write), `rwatch` (read), `awatch` (read or write). Canonical use: **find the line that corrupts a variable** — GDB reports `Old value` / `New value` at the exact write site. Shares the [[GdbBreakpointManagement|`enable` / `disable` / `delete`]] lifecycle with breakpoints ([[dis-3-1-gdb|Ch 3.1]] / [[dis-3-2-gdb-commands|Ch 3.2]]).
- [Weight Initialization](concepts/WeightInitialization.md) — choosing starting values for network parameters.
- [Width–Depth Search](concepts/WidthDepthSearch.md) — 2D control space spanning [[testtimescaling|TTS]]: width = parallel branches, depth = per-branch generation budget. [[2605.08083-autotts|AutoTTS]] shows every TTS algorithm (SC@64, ASC, ESC, ST-BoN, Parallel-Probe) is a hand-designed path through this space; controllers can be discovered automatically over it.
- [Xavier Initialization](concepts/XavierInitialization.md) — Glorot variance $\sigma^2 = 2/(n_\text{in}+n_\text{out})$; the [[WeightInitialization|initialization]] for symmetric activations ([[Tanh]] / [[Sigmoid]]); ReLU variant is [[HeInitialization|He]] ([[d2l-multilayer-perceptrons]]).
- [Word2Vec](concepts/Word2Vec.md) — shallow neural model for word embeddings.
- [WordPiece](concepts/wordpiece.md) — 
- [Workload Function](concepts/WorkloadFunction.md) — user-defined callable for distributed runtimes.
- [Work Stealing](concepts/WorkStealing.md) — A peer-to-peer [[DynamicTaskAssignment|dynamic-task-assignment]] strategy where idle threads raid the work queues of busy peers; the [[Cilk|Cilk language]]'s approach. [[NormMatloff]] cautions in [[parproc-ch02-recurring-performance-issues]] §2.4.4 that *"accessing the other work queue is going to be expensive in terms of time and memory contention overhead."*
- [Writing Granularity (TSW / SSW / MSW)](concepts/writinggranularity.md) — Three δ-mem state-update strategies: per-token, per-message-segment, multiple parallel sub-states.
- [Zero-Shot Learning](concepts/ZeroShotLearning.md) — task performance without labeled examples.
- [Zipf's Law](concepts/ZipfsLaw.md) — Empirical power-law observation that word-rank-$i$ frequency $n_i \propto i^{-\alpha}$; bigrams and trigrams also follow Zipf's law with smaller exponents. The structural reason count-based $n$-gram LMs break down ([[d2l-recurrent-neural-networks]]).
- [δ-mem](concepts/deltamem.md) — Online-state memory mechanism augmenting a frozen Transformer; from [[2605.12357-delta-mem]].

### From *Python for Data Analysis 3E* (May 2026 ingest)
- [Broadcasting](concepts/Broadcasting.md) — NumPy's shape-alignment rule for element-wise ops on differently-shaped arrays; trailing-dimension matching; broadcast axes are read-only views, not copies.
- [Bitonic Mergesort](concepts/BitonicMergesort.md) — Parallel sorting network based on bitonic sequences; pairwise [[CompareExchange]] operations split a bitonic sequence into two bitonic halves; O(log² n) parallel steps ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.2.5).
- [Bubble Sort](concepts/BubbleSort.md) — O(n²) serial comparison sort; inner-loop [[CompareExchange]] structure parallelizes directly in shared memory; basis for [[OddEvenTransposition]] ([[parproc-ch12-parallel-sorting]] §12.3.1).
- [Bucket Sort](concepts/BucketSort.md) — Range-partition sorting algorithm; substrate for the parallel [[SamplingBucketSort]] variant ([[parproc-ch01-intro-parallel-processing]]).
- [Categorical Data](concepts/CategoricalData.md) — pandas extension dtype storing integer codes + categories array; memory-efficient for low-cardinality strings; faster groupby. Analogous to R's `factor`.
- [DataFrame](concepts/DataFrame.md) — 2-D column-oriented labeled table; the central [[pandas]] data structure. Modeled after R's `data.frame`; each column is a [[Series]] sharing a common row [[pandasIndex|Index]].
- [Extension Data Types](concepts/ExtensionDataTypes.md) — pandas extension arrays beyond NumPy: nullable `Int64`/`boolean`/`string` (with `pd.NA`), `category`, tz-aware `datetime64[ns, tz]`. Solves the "missing data forces float64" pain.
- [Global Interpreter Lock (GIL)](concepts/GlobalInterpreterLock.md) — CPython mechanism preventing concurrent execution of Python bytecode; limits CPU-bound multithreading. Escape via multi-process, C-extensions that release the GIL, or [[Numba]] `nogil`.
- [HDF5](concepts/HDF5.md) — Hierarchical Data Format v5; self-describing binary container for typed N-D arrays + groups. `h5py` / PyTables / `pd.HDFStore`. Strong for scientific arrays; [[Parquet]] is the table sibling.
- [Hierarchical Indexing (MultiIndex)](concepts/HierarchicalIndexing.md) — pandas index with multiple levels per axis; lets a 2-D DataFrame represent higher-dimensional data. Backbone of `stack`/`unstack` reshape and `groupby` on index levels.
- [IPython](concepts/IPython.md) — Enhanced interactive Python shell (Fernando Pérez, 2001); tab completion, introspection (`?`/`??`), magic commands (`%run`/`%timeit`/`%debug`/`%pdb`), shell integration. The Python kernel powering [[Jupyter]].
- [Jupyter](concepts/Jupyter.md) — Web-based notebook platform spun out of IPython (2014); language-agnostic kernel architecture (40+ kernels); `.ipynb` JSON file format. Python kernel = IPython.
- [matplotlib](concepts/matplotlib.md) — Foundational Python plotting library (John Hunter, 2002); MATLAB-style API; publication-quality static figures; substrate of [[seaborn]] and pandas's `.plot` accessor.
- [ndarray](concepts/NDArray.md) — NumPy's N-dimensional homogeneous array; data pointer + dtype + shape + strides. Strides enable zero-copy views (slicing, transpose, reverse).
- [Numba](concepts/Numba.md) — LLVM-based JIT compiler for Python; `@numba.njit` / `@numba.vectorize` / `@guvectorize`; reaches C-level speed on numeric Python; can release the [[GlobalInterpreterLock|GIL]].
- [NumPy](concepts/NumPy.md) — Foundational numerical-computing package for Python; ndarray + ufuncs + broadcasting + linear algebra + PRNG + C API. Forged in 2005 by Travis Oliphant from Numeric + Numarray.
