- [MPI_Reduce](concepts/MPIReduce.md) — All-to-one [[CollectiveCommunication|collective]] reduction with a 12-op vocabulary (`MPI_MAX` / `MPI_MIN` / `MPI_SUM` / `MPI_PROD` / `MPI_LAND` / `MPI_LOR` / `MPI_LXOR` / `MPI_BAND` / `MPI_BOR` / `MPI_BXOR` / `MPI_MAXLOC` / `MPI_MINLOC`); the `MAXLOC` / `MINLOC` variants return `(value, location)` pairs via `MPI_2INT`; canonical O(log P) tree implementation ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.3).
- [MPI_Allreduce](concepts/MPIAllreduce.md) — `MPI_Reduce` + `MPI_Bcast` collapsed into one call (drops `root` arg); recursive-halving/doubling schedule on a logical [[Hypercube]] achieves ~2× the latency of separate reduce+bcast; the operation behind [[AllReduce]] / [[RingAllReduce]] / [[NCCL]] / [[Horovod]] / PyTorch DDP gradient sync ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.3).
- [MPI_Gather](concepts/MPIGather.md) — All-to-one [[CollectiveCommunication|collective]] concatenation — each rank contributes a chunk; root receives *"chunk items sent from each node, stringing everything together in node order"*; *"the fifth argument is redundant with the second; same for the third and sixth"* is an acknowledged API wart; `MPI_Gatherv` adds variable-length per-rank chunks ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.4).
- [MPI_Allgather](concepts/MPIAllgather.md) — `MPI_Gather` with no `root` — every rank receives the full concatenated result; recursive-doubling on a logical [[Hypercube]] in `log P` rounds with bandwidth-optimal `(P-1)/P × |total|` per-rank traffic ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.4).
- [MPI_Scatter](concepts/MPIScatter.md) — One-to-all [[CollectiveCommunication|collective]] chunked distribution — *"the opposite of `MPI_Gather()`, i.e. it breaks long data into chunks which it parcels out to individual nodes"*; canonical opener for the manager/worker [[ScatterGather]] pattern; `MPI_Scatterv` for variable-length chunks ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.5).
- [MPI_Barrier](concepts/MPIBarrier.md) — [[CollectiveCommunication|Collective]] synchronization with sole `comm` argument; *"explicit barriers are less common in message-passing programs than in the shared-memory world"* — most MPI sync is implicit at send/recv boundaries and inside collectives; useful for timing, non-MPI side-effect ordering, and debugging ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.6.9).
- [MPI Communicator](concepts/MPICommunicator.md) — Group of processes + communication context; `MPI_COMM_WORLD` is the universal communicator; subgroups via the four-call recipe `MPI_Comm_group` → `MPI_Group_incl` → `MPI_Comm_create` → `MPI_Group_rank`; virtual topologies (`MPI_Cart_create` / `MPI_Graph_create`) carry topology metadata for the implementation to optimize routing ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.3.3.2 / §8.6.10).
- [Buffering, Synchrony, and Safety in MPI](concepts/BufferingMPI.md) — The three-layer abstraction (user MPI program / MPI internals / OS TCP/IP stack); TCP/IP coalesces N `MPI_Send`s into one byte stream that MPI re-parses; **the exact MPI standard send semantic**: *"`MPI_Send(x,...)` will return only when it is safe for the application program to write over the array which it is using to store its message"*; the OS-buffer → app-buffer copy [[Infiniband]] RDMA eliminates; the synchronous tag-mismatch [[Deadlock]] pattern; *"asynchronous communication is considered **unsafe** in MPI terminology"* but most production code accepts the risk for the performance ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.7).
- [Nonblocking Communication (MPI)](concepts/NonblockingComm.md) — *"Living dangerously"* with `MPI_Isend` / `MPI_Irecv` returning immediately + `MPI_Wait` / `MPI_Test` / `MPI_Probe` for completion checks; the *"don't touch the buffer until you've confirmed completion"* safety contract; canonical fix for the synchronous-deadlock pattern + the comm/compute overlap technique that makes [[Infiniband]] / HCA-driven RDMA worthwhile ([[parproc-ch08-introduction-to-mpi]] §8.7.3).
- [MapReduce](concepts/MapReduce.md) — Distributed batch-processing paradigm: map (parallel per-record transform) → shuffle/sort (group by key) → reduce (per-key aggregation); a [[ScatterGather]] variant with sorting; [[Hadoop]] is the canonical implementation ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]]).
- [HDFS](concepts/HDFS.md) — Hadoop Distributed File System; replicates each block on ≥3 disks; stores MapReduce input/output; locality scheduling embodies *"Moving computation is cheaper than moving data"* ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.1.5).
- [Hadoop Streaming](concepts/HadoopStreaming.md) — Language-agnostic stdin/stdout interface to [[Hadoop]]; enables R/Python mappers and reducers via tab-separated `key \t data` text format; combiner reduces shuffle traffic ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.1.1).
- [WordCount](concepts/WordCount.md) — Canonical [[MapReduce]] "Hello World": count word frequencies across a distributed text file; implemented in R via [[HadoopStreaming]] and independently via [[Snowdoop]] ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.1.2 / §9.4.1).
- [Snowdoop](concepts/Snowdoop.md) — [[NormMatloff]]'s lightweight pure-R [[MapReduce]] alternative: chunk files manually, run [[Snow]]'s `clusterCall`, combine with `Reduce` — no Java/configuration; worker data persists in RAM across iterations ([[parproc-ch09-mapreduce-computation]] §9.4).
- [Hillis-Steele Scan](concepts/HillisSteeleScan.md) — Data-parallel [[PrefixScan]] algorithm; $\log_2 n$ rounds, n threads; $O(n \log n)$ total work; requires red/black double-buffer for correctness; load balance degrades each round ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.2).
- [Blelloch Scan](concepts/BlellochScan.md) — Work-efficient two-pass [[PrefixScan]] (up-sweep reduce + down-sweep propagate); $O(n)$ total work, $O(\log n)$ depth; standard GPU scan algorithm ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.3 / literature reference).
- [Run-Length Encoding](concepts/RunLengthEncoding.md) — Lossless compression of consecutive-value runs as (count, value) pairs; decompression maps onto [[PrefixScan|exclusive prefix scan]] of run-counts → start offsets; OpenMP and [[Thrust]] implementations in §10.5–10.6 ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]]).
- [Moving Average](concepts/MovingAverage.md) — Sliding-window mean $a_i = (x_{i-w+1}+\cdots+x_i)/w$; computed in parallel via [[PrefixScan|exclusive cumulative sum]] + element-wise subtract-divide using `thrust::exclusive_scan` + `thrust::transform` ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.7).
- [Lambda Function](concepts/LambdaFunction.md) — C++11 anonymous function `[capture](params){ body }` used inline without a named declaration; replaces [[Functor|functor structs]] in [[Thrust]] / TBB; `[=]` captures outer variables by value, `[&]` by reference ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.7.3).
- [Stream Compaction](concepts/StreamCompaction.md) — Parallel primitive that packs selected elements into a compact output array; implemented via predicate evaluation → [[PrefixScan|exclusive scan]] of indicators → scatter; exposed in [[Thrust]] as `copy_if` / `remove_if` ([[parproc-ch10-parallel-prefix-problem]] §10.6 / [[parproc-ch05-cuda-gpu-programming]] §5.13).
- [Profiling](concepts/Profiling.md) — Empirical measurement of a program's runtime behavior — instructions, time, [[CacheMemory|cache]] misses, heap allocation — to locate [[HotSpot|hot spots]] worth optimizing. The [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 methodological discipline: *"Optimization should never be based on gut feelings"*; serviced by the [[Valgrind]] triad [[Callgrind]] (instructions) + [[Cachegrind]] (cache) + [[Massif]] (heap) ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]] / [[dis-12-3-memory-considerations]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).
- [Benchmarking](concepts/Benchmarking.md) — Controlled empirical measurement of end-to-end program performance (wall-clock, throughput); the **aggregation** counterpart to [[Profiling|profiling]]'s decomposition. Validates every [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 optimization claim — `isPrime` 47% / matrix-vector 8× ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]] / [[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]] / [[dis-12-3-memory-considerations]]).
- [Hot Spot](concepts/HotSpot.md) — A disproportionately resource-consuming code region (function/loop/line) that dominates a program's runtime, cache misses, or memory allocation; the **diagnostic target** of [[Profiling]] and the only profitable optimization target per [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 / Knuth's *"premature optimization"* law ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).
- [Callgrind](concepts/Callgrind.md) — [[Valgrind]] sub-tool that counts **instruction executions per function** and records the dynamic call graph; canonical [[HotSpot|hot-spot]]-finding instrument in [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12.1 — `valgrind --tool=callgrind ./prog` + `callgrind_annotate`; revealed `sqrt` = 20.5% of `isPrime`'s total instructions ([[dis-12-1-first-steps]]).
- [Massif](concepts/Massif.md) — [[Valgrind]] sub-tool that profiles **heap memory usage over time** — peak, per-function breakdown, allocation timeline; `valgrind --tool=massif ./prog` + `ms_print`; the memory-side counterpart to [[Callgrind]] and [[Cachegrind]], completing the [[DiveIntoSystems]] Ch 12 [[Valgrind]] triad ([[dis-12-3-memory-considerations]]).
- [Function Inlining](concepts/FunctionInlining.md) — [[CompilerOptimization|Compiler optimization]] that replaces a function call with the callee body, eliminating call overhead **and** exposing the body to downstream [[ConstantFolding|constant folding]] / [[DeadCodeElimination|dead-code elimination]]; auto-enabled by [[GCC]] at [[GccOptLevels|`-O3`]] via `-finline-functions`; the `static inline` keyword is a programmer hint, not a directive ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).
- [Constant Folding](concepts/ConstantFolding.md) — [[CompilerOptimization|Compiler optimization]] that evaluates constant expressions at compile time (`3*4+7 → 19`); composes with constant propagation, [[DeadCodeElimination|DCE]], and [[FunctionInlining|inlining]] — the downstream chain inlining unlocks; enabled by [[GCC]] at [[GccOptLevels|`-O1`]] and above ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]]).
- [Dead Code Elimination](concepts/DeadCodeElimination.md) — [[CompilerOptimization|Compiler optimization]] (DCE) that removes unreachable code and dead assignments whose results are never used; enabled by [[GCC]] at [[GccOptLevels|`-O1`]]+; composes with [[ConstantFolding]] and [[FunctionInlining]] to prune entire branches once constants prove them unreachable ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]]).
- [GCC Optimization Levels](concepts/GccOptLevels.md) — The `-O0` / `-O1` / `-O2` / `-O3` flag family controlling [[GCC]] aggression; `-O0` no-opt (debug default), `-O1` basic ([[ConstantFolding]] / [[DeadCodeElimination]]), `-O2` standard production, `-O3` adds `-finline-functions` ([[FunctionInlining|inlining]]) + vectorization. Sibling flags `-funroll-loops` ([[LoopUnrolling]]) and `-funroll-all-loops`. Distinct taxonomy from Rust's [[OptLevel]] ([[dis-12-2-compiler-optimizations]] / [[dis-12-4-summary]]).
